variants_low: Three of us. A headman, a lifter. Then me at the bellows. Ask them what they feel.
variants_high: Three of us were hired from three villages. Prices-The-Salvage keeps the count and sleeps by the stacked cakes. He sees no shame in it, since he's paid by the stack. Meets-Every-Tide wades for the iron. I'm on the bellows and I feel the shame more than they do. You listen well. Few visitors stay to hear that.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.bog-iron-workings.n1-2
words: I work the bellows at the clay furnace from first light until the cakes are cool. The furnace is built new at the start of the season. When the iron is ready, we break it open for the bloom. Road gangs buy what comes out for nails and tyres. It's shameful work and I'll say so to anyone who asks.
variants_low: Bellows. The furnace is built new and broken open for the bloom. Road gangs buy the iron.
variants_high: I work the bellows at the clay furnace from first light until the cakes are cool. The furnace is built new at the start of the season, then broken open for the bloom. Road gangs buy the iron for nails and tyres. They pay fair coin for it. I still call it shameful work, but I'll pump for you if you want to see the bloom come out.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.bog-iron-workings.n1-2
words: A digger lifts the iron out of the seep in cakes and stacks them on the bank to dry. I work the bellows instead, so I only hear it from the bench. The mud makes a sucking sound each time a cake comes loose. When that sound comes slow, the lifter is tired.
variants_low: A digger lifts the iron out of the seep in cakes. I don't.
variants_high: A digger lifts the iron out of the seep in cakes and stacks them on the bank to dry. I work the bellows instead, so I only hear it from the bench. The mud makes a sucking sound each time a cake comes loose. Take one if you can lift it. The road gangs pay for every cake, but a stranger's hands are free.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.bog-iron-workings.n1-3
words: Blackwood is the hill country at the western edge of the marsh. The Blackwood Road goes up through it into Cyrodiil. The hill folk keep to the roots of their own tree and ignore strangers. A riddle they like.
variants_low: Hills in the west. The road climbs to Cyrodiil. They ignore strangers.
variants_high: Blackwood is the hill country at the western edge of the marsh. The Blackwood Road goes up through it into Cyrodiil. The hill folk keep to the roots of their own tree and ignore strangers. Bring a riddle and they might listen.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.bog-iron-workings.n1-3
words: The marsh makes bog iron on its own. Seeping water leaves iron crusted in the clay. These workings sit below the road. The crews cut the crust out in cakes. The furnace on the bench smelts the cakes.
variants_low: Iron from the mud. We cut it, we smelt it, the crews buy it.
variants_high: The marsh makes bog iron on its own. Seeping water leaves iron crusted in the clay. These workings sit below the road. The crews cut the crust out in cakes, then the furnace on the bench smelts them. Ask for a cake if you want to feel the weight.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.bog-iron-workings.n1-3
words: Those are Imperial roads and a waystation from the old days. Crews still use the old names, so the roads go by them. Toward the Rose runs the Prison one. The Tag House stands next to it, up on a rise of dry ground.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads. The crews use the old names. Ask them.
variants_high: Those are Imperial roads and a waystation from the old days. Crews still use the old names, so the roads go by them. Toward the Rose runs the Prison one. The Tag House stands next to it, up on a rise of dry ground. Walk it in daylight.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.bog-iron-workings.n1-3
words: Bog iron lies in the mud of the seep, down the bank from here. I lift it out in cakes, one by one. Then I stack them on the bank to dry. The road crews buy the cakes for their nails and tyres.
variants_low: Bog iron, from the seep. I lift it out in cakes and stack them on the bank. Road crews buy them. That is all you need.
variants_high: Bog iron lies in the mud of the seep, down the bank from here. I lift it out in cakes and stack them to dry on the bank. Road crews buy them for nails and tyres. Take a look at the stack if you want to see one.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.bog-iron-workings.n1-3
words: Leeches in the seep. I pull them off at the midday break. Past the near mud is the deep end. The crew will not dig it, but I would, with the near mud worked out. It's a frog down there, that is all.
variants_low: Leeches. Keep out of the seep.
variants_high: Leeches in the seep. Salt on the legs gets them off at the midday break. The deep end is past the near mud. The crew will not dig it, but I would. It's a frog down there, that is all.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.bog-iron-workings.n1-3
words: Back down the path to the seep track, then up to the road. West of here is the Mile House, the one with an eagle in its name. Cartwright's Cross comes after that.
variants_low: Down the path. Then west. You will find it.
variants_high: Back down the path to the seep track, then up to the road. West of here is the Mile House, the one with an eagle in its name. Cartwright's Cross comes after that. Keep to the track edge. The ground is soft.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.bog-iron-workings.n1-3
words: Three of us came for the season. The other two stay dry up at the furnace and the stack. I stand in the mud with the cakes. We do not ask each other our villages.
variants_low: Three of us. They stay dry. I do not.
variants_high: Three of us came for the season. The other two stay dry up at the furnace and the stack. I stand in the mud with the cakes. Still, the walk home is better with company.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.bog-iron-workings.n1-3
words: I lift. From first light I stand in the mud pulling cakes out. The near mud gives less every season. Twenty-six mornings left of it.
variants_low: I lift, from first light. Ask the others what they do.
variants_high: I lift. From first light I stand in the mud pulling cakes out. The near mud gives less every season. Come when the cakes are cool and I will show you how a good one rings.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.bog-iron-workings.n1-3
words: Every season the crew builds the clay furnace new on the bench. When the season ends we break it open to get the bloom out, the lump of iron inside. Twenty-six mornings and it comes down.
variants_low: We build the furnace new each season. We break it open for the bloom. Stand clear of it.
variants_high: Every season the crew builds the clay furnace new on the bench. We break it open at the end to get the bloom out, the lump of iron inside. Twenty-six mornings and it comes down. You can hear the bloom ring when it's struck.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.bog-iron-workings.n1
words: Blackwood is the hill country in the far west of Black Marsh. The road climbs through it into Cyrodiil. The hill folk keep close to their own tree and show strangers little interest. They love a riddle.
variants_low: Hills in the far west of Black Marsh. A road climbs through them to Cyrodiil. The hill folk like riddles.
variants_high: Blackwood is the hill country in the far west of Black Marsh. The road climbs through it into Cyrodiil. The hill folk keep close to their own tree and show strangers little interest. They do love a riddle, so try one on them.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.bog-iron-workings.n1
words: The marsh makes bog iron without help. Water soaks through the clay and leaves a hard crust of iron. The Bog Iron Workings sits below the road. We cut the crust into cakes. Then the cakes go into a clay furnace for smelting.
variants_low: The marsh makes the iron itself. We cut cakes of it from the crust. The workings sit below the road.
variants_high: The marsh makes bog iron without help. Water soaks through the clay and leaves a hard crust of iron. The Bog Iron Workings sits below the road. We cut the crust into cakes. Then the cakes go into a clay furnace for smelting. I will show you the furnace if you ask.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.bog-iron-workings.n1
words: The Border road and the Prison road are Imperial roads. The Mile House is an Imperial waystation. Everyone still uses the old names for them. Beside the Prison road, on a dry rise, you will find the Tag House. The gangs wear nails and tyres off those roads, so they buy my iron.
variants_low: Imperial roads, old ones. People use the old names. The Tag House is on a dry rise by the Prison road.
variants_high: The Border road and the Prison road are Imperial roads. The Mile House is an Imperial waystation. People use the old names still. Beside the Prison road, on a dry rise, you will find the Tag House. I sell iron to the gangs who mend those roads.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.bog-iron-workings.n1
words: The Bog Iron Workings lies below the road. I have charge of the season's diggers. I sleep beside the stacked cakes to tally each one at dawn. Cakes are priced by the stack. Looking at the furnace costs nothing.
variants_low: Below the road. I have charge of the stack. Buy a cake or go back up the path.
variants_high: The Bog Iron Workings lies below the road. Come up to the bench and I will show you the stack. I have charge of the diggers here, so I can name a fair price for a whole stack. If you carry it yourself, I'll knock a little off.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.bog-iron-workings.n1
words: Leeches lie in the seep, so I check my legs after each shift. We stopped working the deep end because something sits in the pools. I still weigh what that iron would fetch. Near the path the mud has given all it had.
variants_low: Leeches in the seep. Something in the deep end. Stay on the path.
variants_high: Keep to the path and look to your legs for leeches after. I do not touch the deep end, since something sits in the pools. The mud near the path has given all it had, so each season's cakes come up smaller and further out.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.bog-iron-workings.n1
words: From the bench a path goes up to the road. Turn west there. You reach Mile House of the Eagle first, then Cartwright's Cross. Take a cake with you if you can lift one. Road gangs pay for them.
variants_low: Up the path to the road. West is Mile House of the Eagle. Cartwright's Cross is past it.
variants_high: Climb the path to the road, then go west. Mile House of the Eagle comes first. Cartwright's Cross lies beyond it. The smith at the Cold Forge buys our scraps, if you pass his way.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.bog-iron-workings.n1
words: Three of us work the season, each from a different village. I have charge. Argues-The-Toll works the bellows. She says what she thinks of the work, loudly. Meets-Every-Tide lifts the cakes. She says little. I pay no mind to the shame of it.
variants_low: Three of us, from three villages. I have charge. That is all you need.
variants_high: Three of us work the season, each from a different village. I have charge. Argues-The-Toll works the bellows. She says plainly what she thinks of the work. Meets-Every-Tide lifts the cakes. Speak to them kindly, since both are low this week.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.bog-iron-workings.n1
words: A digger lifts the bog iron out of the seep in cakes. The cakes dry on the bank. Road gangs pay coin for each one. A good cake is worth more than my cracked bowl. That bowl is worth a copper.
variants_low: We lift iron from the seep in cakes. Road gangs pay for them. Are you buying, or only watching?
variants_high: A digger lifts the iron from the seep in cakes, then they dry on the bank. Road gangs pay coin for each. If you carry them yourself, I'll shave a little off the stack price.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.bog-iron-workings.n1
words: The iron gathers where the water stands stagnant and heavy with iron. A seep like ours has stood still for years. When the season ends, every digger walks off to a separate village. I walk to mine with my pay for the stack.
variants_low: Stagnant water makes it. Every digger walks off to a separate village at season's end.
variants_high: Stagnant water, rich with iron, makes it. Our seep has stood still for years, so the cakes come up good. At season's end, every digger walks off to a separate village. Mine is a long walk. I carry the pay for the stack.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-2
words: Coming down the coast track, you see a straight ridge with a reed roof over it. That's Chasepoint, a road stage the Legion built on the coast road. The wreck-salvage families keep it now. Salvage rights here are hereditary. The old stable dries our rope. Two families each want the keeper's office.
variants_low: Chasepoint is a road stage on the coast road. The Legion built it. The wreck-salvage families keep it. Salvage rights are hereditary. Two families each want the keeper's office.
variants_high: Coming down the coast track, you see the reed roof first. That's Chasepoint, a road stage the Legion built. The wreck-salvage families keep it now. Salvage rights are hereditary, so the shore stretches pass down. The old stable dries our rope. Two families each want the keeper's office.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-2
words: Ojel is our word for outsiders. It's a plain word with no insult in it, so you needn't flinch at it on the quays. Lukiul is the slur. The An-Xileel coined it for Argonians hatched outside Black Marsh, because those Argonians can't hear the Hist. Who uses it against whom is not mine to say.
variants_low: Ojel means outsider. It carries no insult. Lukiul is the slur the An-Xileel coined for Argonians hatched outside Black Marsh, who can't hear the Hist.
variants_high: Ojel is our word for outsiders. It carries no insult, so wear it easily. Lukiul is the slur. The An-Xileel coined it for Argonians hatched outside Black Marsh, who can't hear the Hist. Say that word to a stranger and you'll lose a friend.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-2
words: The Empire left us the Border road, the Prison road and a waystation called the Mile House. Folk still use the old names. Walk east towards Fourth Stage and you come onto the Prison road. On a dry rise beside it, you'll find the Tag House.
variants_low: The Empire left the Border road, the Prison road and the Mile House waystation. Folk use the old names. The Tag House stands on a dry rise beside the Prison road.
variants_high: The Empire left us the Border road, the Prison road and a waystation called the Mile House. Folk still use the old names. Walk east towards Fourth Stage and you come onto the Prison road. The Tag House is on a dry rise beside it. I'll point it out if you're going.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-2
words: In the Third Era, the Empire made Soulrest its capital for all Black Marsh. It stands on the south-west coast, on Topal Bay, a few minutes from the stage. Today it's contested. I haul timber, so that's a quarrel for the people who rule.
variants_low: The Empire's capital for Black Marsh, in the Third Era. South-west coast, on Topal Bay. Contested now.
variants_high: In the Third Era, the Empire made Soulrest its capital for all Black Marsh. It's on the south-west coast, on Topal Bay, a few minutes from here along the track. It's contested now, so keep your purse close when you go.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-2
words: South of us is the Southern Sea, the water beyond the marsh. Of the province's cities, only Lilmoth and Soulrest sit on its water. Oliis Bay is a piece of it. So is Topal Bay. I work its shore south of the stage. It gives me something most low waters.
variants_low: South is the Southern Sea. Lilmoth and Soulrest are the province's only cities on it. Oliis Bay and Topal Bay belong to it.
variants_high: South of us is the Southern Sea, the water beyond the marsh. Only Lilmoth and Soulrest among the province's cities stand on it. Oliis Bay and Topal Bay are parts of it. I'll show you the shore at low water if you want to see it.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-2
words: The Legion built the stage back when they kept the coast road in order. Now the salvage households have it. Our reed went up where the roof tiles were lost. The plaster walls underneath are still sound. I know the place best from the shore side, where I drag the wreck timber up.
variants_low: The Legion built it. We hold it now. Reed on the roof, plaster underneath. I've no time to give you the rest.
variants_high: The Legion built this stage, back when the coast road had a keeper. We've got reed up where the tiles went. I'll show you the sound walls if you're passing the yard. The shore side is my part of it, though. That's where I'm happiest.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-2
words: Fellrunners and marsh rats live in the scrub. I cross it alone to reach the shingle. Out on the shore I watch the tide as well. There's no second pair of eyes out there.
variants_low: Fellrunners and marsh rats in the scrub. Keep off the shore if you can't read the tide.
variants_high: Fellrunners and marsh rats live in the scrub, so keep to the track. I cross it alone to reach the shingle. If you must go down to the shore, ask me the hours to low water first and I'll tell you the safe ones.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-2
words: For Soulrest, go west along the track. It's a few minutes. East on the coast road is Fourth Stage. The Southern Sea is the water south of the marsh, two fields beyond the yard through the scrub. You can't see it from the stage, but I use that way down to the shingle.
variants_low: Soulrest is west along the track. Fourth Stage is east. The Southern Sea lies south of the marsh, two fields off.
variants_high: Soulrest is a few minutes west along the track. Fourth Stage is east on the coast road. The Southern Sea lies south of the marsh, two fields beyond the yard. If you're going to the water, I'll walk the scrub with you as far as the shingle.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-2
words: I went out on the bar and looked. That wreck is Southern Sea wreckage, the same as everything that lands on the shore south of the stage. The wreckers of the Long Bar have taken it over, though, so the families keep off it.
variants_low: That wreck on the bar is Southern Sea wreckage. The wreckers of the Long Bar have taken it over. I've no time for more.
variants_high: That wreck on the bar is Southern Sea wreckage, landsman, the same as all that lands on the shore south of the stage. The wreckers of the Long Bar have taken it over, so the families keep off it.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-2
words: Two families here each say the keeper's office is theirs. It hasn't paid in two hundred years, so I leave them to their papers. Whoever wins it, the stall still opens at the same hour.
variants_low: Two families say the keeper's office is theirs. It hasn't paid in two hundred years. Ask them, not me.
variants_high: Two families here each say the keeper's office is theirs. It hasn't paid in two hundred years, so I stay out of it. The stall opens at the same hour whoever wins. You can come to me for a fair price in the meantime.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-2
words: I walk the shingle at low water and drag the wreck timber above the tideline. The rope goes to dry in the old stable. Before the other families' lots reach the stall, I buy them cheap. They take my low price to save the walk. I count my day in hours to low water.
variants_low: I haul timber up the shingle at low water. The rope dries in the old stable. The stall sells the rest. It's my work. It doesn't need your help.
variants_high: I haul the wreck timber up the shingle when the water's low. The rope hangs in the old stable to dry. The stall sells the week's finds. If you've coin, find me before the stall does. I buy lots from the other families at a price I can resell.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-2
words: Whatever the Southern Sea breaks up lands on the shore south of the stage. Timber, rope, nets, all of it. Our salvage rights are hereditary, so each family has its own stretch. I keep to mine. Lift a plank off another family's shingle and you'll answer for it.
variants_low: The Southern Sea throws wreck up on the shore south of the stage. The rights are hereditary. Keep off my stretch.
variants_high: The Southern Sea breaks ships and the pieces land on the shore south of the stage. Salvage rights are hereditary, so every family keeps its own stretch. If you want timber, I'll sell you some of mine. Lifting it from another family's shingle is another matter.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-3
words: The Legion built this stage on the coast road. Salvage families work it now. The rights pass from parent to child. Rope dries in the old stable. The keeper's office has two families after it.
variants_low: Legion stage. Salvage families, parent to child. Two families want the keeper's office.
variants_high: Soldiers of the Legion raised this stage along the coast road. Salvage is the families' work now, handed down from parent to child. I hang rope in the old stable myself. Two families each want the keeper's office. My own household is one of them.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-3
words: The Mile House is a waystation. The Prison and Border roads are Imperial work, old roads. People still use the old names. East of the stage the Prison road heads for the Rose. On a dry rise by it stands the Tag House.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads, the Mile House too. Old names still used. The Tag House sits on a dry rise.
variants_high: The Mile House is an old waystation. The Prison and Border roads are Imperial work. Most people still say the old names. Walk east from the stage on the Prison road and you pass the Tag House, up on a dry rise.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-3
words: Soulrest is the old capital, a short walk west. These days it is contested. I go in when I must. I am back before the lamps.
variants_low: Soulrest is west. It is contested.
variants_high: Soulrest is the old capital, a short walk west. These days it is contested. Go in by daylight and be back on the track before the lamps.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-3
words: South of the marsh is the Southern Sea. Topal Bay is part of it, and so is Oliis Bay. What it breaks of ships ends on our shingle.
variants_low: The Southern Sea, south. Topal Bay is part of it. So is Oliis Bay.
variants_high: South of the marsh is the Southern Sea. Topal Bay is part of it, and so is Oliis Bay. Ships break on it and we haul the pieces off the shingle.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-3
words: Road or shore? Road, then you saw the front first. It is an Imperial road stage with grey walls. The reed on top is ours. The families call it a bodge.
variants_low: Imperial stage. Grey walls, reed roof. Look all you like.
variants_high: Road or shore? Road, then you saw the front first. It is an Imperial road stage with grey walls. The families put the reed on top. Ask me about the rope if you want to know more.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-3
words: Fellrunners hunt the scrub round the stage. Marsh rats chew rope in the stable. Came by the road? Then stay on it after dark.
variants_low: Fellrunners and marsh rats in the scrub. Stay on the track.
variants_high: Fellrunners hunt the scrub round the stage. Marsh rats go for rope in the stable. Stay on the track after dark and carry a lantern if you must cross.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-3
words: Soulrest is a short walk west on the track. Fourth Stage is further, east along the coast road. The Southern Sea lies south, two fields past the scrub. Most of what I handle comes up from that side.
variants_low: Soulrest west. Fourth Stage east. The Southern Sea lies south.
variants_high: Soulrest is a short walk west on the track. Fourth Stage is further, east along the coast road. The Southern Sea lies south, two fields past the scrub. Stay on the track either way.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-3
words: Two families want the keeper's office. Mine says it is ours by right. I say so in the yard and nowhere louder, because loud talk sends people looking at the sheds.
variants_low: Two families want the keeper's office. That is all I say.
variants_high: Two families want the keeper's office. Mine says it is ours by right. I say it quietly in the yard, since loud talk sends people looking at the sheds. Ask me about the rope instead.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-3
words: Did you come by the road or the shore? The shore people know the bar. The wreckers out there pull people off it. They say the rescue is owed, so they keep them as crew to work it off. I haul rope on this side.
variants_low: The wreckers on the bar keep the people they rescue. The rescue is owed in work.
variants_high: Did you come by the road or the shore? If the shore, keep off the bar, stranger. The wreckers out there pull people off it. They say the rescue is owed, so they keep them as crew to work it off.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-3
words: I haul rope up off the south shingle with the others and hang it to dry in the old stable. My palms show it. The stall sells whatever comes ashore that week.
variants_low: Rope off the south shingle, hung in the old stable. The stall sells it.
variants_high: I haul rope up off the south shingle with the others and hang it to dry in the old stable. My palms show it. The stall sells that week's finds. Come when the tide is low and I will show you a good coil.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-3
words: I haul rope off my family's shore until my palms burn. Each family guards its own stretch of the south shore. Taking timber off another family's stretch is forbidden.
variants_low: Each family guards its stretch of shore. Timber off another's stretch is forbidden.
variants_high: I haul rope off my family's shore until my palms burn. Each family guards its own stretch of the south shore. Taking timber off another family's stretch is forbidden. Ask before you carry anything off the sand.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-4
words: Chasepoint is a stage on the coast road. The Legion built it. The wreck-salvage families work it now. A family's right to the shore passes down to its children. Two families want the keeper's office. The shore rope hangs to dry in the old stable. I mend nets here and say my price once.
variants_low: A coast road stage, salvage families. Ask elsewhere about the rest.
variants_high: Chasepoint is a stage on the coast road, traveller. The Legion built it. The wreck-salvage families work it now. A family's right to the shore passes down to its children. Two families want the keeper's office. The shore rope hangs to dry in the old stable. Sit by the rack awhile.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-4
words: Prison road, Border road, the Mile House: those are old Imperial names. People use them still, though the Empire is gone. The Rose lies where the Prison road heads. Beside that road, on a patch of dry ground, you'll find the Tag House. I mend nets. I've never needed the road.
variants_low: Old Imperial names. Ask a carter.
variants_high: Prison road, Border road, the Mile House, traveller: those are old Imperial names. People use them still, though the Empire is gone. The Prison road heads toward the Rose. The Tag House sits beside it on a patch of dry ground. I've never walked it, but you should.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-4
words: Soulrest is the town west of here. When the Empire ran Black Marsh in the Third Era, it was the capital. Now it's contested. I leave the arguing to others. I go there to sell. I'm back before the lamps are lit.
variants_low: West of here. Once the capital, contested now. I sell there.
variants_high: Soulrest is the town west of here, traveller. When the Empire ran Black Marsh, in the Third Era, it was the capital. Now it's contested. I leave that to others and go to sell. The prices there are fair. I will tell you my own once if you need one.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-4
words: The Legion built this stage in the days when the coast road mattered. The soldiers left. The walls stayed, grey plaster over rubble, still sound. The pantiles went long ago, so the families laid reed across the top. I sit at the net rack in the yard and mend what the shore sends up. I'm fond of the place, bodged roof and all.
variants_low: Chasepoint. The Legion built it. Mind the rope.
variants_high: The Legion built this stage, traveller. I will tell you the lot if you have a moment. Grey plaster, a straight ridge, a reed roof we laid ourselves. I mend nets at the rack in the yard. Come and look if you like. The work is honest and so is the price.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-4
words: Fellrunners and marsh rats live in the scrub round the stage. The fellrunners hunt, so a traveller out there after dusk is asking for trouble. The rats are only a nuisance, though they chew a net through if I leave it down. Stay on the track and be gone before dark. That advice costs you nothing.
variants_low: Fellrunners in the scrub. Stay on the track.
variants_high: Fellrunners and marsh rats live in the scrub, traveller. The fellrunners hunt, so I'd walk the track and be gone by dark. I'll lend you a lantern if you need one. The rats only chew my nets. I rack them high now, so they've given up on me.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-4
words: Soulrest is a short walk west along the track. It's the nearer market if you've coin to spend. East on the coast road is Fourth Stage, further off, with a few turnings. South of here, two fields away, is the sea. The yard wall hides it from you. I'd go to Soulrest first.
variants_low: West is Soulrest. East is Fourth Stage. The sea is south.
variants_high: Soulrest is a short walk west along the track, traveller. Go there first. It is the nearer market. The stalls pay well for a mended net. East along the coast road is Fourth Stage, further off, with a few turnings. The sea is south, two fields away, behind the yard wall.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-4
words: Two families claim the keeper's office. It carries no pay, so I don't care much who wins. What I care about is the tally at the stall. I know what the shore sends up. I also know what reaches the tally from the rope-stable family. The two don't match. A fair count matters more to me than a title on a door.
variants_low: Two families want the office. I want the tally honest. Leave it there.
variants_high: Two families claim the keeper's office, traveller. It carries no pay, so I don't mind who wins. My complaint is the tally. I know what the shore sends up. The rope-stable family's lots do not add up to it. Look at the stall's book yourself, I won't stop you.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-4
words: I mend nets. The families drag wreck up from the shore in the south at low tide. The torn nets come to my rack. When one's done I work out its worth and tell the stall the price once. Ask me again and you'll get the same number. The stall at the north end sells the week's finds. I like watching a straight sale.
variants_low: I mend nets. Ask the stall about the rest.
variants_high: I mend nets, traveller. The families haul wreck up from the south shore and the torn nets come to my rack. I'll mend you one cheap if you've a tear. I price it once, so mind you listen. The stall at the north end sells the week's finds. I like watching a straight sale.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1-4
words: Wreck washes up on the shore south of the stage. Every family guards its own stretch of it. Taking timber off a stretch that isn't yours is forbidden. Mine is mended net and rope, so I stay out of the quarrels over planks. When I name a price for a net it's named once. Buyers who haggle leave empty-handed.
variants_low: Each family guards its shore. No taking timber from another's. Don't try.
variants_high: Wreck washes up on the shore south of the stage, traveller. Each family guards its own stretch. Taking timber from a stretch that isn't yours is forbidden. The families mean it. My work is nets and rope, so I'm no part of those quarrels. Ask me a net's price. You'll hear it once.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1
words: Chasepoint is a stop on the coast road. The Legion built it. Wreck-salvage households keep it now. The right to salvage passes down each family. I hang rope to dry in the stable. Two families claim the keeper's office, though no keeper has seen pay in two hundred years.
variants_low: A coast road stage the Legion built. Salvage households keep it. Two families claim the keeper's office.
variants_high: Chasepoint is a stop on the coast road that the Legion built. Salvage households keep it now. The right to salvage passes down each family. I dry rope in the old stable. Two families claim the keeper's office. Ask the stall for the count, traveller.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1
words: The Prison road is an old Imperial road, east of the stage. It runs toward the Rose. People still use old names for it. The Border road and the waystation called the Mile House keep theirs too. You will find the Tag House on a dry rise beside the Prison road.
variants_low: The Prison road is an old Imperial road toward the Rose. The Tag House is by it.
variants_high: The Prison road is an old Imperial road, east of the stage. It runs toward the Rose. People still use the old names for it. The Border road and the waystation called the Mile House keep theirs too. Walk it. You will find the Tag House on a dry rise beside it.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1
words: In the Third Era, the Empire ruled the marsh out of Soulrest. It was their capital. It sits by Topal Bay on the south-west coast, west of here along the track.
variants_low: Soulrest is the old Imperial capital, on Topal Bay, south-west coast. Walk there and look.
variants_high: Soulrest is a town to the west along the track. In the Third Era, the Empire ruled Black Marsh from it, as its capital. It lies on the south-west coast by Topal Bay. I buy my twine there when I have the coin.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1
words: South of the marsh is the Southern Sea. Of all the cities in the province, Lilmoth and Soulrest alone stand on it. The wrecks start far out over that water. The families only see them after the tide has finished with them.
variants_low: The Southern Sea lies south. Lilmoth and Soulrest are the only two cities on it.
variants_high: The Southern Sea lies south of the marsh. Lilmoth and Soulrest are the only two cities of the province on its shore. Everything the families haul up came across that water first. Ask the stall which ship each piece was.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1
words: The Legion raised this as an Imperial road stage. The pantiles are gone, so the roof is reed now, with the old walls under it. I dry recovered rope in the stable inside the yard wall.
variants_low: An Imperial road stage. The roof is reed. I dry rope in the stable. I have thirty-one coils on the rack.
variants_high: It began as an Imperial road stage, raised by the Legion. The pantiles are gone, so the roof is reed now. I dry recovered rope in the stable here, if you want to see how it hangs.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1
words: Four fellrunners and three marsh rats live in the scrub, by my count. The families say more. I never go in after them. Keep to the track and be gone before dark.
variants_low: Fellrunners and marsh rats in the scrub. Stay on the track.
variants_high: Fellrunners and marsh rats live in the scrub, four of the first and three of the second by my count. I never go in after them. Take the track. Go early, so you are home before dark.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1
words: Soulrest is west along the track, a short walk. East, the coast road runs on to Fourth Stage, The Southern Sea lies south across two fields. The yard wall hides it. I count those fields each time and get two.
variants_low: West for Soulrest. East for Fourth Stage. The sea is south.
variants_high: Soulrest is west along the track, a short walk. East, the coast road runs on to Fourth Stage. The Southern Sea lies south across two fields. Walk them once and count them yourself, traveller.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1
words: The keeper's office belongs with the salvage households, by right. The stage family waves Imperial papers at you instead. Two families claim it. No keeper has been paid in two hundred years, so I ask what the paper is worth.
variants_low: Two families claim the keeper's office. One has papers. I do not care for papers.
variants_high: Two families claim the keeper's office. I will tell you where I stand. It belongs with the salvage households, not with the stage family and its Imperial papers. No keeper has been paid in two hundred years. You may ask them what the papers are worth.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1
words: The Legion built this stage, then stopped paying. In two hundred years, no keeper has been paid. Two families want the office. Mine has the right. The stage family holds the office now.
variants_low: Two hundred years without pay for a keeper here. The office is my family's by right. The stage family says it is theirs.
variants_high: Two hundred years. No keeper at this stage has been paid, traveller. My family has the right to the keeper's office, with the arrears. The stage family holds the office now. Ask Aelia Nerva at the stage door what she was paid.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1
words: I dry the rope that the families bring up from the wrecks. It hangs in the old stable, west of the stage. The stall writes a total for each lot. I dispute it every time. Thirty-one coils this morning. The stall wrote twenty-nine.
variants_low: I dry rope in the old stable. The stall writes the totals wrong. Ask it, not me.
variants_high: I dry the rope that the families bring up from the wrecks. It hangs in the old stable, west of the stage. Come to the rack. I will show you which coils are sound.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n1
words: When a ship breaks up, the sea sends the wreckage to the shore below the stage. The right to gather it passes down the households. My kin work our stretch. The others work theirs. Take timber off a stretch not yours and answer for it.
variants_low: Wreckage comes ashore south of here. The right to it is hereditary. Leave the timber be.
variants_high: Salvage is what a wreck leaves. The Southern Sea sends the wreckage to the shore south of the stage. The right to gather it is hereditary, passed down each household. If you want to learn the stretches, I will walk you along the rack and name them.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n2
words: I sell the families' salvage here. The Legion built this stage on the coast road. Salvage rights pass from parent to child, so each family guards its own. Rope dries in the stable. The keeper's office has two families claiming it.
variants_low: The Legion built this stage on the coast road. Salvage rights pass down the families. Two families claim the keeper's office.
variants_high: I sell the families' salvage here. The Legion built this stage on the coast road. Salvage rights pass from parent to child, so each family guards its own. Rope dries in the stable. The keeper's office has two families claiming it. Buy from the stall, not from the shore.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n2
words: The Prison road is an old Imperial road toward the Rose. People still use its old name. The Mile House and the Border road keep theirs as well. Beside the Prison road, on a dry rise, stands the Tag House.
variants_low: The Prison road is an old Imperial road toward the Rose. People use the old names. The Tag House stands beside it.
variants_high: The Prison road is an old Imperial road toward the Rose. People still use its old name. The Mile House and the Border road keep theirs as well. Beside the Prison road, on a dry rise, stands the Tag House. Dry ground, if you walk it.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n2
words: Soulrest lies a short walk west. It sits on the south-west coast, by Topal Bay. Who holds it is not my business. The stall sells to whoever walks up with coin.
variants_low: Soulrest is west, on Topal Bay, on the south-west coast. Who holds it is not my business.
variants_high: Soulrest lies a short walk west. It sits on the south-west coast, by Topal Bay. Who holds it is not my business, but its streets are worth a look. Come back and tell me what lots you saw there.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n2
words: South of the marsh there is open water, the Southern Sea. From this yard it is two fields off, hidden by scrub. The wrecks I sell come ashore from it.
variants_low: The Southern Sea is south of the marsh. Wrecks come ashore from it.
variants_high: South of the marsh there is open water, the Southern Sea. From this yard it is two fields off, hidden by scrub. Every wreck I sell came ashore from it, so I would not walk the shingle after dark.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n2
words: This is an Imperial road stage. I keep the salvage stall at the north end of it, so I see everyone who comes up the track. The families run the place now, under their own reed roof.
variants_low: An Imperial road stage. The stall is at the north end if you came to buy.
variants_high: This is an Imperial road stage. I keep the salvage stall at the north end, so I see the whole track from my counter. Come by on a Sixthday and I will show you the new lots, with the reed roof overhead.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n2
words: Fellrunners and marsh rats live in the scrub round the stage. I stand behind the stall in the yard all day, so I only hear of them. The shore walkers meet them more often than I do.
variants_low: Fellrunners and marsh rats are in the scrub. I stay in the yard.
variants_high: Fellrunners and marsh rats live in the scrub round the stage. I am in the yard all day, so I only hear of them. If you walk out, ask the shore walkers first, because they meet the beasts more than I do.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n2
words: Soulrest is a short walk west along the track. East, the coast road goes on to Fourth Stage. The sea is two fields south, with scrub in the way. Most of what I sell comes up on that shore.
variants_low: West is Soulrest, a short walk. East is Fourth Stage. South is the sea.
variants_high: Soulrest is a short walk west along the track. East, the coast road goes on to Fourth Stage. The sea is two fields south, with scrub in the way. Take the track to Soulrest first, since it is quickest. Come back for the lots after.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n2
words: Two families claim the keeper's office here. It has paid nothing for two centuries, so I leave them to it. I sell to both households and to any traveller. The stall needs every buyer it can get.
variants_low: Two families claim the keeper's office. I sell to both. Ask them yourself.
variants_high: Two families claim the keeper's office here, with no pay in two centuries to show for it. I sell to both households and to any traveller. Bring your coin and I will sell to you at the same price.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n2
words: The wreckers on the bar pull people out of the water. They keep those people on as crew until the rescue is worked off. I do not know the sum. Opens-The-Second-Shed does. He hauls rope with the households at the drying shed.
variants_low: Wreckers on the bar keep the people they pull out as crew. The rescue is owed in work. The sum is for Opens-The-Second-Shed to say.
variants_high: The wreckers on the bar pull people out of the water. They keep those people on as crew until the cost of the rescue is worked off. I do not know the sum. Opens-The-Second-Shed does.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n2
words: I sell the week's salvage at the stall. This week's lot is Southern Sea wreckage off a ship. The owners have not heard it sank. They should be told. Aelia Nerva keeps the stage office. Ask her who.
variants_low: The owners of this week's ship have not heard it sank. Ask Aelia Nerva at the stage door.
variants_high: This week's lot is Southern Sea wreckage off a ship. The owners have not heard it sank. Aelia Nerva keeps the stage office.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n2
words: I sell the week's salvage over the stall at the north end of the stage. Each lot comes up from the south shore. I read its ship's name off the bow-board before it goes on the counter.
variants_low: I sell the week's salvage at the stall. Lots come from the south shore.
variants_high: I sell the week's salvage over the stall at the north end of the stage. Each lot comes up from the south shore. I read its ship's name off the bow-board first, so you know what you are buying.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.n2
words: I sell the past week's salvage at this stall. Each lot is counted first, then I read its ship's name off the bow-board and sell it under that name. I do not sell a lot that has no ship's name.
variants_low: I sell the week's salvage. Each lot is counted, then sold under its ship's name off the bow-board. No ship's name, no sale.
variants_high: I sell the past week's salvage at this stall. Each lot is counted first. Then I read its ship's name off the bow-board and sell it under that name. I do not sell a lot with no ship's name, so you can trust what you take home.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.station-keeper
words: You're standing in it. This is a stage on the coast road. The Legion put it up, then left it. Wreck-salvage families keep it now. Salvage rights pass from parent to child here. Each family guards its own stretch of shore. Two families want the keeper's office. That argument is older than I am. The rope they bring up dries in the old stable.
variants_low: A coast road stage. The Legion built it. Salvage families keep it now.
variants_high: You're in Chasepoint, a coast road stage the Legion built. The salvage families keep it today. Their rights pass down from parent to child. Ask at the stall for rope or timber. Two families want the keeper's office, but that needn't trouble you.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.station-keeper
words: The Border road and the Prison road are the Empire's old work. There's an old waystation too, the Mile House. We still use all three old names here, as my family always has. The Prison road heads for the Rose. Over on a dry rise beside it you'll find the Tag House.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads, the Border road and the Prison road. The Mile House is a waystation. The Tag House is on a dry rise by the Prison road, toward the Rose.
variants_high: The Border road and the Prison road are Imperial work, with the Mile House as a waystation. People still use the old names. The Prison road heads for the Rose. The Tag House sits on a dry rise there. Go by daylight and you'll find it.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.station-keeper
words: Soulrest was the Empire's capital in Black Marsh once. It's a short walk west of here. Today it's contested. I couldn't tell you by whom, because the stage doesn't see that side of it. I'd go in with nothing I couldn't lose. Be out again before the lamps go down.
variants_low: Soulrest is the old capital, west of here. It's contested. Mind yourself.
variants_high: Soulrest was the Empire's capital in Black Marsh. It's a short walk west, but contested today. Go in with little to lose. If you're robbed, come and tell me. I'll enter it in the ledger.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.station-keeper
words: The Legion built this stage for the coast road. The grey plaster walls are theirs, still sound after all this time. I hold the keeper's office here. The roof tiles went long ago, so the families put reed up in their place. They call that thatch a bodge. They're right, but it keeps the wet off my ledger.
variants_low: The Legion built this stage. I hold the keeper's office here. Reed on the roof is the families' doing.
variants_high: The Legion built this stage for the coast road, you'll see their plaster all round the yard. I hold the keeper's office. The reed roof is a bodge by the families' own word, but sit under it a while. It's drier than you'd think.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.station-keeper
words: Four fellrunners and a few marsh rats live in the scrub round the stage. I've watched the fellrunners from the door. I'd rather not watch them closer. The wet does more harm to the stage than any teeth do, since the coast plaster never dries. If you walk out, get back to the track before the lamps are lit.
variants_low: Fellrunners and marsh rats in the scrub. Stay clear of both.
variants_high: Four fellrunners and a few marsh rats keep to the scrub round the stage. Take a lantern if you walk out there. Be on the track again before the lamps are lit. I've seen the fellrunners from the door. I'd not meet them closer.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.station-keeper
words: Soulrest is a short walk west along the track. East, the coast road runs on to Fourth Stage, another of the Legion's. The sea lies south, two fields off. The scrub and the yard wall hide it from the door. The road and its stages are my inheritance, so I like a traveller to leave here pointed the right way.
variants_low: Soulrest is west along the track. Fourth Stage is east on the coast road. The sea is south.
variants_high: Soulrest is a short walk west along the track. Fourth Stage is east on the coast road, another of the Legion's stages. The sea lies two fields south, hidden by the scrub. I'll walk you to the track if you like.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.station-keeper
words: A wreck has come in on the bar. The families won't work it. Wreckage from the Southern Sea lands on the shore south of the stage often enough, but this one is different. Buys-Cheap has been out to look at it. You'll find him by the drying shed. Ask him what is aboard.
variants_low: A wreck has come in on the bar. The families won't work it. Buys-Cheap went to look. Ask him.
variants_high: A wreck has come in on the bar. Wreckage from the Southern Sea lands south of the stage often enough, but the families won't work this one. Buys-Cheap has been out to look at it. He's by the drying shed.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.station-keeper
words: There are two families here. Each makes its claim to the keeper's office. Mine holds the paper for it. The other has none. It's still loud about the matter at the stall. The standing orders say a keeper answers every traveller at the door. They don't say what to do about neighbours.
variants_low: Two families make their claim to the office. Mine has the paper. That's all you need.
variants_high: Two families lay claim to the keeper's office. Mine has the paper. I'll show it to you if you doubt me. The other is loud at the stall about it. I'd rather you heard my side first.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.station-keeper
words: Chasepoint is the last solid footing before the road swings inland. Past here it needs a causeway. A survey went east out of Soulrest to cost the mending, but no word has come back. Go to The Tag House on the Prison road. Look for the survey's trail there.
variants_low: A survey went east out of Soulrest to cost a causeway and sent no word back. Try The Tag House on the Prison road. This is the last solid ground before the road swings inland.
variants_high: This is the last solid ground before the road swings inland. Past it the road is poor. A survey went east out of Soulrest to cost a causeway and sent no word back. Find The Tag House on the Prison road. Look for the survey's trail there.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.station-keeper
words: Wreckage comes ashore to the south of the stage. That part is no secret. I don't carry talk about lots traced to sunk ships. It isn't the office's business. A ship's owners can think her still afloat when she is on our shingle, though. You'd find them in Soulrest, west along the coast road.
variants_low: I don't repeat that talk. Wreckage comes ashore south of the stage. Owners who think their ship is afloat will be in Soulrest, west along the coast road.
variants_high: I don't repeat that talk, traveller, but I'll give you the part that helps. Wreckage comes ashore south of the stage. Some owners think their ship is afloat when she is on our shingle. Ask in Soulrest, west along the coast road, if you want to tell them.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.station-keeper
words: I hold the keeper's office here. The Legion built this stage, then the pay stopped. No keeper has drawn a wage in two hundred years. Two families say the office is theirs, with the arrears. Argues-With-The-Clerk speaks for the other one, if you want his side.
variants_low: No keeper here has drawn pay in two hundred years. Two families want the office. Argues-With-The-Clerk speaks for the other one.
variants_high: No keeper at this stage has drawn a wage in two hundred years. I hold the office all the same. Two families say it is theirs, with the arrears. Argues-With-The-Clerk speaks for the other one. Hear him out, traveller, then come back and I'll read you the old orders.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.station-keeper
words: The families walk the shingle to the south at low tide and drag the wreck timber up above the tideline. The rope comes back here to dry in the old stable. I haul nothing myself. I watch the track from the stage door. That's the work of the office. On a slow day, the weather is the busiest entry.
variants_low: The families haul wreck timber from the shore. The rope dries in the old stable. The stall sells the finds.
variants_high: The families haul wreck timber up from the south shore. I note every load that comes in past my door. The rope dries in the old stable. The stall at the north end sells the week's finds. Ask there for a price.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.chasepoint.station-keeper
words: This is an Imperial road stage. The keeper's office came to me by inheritance, wageless. Nothing has been paid to a keeper since the road fell out of repair. Each of two families lays claim to the office. I hold the paper. The standing orders say a keeper keeps the door, the lamp and the ledger. Money isn't mentioned.
variants_low: An Imperial stage. The office is inherited. It has paid no keeper for ages. Two families claim it.
variants_high: This is an Imperial stage. The keeper's office is inherited. It pays nothing. No keeper has seen a wage since the road fell out of repair. Two families lay claim to it. Mine has the paper. I'm glad of company in the argument.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.landing-s-poler
words: Blackwood is hill country, far over in the west. The road climbs up through it to Cyrodiil. I've never been up there. The hill people stay near the roots of their own tree, the carters tell me. They pay little mind to strangers. A riddle they do like.
variants_low: Hill country in the west. The road climbs through it to Cyrodiil. They keep to their own tree. They like riddles.
variants_high: Blackwood is hill country in the far west. The road climbs up through it to Cyrodiil. The hill people keep to the roots of their own tree. They pay strangers little mind. Carters say a riddle will keep them talking all evening.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.landing-s-poler
words: Claywater is one ford with two halves. The station half has timber and stone, with the well and the house. Ours is mud and thatch, over the ford from them. We replastered it last year before the rains. A traveller pays at the well for the station half. Then the traveller pays at my hut for the landing half.
variants_low: A ford with two halves. Timber and stone on the station bank. Mud and thatch here. Each bank charges its share.
variants_high: Claywater is a ford with two halves. The station bank is timber and stone. Ours is mud and thatch, replastered last year before the rains. Each bank charges a traveller separately for the stop. Keep two purses ready. I'll take the smaller coins at the hut.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.landing-s-poler
words: Gideon is the city on the western frontier. Coming down the Blackwood Road out of Cyrodiil, it's the first settlement you reach. I've not been. Carters say its courts still sit. An Owing is a debt worked off in labour. If one was written there, the paper can be contested before a judge. Most of Gideon's people are Argonian.
variants_low: A frontier city in the west, first on the road from Cyrodiil. Its courts still sit. Most are Argonian.
variants_high: Gideon is the city on the western frontier, the first settlement on the Blackwood Road from Cyrodiil. Carters say its courts still sit. An Owing is a debt worked off in labour. One written there is a paper contract you can contest before a judge. Most of Gideon's people are Argonian, like me.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.landing-s-poler
words: Helstrom is the interior's capital for us Argonians. The city has grown into a grove of great trees with minds of their own. After the Battle of Argonia, our armies pulled back there. The Empire decided against besieging it. No army has taken the city. I know it only from carters.
variants_low: The Argonian capital, a city grown into a grove of great trees. The armies pulled back there after the Battle of Argonia. The Empire decided against besieging it. No army has taken it.
variants_high: Helstrom is the interior's capital for us Argonians. The city has grown into a grove of great trees with minds of their own. After the Battle of Argonia, our armies pulled back there. The Empire decided against besieging it. No army has taken the city. Carters who cross on my raft talk of little else.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.landing-s-poler
words: The Onkobra is a river. Its source lies near Topal Bay. It flows east beyond Gideon, toward the heart of the province. Carters say the road along it is muddy and badly kept. Near Gideon the current is white and fast. The red clay of the Onkobra sells widely in the marsh. I'd price a cartload by the wheel.
variants_low: A river flowing east from Topal Bay past Gideon. Muddy road along it. Red clay.
variants_high: The Onkobra starts near Topal Bay and flows east beyond Gideon, toward the heart of the province. The road along it is muddy and ill kept. Near Gideon the current is white and fast. Red clay from it sells all over the marsh. A cartload crosses my raft for a fair price.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.landing-s-poler
words: The Prison road and the Border road are old Imperial roads. The Mile House is an old Imperial waystation. People here still use the old names for all three. The Prison road heads for the Rose. Next to it, on a dry rise, stands the Tag House. I've only heard of it from carters.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads and a waystation, the Mile House. The old names stay. The Tag House is on a dry rise by the Prison road.
variants_high: The Prison road and the Border road are old Imperial roads. The Mile House is an old Imperial waystation. People still use the old names. The Prison road heads for the Rose, with the Tag House on a dry rise next to it. Carters tell it better than I do.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.landing-s-poler
words: This is the landing. The mud huts sit low beside the channel. I pole the raft from here. The well and the station house are over the ford, with their own charge on that bank. Carters tell me Helstrom, the capital of the heartland, has a rootworm station for the great worms that carry people through the roots.
variants_low: The landing's this bank. The station's across the ford. Carters talk of a rootworm station at Helstrom. I haven't seen it.
variants_high: This is the landing, with the mud huts low by the channel. I pole the raft here. Ask me the price before you unload anything. The well and station house are across the ford. Carters say Helstrom has a rootworm station, a stop for the great worms under the roots. I'd like to see it one day.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.landing-s-poler
words: Bog dogs come down to the banks at dawn and again at dusk. Between those hours the banks are quiet enough. A crocodile lives in the channel. I keep my feet on the planks and my pole short when I take a cart over. I keep my work to the light.
variants_low: Bog dogs on the banks at dawn and dusk. A crocodile in the channel. Don't wade.
variants_high: Bog dogs come down to the banks at dawn and dusk, so cross in the middle of the day. A crocodile lives in the channel. Keep off the edge of the planks when I pole. I'll bring you over dry.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.landing-s-poler
words: I give ways by the water, since the channel is what I know. The road is the station's business. Past the ford, Cartwright's Cross is a short walk off. Further along the road is the Eagle's Mile House. Carters say Gideon is at the far end. I've not poled anyone that far.
variants_low: I know the channel. Road stages are the station's affair. Cartwright's Cross, then the Eagle's Mile House.
variants_high: I give ways by the water, as the channel is my work. Past the ford, Cartwright's Cross is a short walk. The Eagle's Mile House lies beyond it. Carters say Gideon is at the far end of the road. Ask the well-keeper about the road. Take her a coin.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.landing-s-poler
words: Imperial families live over by the well. Argonian families live here in the huts. Livia Varinius keeps the well, so quarrels on her bank go to her. Ours come to me. The station folk count everything twice. They drink from a cracked well, yet they call my fee dear. Some travellers wade over to dodge a charge.
variants_low: Imperials by the well. Argonians in the huts. Livia Varinius has the well. I have the landing.
variants_high: Imperial families live by the well. Argonian families live here in the huts. Livia Varinius keeps the well and settles quarrels on her bank. Ours come to me. The station folk count everything twice, yet they're fair when you deal with them straight. A traveller who wades over to dodge a charge sours me.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.landing-s-poler
words: The well, the beds and the stable are over the water. I keep the plank raft on this bank. A handcart costs less than a wagon. A sack of salt has no wheels at all, so I call it half a wheel. The station takes its charge for its half of the stop. I take mine for the crossing.
variants_low: Station has the well and beds. I have the raft. Each bank charges for its own half of the stop.
variants_high: The well, the beds and the stable are over the water. I keep the plank raft here. A handcart costs less than a wagon. I'll tell you the price before the pole goes in the water. Each bank charges for its own half of the stop. Pay the station at its door, then me at the hut.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.landing-s-poler
words: The station charges on that bank. I charge here, for the crossing. The landing is older than the station. Polers worked this ford before the well was dug. Now the well head is cracking. We won't help mend it in stone. Neither side could keep the other's half going.
variants_low: Station charges on its bank. I charge on mine. The landing is older than the well. We won't mend it in stone.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.landing-s-poler
words: The ford is shallow, so a walker can wade it. A cart can't. The carts come to my plank raft instead. I charge by the wheel. A wagon pays more than a handcart. The oldest rule of this landing is that a cart pays me. A cart that goes over unpaid has broken it.
variants_low: Walkers wade the ford. Carts can't. They take my plank raft. I charge by the wheel. Unpaid, a cart breaks the landing's oldest rule.
variants_high: A walker can wade this ford. A cart can't. The carts come to my plank raft instead. I charge by the wheel. A wagon pays more than a handcart. I'll name the price first. The oldest rule of the landing is that a cart pays the poler. Go over unpaid and you've broken it.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1-2
words: Blackwood is the hill country in the west. The road past our ford climbs through it into Cyrodiil. I have never been up there. The carters say the hill folk keep close to their own tree and ask little about strangers. They like a riddle.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1-2
words: This is Claywater. It is one stop on both banks of the ford. Timber and stone on the station side. Mud and thatch on mine. You pay each side separately.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1-2
words: Gideon is the frontier city in the west. Coming from Cyrodiil, it is the first town you reach on the Blackwood Road. The courts there still sit. An Owing is a debt worked off in labour. In Gideon, it is a paper contract you can contest. Most of the people are Argonian.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1-2
words: The Onkobra is a river. It rises near Topal Bay, then runs east by Gideon into the heart of the province. The road along its bank is mud, badly kept. Red Onkobra clay is known across the marsh.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1-2
words: The Prison road and the Border road are old Imperial roads. The Mile House was their waystation. People still use the old names. Heading for the Rose, you take the Prison road. You will see the Tag House standing on a dry rise by it.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1-2
words: I dry fish on the landing racks, then sell it to the station counter. The road crosses the ford here, with the well house on one bank and our huts on the other. The carters tell me Helstrom has a rootworm station.
variants_low: Claywater Station. A ford, a well, a raft. Buy something or leave.
variants_high: I dry fish on the landing racks, then sell it to the station counter. The road crosses the ford here, with the well house on one bank and our huts on the other. Carters tell me Helstrom has a rootworm station. Bring a buyer's coin and I'll show you the racks.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1-2
words: Bog dogs hunt both banks at first light and again at dusk, so I hang my catch at midday. The crocodile stays in the channel. Keep off the stones when the light is low, stranger.
variants_low: Bog dogs at dawn and dusk. A crocodile in the channel. Mind yourself.
variants_high: Bog dogs hunt both banks at first light and again at dusk, so I hang my catch at midday. The crocodile stays in the channel. Keep off the stones when the light is low, stranger. I'll walk you to the track if it is late.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1-2
words: Take the track east to the Blackwood Road. Cartwright's Cross lies a few minutes along the road, on a north-west track. Fifteen minutes east on the road, you reach the Mile House. Gideon is farther than either.
variants_low: East by the track to the Blackwood Road. Cartwright's Cross, the Mile House, then Gideon.
variants_high: Take the track east to the Blackwood Road. Cartwright's Cross lies a few minutes along the road, on a north-west track. Fifteen minutes east on the road, you reach the Mile House. Gideon is farther than either. Leave before the dogs come down.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1-2
words: Imperial families live by the well. Argonian households live over here on the landing. If two neighbours fall out, the Imperials go to the well-keeper, we go to the poler. I buy nothing from the well, but I'll sell fish to anyone.
variants_low: Imperials by the well. Argonians here. Quarrels go to the well-keeper or the poler.
variants_high: Imperial families live by the well. Argonian households live over here on the landing. If two neighbours fall out, the Imperials go to the well-keeper, we go to the poler. Come by the racks at midday and I'll give you the names.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1-2
words: I dry fish on the landing racks. The station counter buys it. My ledger says nine strings went to the counter. A traveller pays the station for the well and the bed, then the landing for the raft. Each bank charges for its own share.
variants_low: I dry fish. The counter buys it. Ask the poler about the raft.
variants_high: I dry fish on the landing racks. The station counter buys it. My ledger says nine strings went to the counter. A traveller pays the station for the well and the bed, then the landing for the raft. Each bank charges for its own share. I'll take less from a regular.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1-2
words: Two banks, one ford. The station half has the well and the beds. The landing half has the raft and my racks. A traveller pays at both, because each bank charges for its own share. The station well is cracking. Its water is sour anyway.
variants_low: Two banks, one ford. Each bank charges you. The station well is cracking.
variants_high: Two banks, one ford. The station half has the well and the beds. The landing half has the raft and my racks. A traveller pays at both, because each bank charges for its own share. The station well is cracking. Its water is sour anyway. Brine takes ford water on my racks.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1-3
words: Blackwood is hills, out at the western end of Black Marsh. The road to Cyrodiil climbs through them. I haven't walked it. The carters who come down say the water is cold up there.
variants_low: Hills in the west. That's all I know.
variants_high: Blackwood is hills, out at the western end of Black Marsh. The carters who come down say the water is cold there. I'd like to taste it. Tell me if you have.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1-3
words: The village is two halves at one ford. The Imperial station is on one bank. The Argonian landing is on the other. Both banks charge you for the same stop. You pay at the well, then you pay again at the landing. I tell travellers so at my bucket, before they get to the counter.
variants_low: Two halves, one ford. Both banks charge you.
variants_high: The village is two halves at one ford. The Imperial station is on one bank. The landing is on the other. Both banks charge you for their share. Pay the poler first. The water at my bucket costs you nothing.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1-3
words: Gideon is the first town on the Blackwood Road, coming in from Cyrodiil. The courts there still sit, which is more than I can say for the Imperial well. I've never been there. Carters tell me about it when they stop at my door.
variants_low: The first town on the Blackwood Road from Cyrodiil. Courts still sit.
variants_high: Gideon is the first town on the Blackwood Road from Cyrodiil. The courts there still sit. I haven't been myself. The carters have told me about it. I'll tell you what I heard if you sit awhile.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1-3
words: When the Empire pulled out, some garrisons stayed in the marsh. Their children after them are Legion as well. The old road stages are their work. The well-keeper is one of them. I take my quarrels to the poler. She gets none from me.
variants_low: Garrisons stayed when the Empire left. Their children are Legion too. They made the stages.
variants_high: When the Empire withdrew, some garrisons stayed in the marsh. Their children after them are Legion as well. The old road stages are their work. I keep clear of the well. The poler will hear you out.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1-3
words: The Onkobra is a river. It runs east past Gideon and on into the interior. I haven't drunk from it, so I can't tell you how it tastes. I'd want a cup of it before I said a good word of it.
variants_low: A river that runs east past Gideon. I don't know it.
variants_high: The Onkobra is a river that runs east past Gideon into the interior. I haven't tasted it yet. A carter may bring me a bottle one day. I'd give him a cup of mine in trade.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1-3
words: People still call the old Imperial roads by their old names, long after the Empire left. The Prison road is one. The Mile House is a waystation on another. I use those names as the carters do. I have no love for the Empire, but the names help a stranger.
variants_low: The old Imperial roads keep their old names. I don't walk them.
variants_high: People still call the old Imperial roads by their old names. I hear them from the carters. It's an Imperial habit. The names are useful all the same, so I use them. Ask at my door and I'll point you.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1-3
words: Claywater is where I live. My hut stands on the landing bank, on the driest ground this side of the ford. The water here tastes of clay and stone. I like that. The well across the ford tastes tinny to me. Now its head is cracking.
variants_low: It's a ford with two banks. I live on this one.
variants_high: Claywater is my home, traveller. My hut is on the driest ground this side of the ford. The water here tastes of clay and stone. I'll tell you so over a cup of it. The well across the ford tastes tinny to me. Its head is cracking too.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1-3
words: Bog dogs hunt along both banks around first light and again near dark. A crocodile lives in the channel. I stand well back from its edge when I fill my bucket. I do my carrying in the hours between the dogs. The dogs are bad enough, but I like the crocodile less.
variants_low: Dogs on the banks at dawn and dusk. A crocodile in the channel. Keep back.
variants_high: Bog dogs hunt the banks at first light and near dark. A crocodile lives in the channel. Stand back from the edge. Drink from my bucket instead.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1-3
words: I don't walk past the ford, so I can't tell you the road from my feet. Carters say the track east meets the Blackwood Road. Cartwright's Cross comes first. After it, comes the Mile House. Gideon is last. What I can show you is the water. The stones of the ford start at my door.
variants_low: I don't go past the ford. Carters say east to the Blackwood Road.
variants_high: I don't walk past the ford, but I hear the carters. East on the track to the Blackwood Road. Then comes Cartwright's Cross, then the Mile House, then Gideon. Take water from my bucket before you start.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1-3
words: Imperial families live over by the well. Argonian households live here at the landing. When two Imperial families fall out, they take it to Livia Varinius at the station house. We take ours to the poler. I take mine to him whatever the quarrel is.
variants_low: Imperials by the well, Argonians here. Quarrels go to the poler on this bank.
variants_high: Imperial families live by the well and Argonian households live here at the landing. Livia Varinius hears the Imperials' quarrels. The poler hears ours. He hears me out even when I'm in the wrong. His name is Signs-For-The-Cargo.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1-3
words: I keep a bucket of ford water by my door and fill it again after every crossing. The poler takes carts over on a plank raft. Carts pay him by the wheel. I argue his fee with him every week, and then I pay it in full.
variants_low: I carry water. The poler runs the raft for carts. Ask him about the fee.
variants_high: I keep a bucket of ford water by my door and fill it after every crossing. You're welcome to a cup. The poler takes carts over on a plank raft. He charges by the wheel. I argue his fee with him weekly, then I pay all of it.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1-3
words: Across the ford, they build with timber and stone. That's the well, the beds and the counter at the door. We on the landing build in mud and thatch. We replaster before the rains.
variants_low: Timber and stone across the water. Mud here.
variants_high: Across the ford, they build with timber and stone, for the well and the beds. Our half is mud and thatch. We replastered last year. Come and see the walls, traveller. They're dry inside.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1
words: Blackwood's the hill country in the west of the marsh. The road climbs through it into Cyrodiil. The hill people stay close to their own tree and ask nothing of strangers. They like a riddle, I'm told.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1
words: It's the stop at this ford, in two halves. My bank is timber and stone, the far bank mud and thatch. You pay each bank for its own half. Ask the well-keeper before you draw.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1
words: It's the city on the western frontier. Come down out of Cyrodiil by the Blackwood Road and Gideon's the first settlement you reach.
variants_low: The frontier city in the west. First on the Blackwood Road from Cyrodiil.
variants_high: It's the city on the western frontier. Come down out of Cyrodiil by the Blackwood Road and Gideon's the first settlement you reach. The carters eat well there, I'm told.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1
words: The Onkobra rises by Topal Bay and flows east beyond Gideon, deep into the province. Its road is muddy and poorly kept. The marsh is known for red Onkobra clay.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1
words: The Empire built the Prison road and the Border road, with the Mile House as a waystation. People use those Imperial names still. A Tag House sits on a dry rise beside the Prison road.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads with a waystation. A Tag House sits on a dry rise by the Prison road.
variants_high: The Empire built the Prison road and the Border road, with the Mile House as a waystation. People use those Imperial names still. A Tag House sits on a dry rise beside the Prison road. Pack bread for it.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1
words: Two banks at a ford. The well and the station house are on my side, the landing across the water. A rootworm station stands at Helstrom, far off.
variants_low: A well, a house, a ford. A rootworm station stands at Helstrom, far off. Not here.
variants_high: Two banks at a ford. The well and beds are on mine, the landing across the water. A rootworm station stands at Helstrom, far off. Ours has a good pot.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1
words: Bog dogs run the banks at dawn and dusk, four of them. A crocodile lies in the channel. I'm indoors with the pot on by dusk.
variants_low: Four bog dogs on the banks, dawn and dusk. A crocodile in the channel.
variants_high: Four bog dogs run the banks at dawn and dusk. A crocodile lies in the channel. Be off the banks by dusk, citizen. Supper waits at the fire.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1
words: East along the track to the Blackwood Road. Cartwright's Cross lies a few minutes from the turning, then the Mile House some fifteen minutes farther. Gideon lies beyond.
variants_low: East along the track to the Blackwood Road. Cartwright's Cross, then the Mile House. Gideon after.
