variants_high: East along the track to the Blackwood Road. Cartwright's Cross lies a few minutes from the turning, then the Mile House some fifteen minutes farther. Gideon lies beyond. Eat before you go.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1
words: Imperial families by the well, Argonian families in the huts over the water. The landing folk are good neighbours until the well comes up.
variants_low: Imperials by the well, Argonians in the huts. Good neighbours, till the well comes up.
variants_high: Imperial families by the well, Argonian families in the huts over the water. The landing folk are good neighbours until the well comes up. Their pots are theirs, ours are ours, but I'll share bread.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1
words: I cook for my household. That's my work. The poler over the ford takes carts across on a plank raft, because a cart can't wade those stones.
variants_low: I cook. The poler takes carts over on a plank raft. A cart can't wade the stones.
variants_high: I cook for my household, so the pot's open to a hungry traveller. The poler over the ford takes carts across on a plank raft, because a cart can't wade those stones.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n1
words: Two halves, one ford. Ours is timber and stone. The landing's is mud and thatch, replastered last year.
variants_low: Two halves. Timber and stone here, mud and thatch there.
variants_high: Two halves, one ford. Ours is timber and stone. The landing's is mud and thatch, replastered last year. I like their walls, I'll say that.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n2-2
words: West of here, the hill country is called Blackwood. The road I mean to take goes up through those hills into Cyrodiil. The hill folk stay close to the roots of their own tree and ask strangers few questions. A riddle will still get a word out of them.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n2-2
words: Two halves share this ford. The station bank is timber and stone. The landing bank is mud and thatch. A traveller pays the station for its half of the stop and the landing for the other. I pay twice for one night.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n2-2
words: Gideon is the frontier city out west. Its courts still sit. That matters to a man like me. An Owing is a debt you work off with your hands. One made in Gideon is a paper contract, so a court will hear you contest it. I want a paper with my name on it.
variants_low: Gideon is a frontier city with working courts.
variants_high: Gideon is the frontier city out west, with courts that still sit. I will tell you what I know of the paper there. Tell me what you know of the road.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n2-2
words: The Onkobra starts near Topal Bay. From there it flows east, passing Gideon, then on into the province's heart. The track along its bank is muddy and in poor repair. Red clay from its banks sells well in the marsh. I'd walk that track only in the dry.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n2-2
words: This road ends at Gideon. That is the road I follow. The Prison road and the Border road were laid by the Empire. The Mile House was an Imperial waystation. I have not walked any of the three.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads. Not mine.
variants_high: The Prison road and the Border road are old Imperial work, while the Mile House was a waystation. I have not walked them, but I am glad to say so.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n2-2
words: The Sul-Xan are Naga who take souls. They put on jade death masks and sacrifice ojel and Argonians both. Every tribe fears them. Traders here mention a mask found at a border post. I want to be in Gideon behind a court door before I hear more.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n2-2
words: I'm only a traveller here. I pay for a bed at the station house. The well and the counter are on this bank. The landing across the ford is older than all of it, since the polers worked this crossing before the Imperials dug a stone. You came by the Gideon road? Then you have walked further than I have.
variants_low: Ask the well-keeper. I only pay for a bed.
variants_high: Sit by me at the well. I will tell you what I have learnt of this ford. You can tell me of the road.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n2-2
words: Bog dogs run the banks at dawn and again at dusk, so I stay inside at both hours. A crocodile lies in the channel. Wait for full light before you set off, because the road to Gideon is long enough without a bite in it.
variants_low: Dogs at dawn and dusk. A crocodile in the channel. Stay indoors.
variants_high: Bog dogs and a crocodile are the whole of it. I walk the ford at midday. You should do the same.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n2-2
words: Take the track east from the ford, a few minutes, to the Blackwood Road. You have walked it before? Cartwright's Cross is a short walk off it to the north-west. Some fifteen minutes east along the road, a track turns toward Mile House of the Eagle. Gideon is some twenty-five minutes along the road, then a few turnings.
variants_low: East from the ford to the Blackwood Road. Gideon is at its far end.
variants_high: East from the ford, a few minutes, to the Blackwood Road. Cartwright's Cross is off it, then Mile House of the Eagle. Gideon is some twenty-five minutes along the road, then a few turnings. I will draw it in the dust if you wish.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n2-2
words: Imperial families live by the well. The Argonians live in the huts across the ford. When two neighbours fall out, the Imperials go to the well-keeper and the Argonians go to the poler. I'm a customer to both banks. You learn quickly which of them wants paying first.
variants_low: Two banks, two sets of neighbours. Pay both.
variants_high: Imperial or Argonian, they will serve you if you pay first. I can tell you who to pay first.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n2-2
words: I don't work here, I just pay. I sleep at the station house, then walk down to the landing in the morning. The poler poles carts across the ford on a raft of planks, since a cart can't wade the stones. I'm saving my coin for the courts at Gideon.
variants_low: Work is for those who stay. I pay and I leave.
variants_high: You will want a seat on the raft. Pay the poler before the planks are loaded.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n2-2
words: It's the Blackwood Road, an Imperial road. Carts use it between Leyawiin and Gideon. You pass Cartwright's Cross on the way, then Mile House of the Eagle. The road closes in the monsoon season, so I mean to reach Gideon before the rains.
variants_low: It's the Blackwood Road. It closes in the monsoon season.
variants_high: It's the Blackwood Road, which carts use between Leyawiin and Gideon. The monsoon shuts it, so start before the rains.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n2
words: It goes up. Blackwood is the hill country in the west. The Blackwood Road climbs up through those hills to Cyrodiil. A pack feels every step of a climb.
variants_low: The Blackwood Road climbs through the hills to Cyrodiil. Go and see.
variants_high: West and up, friend. The Blackwood Road climbs through the Blackwood hills to Cyrodiil. Take a good cloak for the climb.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n2
words: One ford, two banks, two halves of a village. The half with the well and the station house is timber frame and masonry. The well is cracking in its stone. This one has heard the Argonians will not help mend it. The brazier is the best part.
variants_low: The station half is timber frame and masonry. The well is cracking.
variants_high: Claywater is a ford with two halves, friend. Mine, the station half, is timber frame and stone. Sit by the brazier and watch the well.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n2
words: Walkers on this road talk of Gideon all day. The courts there still work. An Owing is a debt worked off in labour. When one is made in Gideon it is written on paper, so the bound one can take it to the court and contest it. This one has the pack to carry and no Owing to carry with it.
variants_low: Gideon has courts and they still work. An Owing made there is a paper that a court can contest.
variants_high: Gideon's courts still work, friend. An Owing is a debt worked off in labour. If one is made in Gideon it is a paper contract, so the bound one can contest it in court.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n2
words: Black Marsh had its coasts and border lands held by the Empire. It never held the deep marsh. What it built was roads, road stages and prisons. Then it withdrew from the province. This one sits at one of its stages today, by a brazier at a well it dug.
variants_low: The Empire held coasts and borders, not the deep marsh. It built roads, stages and prisons. Then it withdrew.
variants_high: The Empire held the borders and coasts of Black Marsh, friend, but not the deep marsh. It built roads, road stages and prisons. Then it withdrew. The stages still serve a traveller.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n2
words: The Onkobra flows past Gideon, heading east into the heart of the province. The road that follows its bank is muddy. A pack sits better on a dry back than a wet one, so this one waits for dry days.
variants_low: The Onkobra runs east. The road beside it is muddy.
variants_high: Mind the mud on the Onkobra road, friend. The river runs east from Gideon. The road beside it is muddy. Wait for a dry day.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n2
words: The Prison road is the one with the Tag House beside it, up on a dry rise above the mud. This one would pick that rise over the road itself on any wet night. Where the road ends, Abhuki cannot say. She knows only what stands beside it.
variants_low: The Tag House stands by the Prison road, on a dry rise. That is all this one knows of it.
variants_high: Look for the Tag House, friend. It stands beside the Prison road on a dry rise. A good place to be out of the mud.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n2
words: Where does this one sit, you ask? By the brazier at the well, with her pack close against her leg. A station is a stop on the road, not a home. The station house is on this bank. Across the ford, the landing huts sit low by the channel. Those Argonians poled the crossing long before anyone dug the well.
variants_low: A stop on the road. The well is on this bank, the landing across the ford. Ask the well-keeper for the rest.
variants_high: Sit down by the brazier, friend. This one will show you the place with her hand. The station house is here on the near bank. The landing huts across the ford are older than the well.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n2
words: Bog dogs, you ask? They prowl both banks at dawn and again at dusk, so this one keeps to her brazier at those hours. A crocodile lives in the channel and keeps to it. It is no trouble if you stay out of the water. The dogs are different. A hungry dog will go round a camp half the night, sniffing at every bundle on the ground.
variants_low: Bog dogs on the banks at dawn and at dusk. A crocodile in the channel. Keep away from both.
variants_high: Stay by the brazier at dawn and dusk, friend. Bog dogs prowl the banks then. The crocodile keeps to the channel, so keep out of the water. A dog finds a pack by its smell, this one has heard.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n2
words: The road east is easy to find. Take the track to the Blackwood Road, then follow the road east. Cartwright's Cross is a few minutes off it. Next comes Mile House of the Eagle, after some fifteen minutes along the road. Gideon is about twenty-five minutes on from the turning. This one would reach the Mile House before dark.
variants_low: East by the track, then the Blackwood Road. Cartwright's Cross, the Mile House, Gideon, in that order.
variants_high: It's easy, friend. East on the track to the Blackwood Road, then keep going. Cartwright's Cross comes first, Mile House of the Eagle after it, Gideon last. Rest at the Mile House if the light goes.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n2
words: The station bank is where the Imperial families live. The Argonian families are across the ford on the landing bank. Imperials bring a quarrel to the well-keeper. Argonians bring theirs to the poler. This one finds Argonians fair in trade. They weigh honestly. They remember every coin you owe them.
variants_low: Imperials on this bank, Argonians on that one. Imperials bring a quarrel to the well-keeper. Argonians bring theirs to the poler. This one keeps out of both.
variants_high: Imperial families are on the station bank. Argonian families are on the landing bank. The well-keeper hears the Imperial quarrels. The poler hears the Argonian ones. Trade with the Argonians, friend. They weigh honestly.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n2
words: A plain arrangement pleases this one. On the station bank, you find water, a counter, beds upstairs and a stable. The landing across the water keeps the crossing. A traveller pays twice for one stop. The station bank charges for its half. The landing charges for the other half. Neighbours on both banks dislike travellers who wade over to dodge a charge.
variants_low: Water, beds and a stable on this bank. The crossing on that one. The station charges for the beds. The landing charges for the crossing. It's coin twice. This one pays it.
variants_high: The station bank has water, beds and a stable. The landing has the crossing. Each side charges you for its part, so carry coin for both, friend. Wading over to dodge one charge only annoys the neighbours.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.n2
words: The Blackwood Road is what this is. The Empire built it. Carts still roll on it between Leyawiin and Gideon. On the way, a traveller passes Cartwright's Cross and Mile House of the Eagle. In the monsoon season, the road closes. This one would not like to be caught on the wrong side of that with a pack to keep dry.
variants_low: The Blackwood Road, an Imperial road. Carts run it between Leyawiin and Gideon. Cartwright's Cross and Mile House of the Eagle lie along it. It closes in the monsoon season.
variants_high: The Blackwood Road is Imperial work. Carts run along it between Leyawiin and Gideon. You pass Cartwright's Cross and Mile House of the Eagle. Plan around the monsoon season, friend, because the road closes then.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.well-keeper
words: Blackwood is the hill country in the west. The road climbs through it toward Cyrodiil. The hill people like a riddle, so I would carry one up there. They show strangers little interest otherwise.
variants_low: Hill country in the west. They like riddles up there. I have none to give you.
variants_high: Blackwood is the hill country in the west, where the road climbs toward Cyrodiil. The hill people like a riddle. Carry one up there. A good one will get you a hearing.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.well-keeper
words: Claywater is the ford with a stop on each bank. My bank has timber and masonry. Across the water, the huts are mud walls and thatch. They replastered them last year before the rains.
variants_low: A ford with a stop each side. Timber and stone here. Mud and thatch over the water.
variants_high: Claywater is the ford with a stop on each bank. My bank is timber and stone. The huts across the water are mud and thatch, plastered fresh last year. The landing folk keep them tidy.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.well-keeper
words: Gideon is the city on the western frontier. More travellers ask me the road to it than to anywhere else, so I know it by heart. Three turnings follow the Blackwood Road.
variants_low: Gideon is the frontier city. Take the Blackwood Road east. That's all I know of it.
variants_high: Gideon is the city on the frontier in the west. I send travellers there often. East along the Blackwood Road, twenty-five minutes, then a few turnings. I'll draw you water for the road.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.well-keeper
words: Cyrodiil's Empire kept hold of the coasts and the borderlands, but never the deep marsh. The Empire withdrew from the province. Roads came from it, with the stages along them and the prisons. This station was one of its stages.
variants_low: It had the coasts and borderlands, never the deep marsh. Roads, stages, prisons: it built those. It withdrew.
variants_high: Cyrodiil's Empire kept the coasts and the borderlands but never the deep marsh. It built roads, stages and prisons. The Empire withdrew from the province. This station was one of its stages. I keep its well.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.well-keeper
words: Some Legion garrisons stayed on in the province after the Empire pulled out. Their heirs are Legion too, myself among them. Legion hands laid out the old road stages. The post sends me no pay.
variants_low: Garrisons stayed on after the pull-out. Heirs are Legion too. Legion hands laid out these stages. There's no pay in it.
variants_high: The garrisons stayed on after the Empire pulled out. Their heirs are Legion too. I am one of the heirs. Legion hands laid out these stages. No pay comes with the post. I keep faith with the well, not with Cyrodiil.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.well-keeper
words: The Onkobra is the river with the clay pits. Red clay from it is known across the marsh. The pits lie east then north off the Blackwood Road, a good walk from my well.
variants_low: The river with the clay pits. Red clay, known across the marsh. East of here.
variants_high: The Onkobra is the river with the clay pits. Red clay from it is known across the marsh. The pits lie east then north off the Blackwood Road. Go in daylight and take water from my well.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.well-keeper
words: Which road do you want? People round here still call the Imperial roads by the old names, so I do the same. Give me the old name and I can point you. Give me another and I will have to think.
variants_low: Which road? Folk use the old names, so I do. Say one and I'll point.
variants_high: Which road do you want? Folk here call the Imperial roads by their old names. I keep to them too. Say the one you want. I will tell you the first turning.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.well-keeper
words: The poler says the landing won't help mend the well in stone. I'll take the matter up with him myself.
variants_low: The landing won't help mend the well in stone. I'll take it up with the poler myself.
variants_high: The landing won't help mend the well in stone. That's the poler's answer. I'll take it up with him myself.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.well-keeper
words: I keep the well at Claywater Station and the beds in the house behind it. Dawn, travellers asleep upstairs, rope dry. Noon, a cart waiting at the ford. The huts across the water are older than my well.
variants_low: Well and beds. That is all I keep. The counter at the door will sell you either.
variants_high: I keep the well and the beds here. Dawn is quiet. Noon brings the carts. Stay a night and your first bucket is on me.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.well-keeper
words: Bog dogs come down to the water at first light and last light, so I draw at midday. A crocodile lies in the channel. The ford stones look easy. I would not wade them. Be indoors when the lamps are lit.
variants_low: Bog dogs at first and last light. A crocodile in the channel. Keep out of the water.
variants_high: Bog dogs come down to the water at first light and last light. A crocodile lies in the channel, so keep off the ford stones. If you sleep here, I'll light the lantern post for you.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.well-keeper
words: Take the track east to the Blackwood Road, a few minutes. Cartwright's Cross is the first stop, a short walk. The Mile House is next, some fifteen minutes east. Gideon is last, some twenty-five minutes, then a few turnings.
variants_low: East along the track to the Blackwood Road. Cartwright's Cross, then the Mile House, then Gideon.
variants_high: East along the track to the Blackwood Road, then Cartwright's Cross, the Mile House and Gideon in that order. Fill your skins first. I'll draw them myself.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.well-keeper
words: Imperial families live on this bank, the Argonian families in the huts across the ford. Quarrels from our side come to me. The poler hears the ones from his. The landing folk are good neighbours until the well comes up in talk.
variants_low: Imperials this side, Argonians across the ford. I hear the quarrels from my side. The poler hears his.
variants_high: Imperial families live this side, Argonian families across the ford. I hear our quarrels. Signs-For-The-Cargo, the poler, hears theirs. The landing folk are good neighbours.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.well-keeper
words: I draw the water. You ask me before any bucket goes down. The house behind the well has beds upstairs and a counter at the door for provisions. Four stalls in the stable take your horse.
variants_low: I draw the water. Ask before any bucket goes down. Beds and provisions are at the house.
variants_high: I draw the water, so ask me before any bucket goes down. Beds are upstairs and the counter at the door sells provisions. I'll see a stall is swept for your horse.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.well-keeper
words: Both the well and the landing charge you for stopping here. I take the station's share on this bank. The poler takes the landing's share across the ford. Ask him what the landing charges you.
variants_low: Two charges, one stop. Ask the poler across the ford what the landing charges.
variants_high: You'll pay twice for the one stop, here and at the landing. Ask the poler across the ford what he wants. I'd sooner you knew before you wade over.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.claywater-station.well-keeper
words: The head of the well is Imperial stone. A windlass draws the water at set hours. I work it myself. The stone is cracking, so I look it over each morning. A traveller asks me before any bucket goes down.
variants_low: Imperial stone, a windlass at set hours, cracking at the head. A traveller asks me first.
variants_high: The well is Imperial stone with a windlass that draws at set hours. It is cracking, which worries me. I work the windlass myself. A traveller asks me before drawing, so ask and I'll draw yours fresh.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
words: Travellers on the way to Helstrom stop at Greenspring for water and a bed. Water from the spring costs nothing. Few places in this region have water that's safe to drink unboiled. Salt has begun to reach the spring. The village points at the salt works upstream. I point there too after one cup.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
words: Argonians of the interior have their capital at Helstrom. The city grew up into a grove of Hist trees, so the houses stand among the trunks. A grove is a stand of those great trees close together. I rent a mat to nearly everyone bound there.
variants_low: Helstrom is the interior's capital. It grew into a grove of Hist trees. That's all I know.
variants_high: Argonians of the interior have their capital at Helstrom. The city grew up into a grove of Hist trees, with houses between the trunks. I rent a mat to nearly everyone bound there. Tell them Haj-Tei sent you and they'll give you the road news.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
words: A Hist is a great tree with a mind of its own. The clutch of eggs sits beside its roots until the hatchlings come out. It's older than any of us. The village stands round ours. I treat it as kin.
variants_low: A Hist is a great tree with a mind of its own. The eggs sit in a clutch by its roots.
variants_high: A Hist is a great tree with a mind of its own. The clutch of eggs sits beside its roots until the hatchlings come out. It's older than any of us. Come to the shrine and see ours before you leave.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
words: The Border road and the Prison road date from the Empire. So does the waystation called the Mile House. The old names stuck. The old ones say the Imperial roads rotted the cargo. The Prison road heads toward the Rose. On a dry rise by that road, you will find the Tag House.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
words: Dunmer hold Tear as a town on their border. It sits on the coastal plain north of the saltrice country. From Thorn, the Tear road leads there. For centuries the slave trade out of Tear was House Dres's business. My people have no kind word for that.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
words: Thorn is the border city at the north end of the saltrice fields. From Thorn the Tear road runs into Morrowind. House Dres raided the place for slaves once and took profit from the rice. The Thorn Ash-Reed Accord now argues over title to the fields.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
words: The Hist here has a minder, Vees-Wai. He looks after the tree and talks for it. He reads its signs and what it wants. He feels it if trouble touches the eggs or the tribe. The Many-Root Conclave sends the minders to their villages and watches over the trees.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
words: I'm the bed-keeper. Beds and rope are my trade, sold from a chest inside the lodge, across the common from the Hist shrine. Travellers come in off the track or up from the landing and drink at the spring first. Then they find me. My hours are the late ones, while the lamp burns and the last lodgers hunt for a dry mat.
variants_low: Bed-keeper. I sell beds and rope from the lodge chest. Drink at the spring first, then come to me.
variants_high: Come in out of the dark. I'm the bed-keeper. The lodge chest holds my rope and my mats. Drink at the spring before anything else. Then find me. I'll point you to the driest mat there is.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
words: Salt is in the spring now. I drink a cup before I lie down for the day. It bites more than it did. The tree over the pool droops. I see it from the lodge step. Giant wasps nest by the huts as well, so I tell travellers to walk the path and stay off the grass.
variants_low: Salt is in the spring. Giant wasps nest by the huts. Walk the path.
variants_high: Salt is in the spring now, a little more every week. I won't pretend otherwise to a friend. Giant wasps nest by the huts as well. Walk the path and carry a full jar for the road.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
words: Helstrom lies south-west of the spring, past Ux-Aneet. Fill a jar before you go. Both the road and the landing are a few steps from the spring.
variants_low: South-west, past Ux-Aneet, is Helstrom. The road and the landing both start near the spring.
variants_high: Helstrom lies south-west of the spring, past Ux-Aneet. Fill a jar first, since the water costs nothing. The road and the landing both start a few steps from the spring, so choose whichever you trust.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
words: The spring families mend rope for me to sell. Tsono-Ra works behind the lodge and tests each length by pulling it, so I trust his rope before I trust my own eye. Vees-Wai tends the tree. Im-Moro pours at the stone lip. From the lodge step, I watch them all at their work.
variants_low: The spring families mend rope for me to sell. I deal with them. The rest of the village I leave to itself.
variants_high: The spring families mend rope for me to sell. Tsono-Ra's lengths are the best I stock. Vees-Wai tends the tree. Im-Moro pours at the stone lip. Walk over to the shrine and see them. They like a visitor.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
words: The village gives water to every traveller who climbs the path. The cup costs nothing. The rest I sell from the chest in the lodge, a mat for the night and rope by the arm-span. Those two feed the whole village, my own pot included.
variants_low: Water costs nothing here. Beds and rope cost what the village set. Take it or leave it.
variants_high: Water from the spring costs nothing, so drink all you like. The beds and the rope pay for the village's meals, mine too. Ask me about the rope lengths if you need a long one for the marsh.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
words: The talk at the lodge is the salt. It has reached the spring. The families blame the salt works upstream for it. I'd guess the works wash their brine into the river and the river carries it down to us. I can't say how far upstream they stand.
variants_low: Salt has reached the spring. The families blame the salt works upstream. I won't swear to it.
variants_high: The talk at the lodge is the salt. It has reached the spring. The families blame the salt works upstream for it. I'd guess the brine washes down the river. If you pass the works, tell me what you see.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
words: Travellers bound for Helstrom sleep at the lodge. It's the village inn and I run it. The village agreed one price for a night, so I can't give one traveller a better price than the next. I take a fist of salt for a mat. Rope goes by the arm-span from the same chest. Spring water is free, so the beds and the rope pay for everything else.
variants_low: This is the inn. One price a night, agreed by the village, so don't ask me to bend it. Rope is sold here. Water is free.
variants_high: Travellers bound for Helstrom sleep here. You're welcome. The whole village agreed one price a night, a fist of salt, so every guest pays alike. Rope is sold here by the arm-span. The water is free. I'll tell you where the dry mats lie.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
words: Travellers heading for Helstrom stop here to drink and to sleep. Water from the spring costs nothing. Most water in this country must be boiled first, but this you can drink raw. Salt is reaching it now. We blame the salt works up the river.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
words: Helstrom is the capital of our interior, a city that grew into a Hist grove. The Empire decided against a siege. The native armies had pulled back inside once the Battle of Argonia was over. No army has taken the city.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
words: The Hist is a tree with its own mind. Our eggs lie in a clutch by its roots. At the naming, each hatchling drinks the sap. The sap shapes body and scales for life. It is our blood and soul. After death, our spirit returns to the tree. The minder reads the signs and tells us how the clutch fares.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
words: Ojel is our word for outsiders. It carries no insult, so say it freely. Those hatched outside Black Marsh cannot hear the Hist, the great tree that speaks to us. The An-Xileel made a slur for them. I will not say it.
variants_low: Ojel means outsider. It is not an insult. Those hatched outside Black Marsh cannot hear the Hist.
variants_high: Ojel is our word for outsiders. It carries no insult, so say it freely. Those hatched outside Black Marsh cannot hear the Hist, the tree that speaks to us. There is a slur for them. I will not say it. You will hear it from other mouths. Leave it there.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
words: The Empire laid those roads and put up the Mile House as a waystation. The old ones say the roads rotted the cargo. We still use the Imperial names. The Prison road runs on toward the Rose. Beside it the Tag House stands on a dry rise.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
words: Tear is a town of the Dunmer up on the border, on the coastal plain beyond the saltrice fields. You reach it by the road from Thorn. For centuries the slave trade of House Dres worked out of Tear.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
words: Thorn is the city on the northern border of the saltrice fields. From there the Tear road leads into Morrowind. House Dres raided Thorn for slaves once and grew rich on its rice. Now the Thorn Ash-Reed Accord quarrels over title to the fields.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
words: A tree-minder looks after the Hist in a village and speaks for the tree. He reads its signs. He feels it if the eggs are in trouble, or the tribe. Minders are sent out to the villages by the Many-Root Conclave.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
words: I mend rope behind the lodge, out of the sun, where the coils dry flat. The village sits round a spring with our Hist standing over it. The ground is firm here and the water is cold, so I am glad of the place.
variants_low: Rope, behind the lodge. The spring is round the corner with the Hist over it. Go and drink.
variants_high: I mend rope behind the lodge, out of the sun. Come and watch a coil dry if you like. The spring lies past the lodge with our Hist standing over it. Drink there first.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
words: Salt is in the spring now, a little more each week. I taste it in the cup at dusk. Wasps nest too close to our fire stand as well, so I carry my coils wide of the thatch.
variants_low: Salt is in the spring. Wasps nest by our fire stand. Mind the thatch.
variants_high: Salt is in the spring, more each week. Taste a cup at dusk and you will know. The wasps nest too close to our fire stand, so walk wide of the thatch, traveller.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
words: Helstrom is south-west of the spring. Walk through the village of Ux-Aneet. The road continues beyond it. The river landing is below the huts if you want the boats.
variants_low: Helstrom is south-west of the spring, past the village of Ux-Aneet.
variants_high: Helstrom is south-west of the spring, past the village of Ux-Aneet. The road is a short walk from here. Drink before you leave. The water costs you nothing.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
words: My family mends rope for the bed-keeper to sell. Travellers talk to me only when they dispute the price. Then I tell them what the length will bear. They usually pay it.
variants_low: My family mends rope for the bed-keeper to sell. The price is his to name.
variants_high: My family mends rope for the bed-keeper to sell. I am out behind the lodge from first light. Come by if the price troubles you. I will say what the length will bear.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
words: The cup from the spring is free to any traveller. Beds and rope cost plenty. I mend the rope. Every length gets a hard pull before it goes to the lodge, because one that stretches is worth less than one that holds.
variants_low: The cup from the spring is free. Beds and rope are not.
variants_high: The cup from the spring is free to any traveller. Beds and rope cost plenty. I mend the rope. If you buy a length, ask for one of mine, because I pulled it hard and it held.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
words: At the lodge, they argue over who will take the next load down to Helstrom. The other talk is salt reaching our spring. I hear both from behind the lodge while I pull on my coils.
variants_low: They argue at the lodge over who hauls the next load to Helstrom. Salt in our spring is the other talk.
variants_high: At the lodge, they argue over who hauls the next load to Helstrom. The other talk is salt in our spring. I hear it all behind the lodge, so come and ask me what they said.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
words: We cook at the fire stands before the huts. The lodge jars are filled from the spring each morning. My part is the rope. Mee-Sei does better with a pot than I do.
variants_low: We cook at the fire stands and fill the lodge jars. I do the rope.
variants_high: We cook at the fire stands before the huts. The lodge jars are filled from the spring each morning. My part is rope. Mee-Sei at the fire stand will feed you.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
words: Greenspring is where travellers heading for Helstrom stop for a drink and a mat. I fill the jars at the spring. A cup is free to anyone. The water is fine unboiled, which is rare in this part of the marsh. Lately salt creeps in from the works upstream. The village blames them.
variants_low: A spring village on the Helstrom road. Free water, no boiling. Salt's coming in from upstream.
variants_high: Greenspring is where travellers bound for Helstrom stop. You may drink free, traveller, with no boiling needed, which is rare in the marsh. Salt is creeping in from the works upstream, so take your fill now. The village blames them.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
words: Helstrom is the interior's capital, the great Argonian city. It grew into a Hist grove, so the trees and the houses are one place. When the native armies drew back from the Battle of Argonia, that is where they went. The Empire decided against a siege. To this day no army has taken it. Travellers bound for it drink at my spring first.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
words: The Hist is a great tree that thinks for itself. It is older than any people. Our eggs are laid in a clutch beside its roots. At the naming, every hatchling drinks the sap. It shapes the body and the scales for life. Our blood and our soul are that sap. After death, the spirit goes home to the Hist. Vees-Wai reads its signs and tells us how the clutch fares.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
words: Those are old Imperial roads: the Prison road and the Border road. The old ones say the Empire is a story about roads that rotted the cargo. The Mile House is an old waystation. We still use the old names. The Prison road heads toward the Rose. Up on a dry rise by that road is the Tag House.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
words: Tear is a Dunmer town on the border, lying north of the saltrice country, out on the coastal plain. You reach it from Thorn by the Tear road. For centuries, House Dres carried on its slave trade out of Tear.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
words: Thorn is the border city in the north of the saltrice fields. A road, the Tear road, leads out of Thorn into Morrowind. House Dres raided it for slaves in the old days. It profited from the rice too. These days the Thorn Ash-Reed Accord is arguing about who holds the fields.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
words: Vees-Wai is our tree-minder. He looks after the village Hist and speaks for it. He reads the Hist's will and its signs. He feels it if the eggs or the whole tribe come to harm. The Many-Root Conclave is who sends minders to the villages. It keeps the trees.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
words: I fill the lodge jars from the spring, so I know this village by its water first. Greenspring sits where the Panther Race forks. Over the pool grows the Hist of our tribe. Seven jars are done and three to go, so it's early yet. Sit and look at the tree a while. It doesn't mind company.
variants_low: Greenspring. The village by the spring. I've jars to fill.
variants_high: Greenspring is the village where the Panther Race forks. You've come at a good hour, traveller. The tree over the pool is our Hist. Sit by it. I'll bring you a cup when this jar is full.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
words: Salt has got into our spring. The village blames the works upstream. I taste it first, since the first cup of the morning is mine. It's thin, at the back of the tongue. The wasps nest so near the fire stand that Mee-Sei keeps the pot covered all day.
variants_low: Salt in the spring, from the works upstream. Wasps by the huts. Mind both.
variants_high: The salt comes from the works upstream. The village says so loudly. I taste it before anyone, every morning. The wasps are the worse trouble for you. They nest by the fire stand, so walk wide of it, traveller.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
words: Helstrom lies south-west of the spring. You go through Ux-Aneet on the way. The road and the landing both begin below the huts, a short walk from my jars. Drink a cup before you leave. The water is sweet, whatever the salt does to it later.
variants_low: South-west, through Ux-Aneet. Road or landing, below the huts.
variants_high: Helstrom is south-west, traveller. Ux-Aneet comes first. Road and landing both begin below the huts, a short walk. Drink here before you go. I'll fill your skin myself.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
words: Vees-Wai is our tree-minder. He tends the Hist, the great tree over the pool, from before light. Im-Moro keeps the spring. I take my jars to her stone lip. Ixo-Vaal is the root-herald who trades for the tribe, so he knows what a load is worth.
variants_low: Vees-Wai tends the Hist. Im-Moro keeps the spring. The rest you'll meet.
variants_high: Vees-Wai is our tree-minder. He tends the Hist from before light, so you'll find him at its foot. Im-Moro keeps the spring, where I fill my jars. Ixo-Vaal trades for the tribe. He's a fair man to ask about a load.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
words: My work is the jars. Each morning I carry water up from the spring to fill them for the lodge. A cup from the spring is free to any traveller, not a coin or a pinch of salt. Beds and rope are dear, though. Haj-Tei names the price. Three jars filled, seven waiting: I've only just begun.
variants_low: I fill jars. The water's free. Beds and rope aren't, so ask Haj-Tei.
variants_high: I fill the lodge jars from the spring. A cup is free to you whenever you ask. Take two, if the day is hot. Beds and rope are dear, so ask Haj-Tei the price before you hand over salt.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
words: The talk at the lodge is of the guests. Couriers for the cult and tappers are stopping there on the way to Helstrom, more than I remember. Tappers are the ones who draw sap out of trees. I'd sooner they drew it far from our pool. I see their boots on the step when I carry the jars past.
variants_low: More couriers and tappers at the lodge than before. Tappers draw sap. That's all I'll say.
variants_high: The lodge has been busy, traveller. Couriers and tappers sleep there on the way to Helstrom, more than I remember. Tappers draw sap from trees, so keep your own counsel near them. Haj-Tei knows their faces better than I do.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
words: We are the families who live round the spring. My hut is Mee-Sei, Tsono-Ra, Ux-Ossa and me. Between the cooking and the jars we mend rope for the lodge to sell. If two families quarrel, Vees-Wai hears out both sides, then settles it.
variants_low: Families by the spring. We mend rope. Vees-Wai settles quarrels.
variants_high: We live round the spring, four of us to my hut. Between the jars and the cooking we mend rope. Come by Tsono-Ra's length and pull it yourself. When families quarrel, Vees-Wai hears both sides out.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4
words: A spring village. Travellers stop here for beds and water. The water is free and safe unboiled, rare here. Salt is reaching it. Villagers blame the salt works upstream.
variants_low: A spring village. Water free, beds dear. Salt's in it.
variants_high: A spring village. Travellers stop here for beds and water. The water is free and safe unboiled, rare here. Salt is reaching it. Villagers blame the salt works upstream. Drink before you go.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4
words: Helstrom is the interior's capital. The city grew inside a Hist grove. After the Battle of Argonia our armies withdrew there. The Empire decided against besieging it. No army has taken the place.
variants_low: Our capital, in a Hist grove. No army took it.
variants_high: Helstrom is the interior's capital. The city grew inside a Hist grove. After the Battle of Argonia our armies withdrew there. The Empire decided against besieging it. No army has taken the place. I'd like to see it again.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4
words: A Hist is a mind in a tree. Eggs lie in a clutch by its roots. Naming-day sap shapes our scales and is our soul. The minder reads its signs.
variants_low: A tree with a mind. We hatch by it.
variants_high: A Hist is a mind in a tree. Eggs lie in a clutch by its roots. Naming-day sap shapes our scales and is our soul. The minder reads its signs for us.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4
words: The Border and Prison roads are old Imperial work. We still use the old names. The Tag House sits on a dry rise beside the Prison road.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads. Old names. Walk them.
variants_high: The Border and Prison roads are old Imperial work. We still use the old names. The Tag House sits on a dry rise beside the Prison road. Carry water.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4
words: Tear is a Dunmer town on the coastal plain north of the saltrice fields. From Thorn the Tear road leads there. House Dres sold slaves out of Tear for centuries.
variants_low: A Dunmer town to the north. House Dres sold slaves there.
variants_high: Tear is a Dunmer town on the coastal plain north of the saltrice fields. From Thorn the Tear road leads there. House Dres sold slaves out of Tear for centuries.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4
words: Thorn is the border city among the saltrice fields. From there the Tear road leaves for Morrowind. House Dres raided it for slaves. Its Ash-Reed Accord disputes title to the fields.

variants_high: Thorn is the border city among the saltrice fields. From there the Tear road leaves for Morrowind. House Dres raided it for slaves. Its Ash-Reed Accord disputes title to the fields.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4

variants_high: A tree-minder looks after a village's Hist. He reads what the tree shows and what it wants. If trouble comes for the eggs or the tribe, he feels it first. The Many-Root Conclave sends minders to the villages. Ours is Vees-Wai.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4
words: A village round a spring, a short walk from the road. I sit on the lodge step and roll seed pods with travellers for a night's meal.
variants_low: It's a village. Walk round it.
variants_high: A village round a spring, a short walk from the road. Come to the lodge step. I'll show you the pods and stake you a meal.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4
words: Salt is in the spring water now. Taste it at the stone lip. The wasps trouble me more. They nest close to the fire stand and go for the pots.
variants_low: Salt in the spring. Wasps by the fire stand. Stay clear.
variants_high: Salt is in the spring water now. Taste it at the stone lip. The wasps trouble me more. They nest close to the fire stand, so stay off that path.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4
words: The landing is below the huts, where the canoes lie. The track north meets the Border road in a few minutes. Past that, I don't know.
variants_low: Landing below the huts. Track north for the road.
variants_high: The landing is below the huts, where the canoes lie. The track north meets the Border road in a few minutes. Past that, ask the herald.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4
words: The spring families fetch water, cook and mend rope to sell. I'm one of them. Travellers pay dear for beds and rope, then come back to the lodge anyway.
variants_low: Families fetch water and mend rope to sell. Ask them.
variants_high: The spring families fetch water, cook and mend rope to sell. I'm one of them. Travellers pay dear for beds and rope, then come back to the lodge. I know half their names.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4
words: I work the lodge step, rolling seed pods. Wager a night's meal with me if you like. Beds and rope cost dear here.
variants_low: The lodge step. Beds and rope cost dear. Pay or leave.
variants_high: I work the lodge step with seed pods. Travellers wager a night's meal. Beds and rope cost dear, so I'll stake you one throw free.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4
words: Travellers say cutters are chopping at the fringe of a Hist grove inland. I can't say how far. The Conclave's minders keep those trees, so they will hear of it.
variants_low: Cutters at a grove inland. Ask the minder.
variants_high: Travellers say cutters are chopping at the fringe of a Hist grove inland. I can't say how far. The Conclave's minders keep those trees, so they will hear. I'd bet on a hard answer.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4
words: We haul water, cook at the hut fires and mend rope for selling. If two families quarrel, Vees-Wai the tree-minder hears each and decides.
variants_low: We cook, haul water and mend rope for selling. Quarrels go to the tree-minder.
variants_high: We haul water, cook at the hut fires and mend rope for selling. If two families quarrel, Vees-Wai the tree-minder hears each and decides. I lost one once.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2
words: Travellers stop here for a bed and water on the road to Helstrom. Spring water costs nothing. Drink it unboiled. Few springs allow that here. Salt is getting into it now. We blame the works upstream.
variants_low: Travellers stop for a bed and water. The water is free and safe raw. Salt is coming in from the works upstream.
variants_high: Travellers stop here for a bed and water on the road to Helstrom. Spring water costs nothing. Drink it unboiled, few springs allow that here. Salt is getting into it now. We blame the works upstream.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2
words: Helstrom is our capital, deep in the interior. The city grew up inside a grove of Hist trees. After the fight at Argonia, the native armies fell back into it. The Empire would not lay siege. It has never been taken.
variants_low: Our capital. Built into a Hist grove. The armies fell back there. Never taken.
variants_high: Helstrom is our capital, deep in the interior. The city grew up inside a grove of Hist trees. After the fight at Argonia, the native armies fell back into it. The Empire would not lay siege. No army took it. Go and see.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2
words: The Empire made these roads and the waystation. We still use the first names: Prison road, Border road, Mile House. Toward the Rose goes the Prison road. The Tag House sits on a dry rise next to it.
variants_low: Imperial roads and a waystation. We use the old names. The Tag House is on a rise.
variants_high: The Empire made these roads and the waystation. We still use the first names: Prison road, Border road, Mile House. Toward the Rose goes the Prison road. The Tag House sits on a dry rise next to it. Go dry-shod.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2
words: Tear is a Dunmer town on the coastal plain. Saltrice country lies just south of it. The road to Tear comes down from Thorn. House Dres ran slaving out of it for centuries.
variants_low: A Dunmer town on the coast plain. The road comes from Thorn. House Dres ran slaves there.
variants_high: Tear is a Dunmer town on the coastal plain. Saltrice country lies just south of it. The road to Tear comes down from Thorn. House Dres ran slaving out of it for centuries. Do not go there.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2
words: The Tear road leaves Thorn for Morrowind. Thorn is the border city on the north side, beside the saltrice fields. House Dres raided Thorn for slaves. They profited from its rice. Now the Accord argues over title to the fields.
variants_low: A border city by the rice fields. The Tear road leaves it. Dres raided it. The Accord argues title.
variants_high: The Tear road leaves Thorn for Morrowind. Thorn is the border city on the north side, beside the saltrice fields. House Dres raided Thorn for slaves. They profited from its rice. Now the Accord argues over title to the fields.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2
words: The minder looks after one village's tree and reads its signs and what it wants. He feels trouble among the eggs and among the tribe. The Conclave sends minders to the villages. What the tree says to him, I do not ask.
variants_low: He reads one tree's signs. He feels trouble in the tribe and the eggs. The Conclave sends him. That is all.
variants_high: The minder looks after one village's tree and reads its signs and what it wants. He feels trouble among the eggs and among the tribe. The Conclave sends minders to the villages. Vees-Wai is ours, speak to him kindly.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2
words: Eaten yet? This is the village over the spring. I cook at the fire stand before our hut and keep the pot lidded. The wasps come for it.
variants_low: Greenspring. The spring is there. I have a pot to watch.
variants_high: This is Greenspring, the village over the spring. I cook at the stand before our hut. Sit by the fire, the pot is nearly done.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2
words: Salt comes down from the works upstream. The village blames them. Wasps nest close to my fire stand too, so the pot stays covered all day.
variants_low: Salt from the works upstream. Wasps at my stand. Mind yourself.
variants_high: Salt comes down from the works upstream, the village blames them. Wasps nest close to my stand, so keep clear of the thatch. Stay by the pot, I will watch the lid.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2
words: Helstrom is south-west of the spring. Walk past Ux-Aneet. The landing is below the huts if you want the river. Have you eaten first? Eat, then go.
variants_low: South-west, past Ux-Aneet. The landing is below the huts.
variants_high: Helstrom is south-west of the spring, past Ux-Aneet. The landing is below the huts if you want the river. Take bread with you, the walk is long.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2

variants_high: Vees-Wai is the tree-minder, he tends the Hist. Im-Moro keeps the spring. I cook for the families at the hut, so you will find me by the pot.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2
