speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2
words: Salt is getting into the spring. Talk at the lodge blames the works upstream. Mostly I hear about wasps, at my own pot.
variants_low: Salt in the spring. The works upstream, they say. Ask at the lodge.
variants_high: Salt is getting into the spring. Talk at the lodge blames the works upstream. I hear it all while I stir the pot, so come back at dusk.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2
words: Have you eaten? We cook over the fire stands. The lodge jars get filled from the spring by us too. Mine is the stand before our hut.
variants_low: We cook over the stands. We fill the lodge jars. Nothing more.
variants_high: Have you eaten? We cook over the fire stands. We fill the lodge jars from the spring too. Mine is the stand before our hut, come by at midday.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
words: This village sits on the Helstrom road, so travellers stop for a cup and a bed. The spring costs nothing. Few springs around here give water you can drink unboiled. Salt is reaching it now. The villagers blame the works upstream.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
words: Helstrom is the capital of our whole interior. The city has grown into a Hist grove. I haven't seen it yet, being only on the road toward it. Hours still, by my reckoning.
variants_low: Helstrom is the capital of our interior. The city has grown into a Hist grove. I haven't seen it.
variants_high: Helstrom is the capital of our whole interior. The city has grown into a Hist grove. I haven't seen it yet. Come along the road with me and we'll both see it.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
words: A Hist has a mind of its own and is older than any people. Our eggs sit together among the roots until they hatch. When the naming day comes, every hatchling drinks the sap. That sap shapes the body and scales for life. It's our blood and soul, so at death the spirit goes home to the tree. The minder reads its signs and says how the clutch is faring.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
words: Ojel is what we call outsiders. You needn't take it ill, since it's a plain word with no insult in it. What the tree makes of outsiders isn't mine to tell.
variants_low: Ojel means outsider. It's a plain word with no insult in it. Don't ask me what the tree thinks.
variants_high: Ojel is what we call outsiders. You needn't take it ill, since it's a plain word with no insult in it. I'd use it to your face. What the tree makes of outsiders isn't mine to tell.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
words: The Border road and the Prison road are old Imperial roads. People still use the old names, for the Mile House waystation too. Follow the Prison road and you'd come to the Rose. The Tag House sits on a dry rise next to that road.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
words: Tear is a border town of the Dunmer, up on the coastal plain north of the saltrice country. You reach it by the Tear road from Thorn. For centuries, House Dres ran slaves through the town.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
words: Thorn is a border city. It stands at the north of the saltrice fields, where the Tear road leaves for Morrowind. Long ago, House Dres raided it for slaves. Over title to those fields, the Thorn Ash-Reed Accord now argues.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
words: A minder looks after the Hist of his village and talks for it. He reads what the tree shows and what it wants. When the eggs are in danger, or the tribe is, he feels it. The Many-Root Conclave sends the minders to their villages.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
words: I'm bound for Helstrom, so I stopped here for the night. I pay for my bed in salt and I resent what they ask. This isn't my tribe's tree over the pool, so I drink as a guest. Hours of walking yet before the road ends for me.
variants_low: I'm bound for Helstrom. I stopped here for the night because the road says so. I pay for the bed in salt. This isn't my tribe's tree over the pool so that is all I will say of it.
variants_high: I'm bound for Helstrom, so I stopped here for the night. The bed costs me salt and I resent it. This isn't my tribe's tree over the pool, so I drink as a guest. If you walk my way, I'll show you where the track turns.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
words: Salt is getting into the spring from the salt works upstream. The village blames the works for it. I taste it in my cup at dusk, a little more each night. The tree over the pool looks sicker for it.
variants_low: Salt is getting into the spring from the salt works upstream. Drink early in the day, before it shows.
variants_high: Salt is getting into the spring from the salt works upstream. The village blames the works for it. Drink at dawn, when the cold hides the taste. I'd not ask the tree how it feels. It looks sick enough.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
words: Take the track north from the huts, a few minutes, to the Border road. Go east on it a few minutes, then the track south-east, then south-west for some twenty minutes. A short track north-east after that brings you into Ux-Aneet. Helstrom is hours on beyond it. I've walked a good many of them already.
variants_low: Track north from the huts to the Border road. East on it, then the track south-east, then south-west some twenty minutes. A short track north-east reaches Ux-Aneet.
variants_high: Take the track north from the huts, a few minutes, to the Border road. Go east on it a few minutes, then the track south-east, then south-west for some twenty minutes. A short track north-east brings you into Ux-Aneet. Helstrom is hours on beyond it. Walk it with me and the hours go faster.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
words: Vees-Wai tends the Hist over the pool. He's the tree-minder. I hardly know him, since it isn't my tribe's tree and I stay one night. Haj-Tei keeps the lodge where I sleep. He's the one who gets my salt.
variants_low: Vees-Wai tends the Hist over the pool. I don't know him. Haj-Tei has the lodge.
variants_high: Vees-Wai tends the Hist over the pool. He's the tree-minder. I'd greet him if I knew him better. It isn't my tribe's tree, so I only watch from the path. Haj-Tei keeps the lodge where I sleep. He's fair about the salt.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
words: Rope is dear here. So is a bed. I paid for mine in salt. The rope I paid for the same way. The village calls that a fair price. I call it a toll on people with no other roof before Helstrom.
variants_low: Rope is dear here. So is a bed. I paid in salt for both. The price is the price.
variants_high: Rope is dear here. So is a bed. I paid in salt for both, though the lodge will name a better coil if you ask for it. I call it a toll on people with no other roof before Helstrom.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
words: The lodge is full of cult couriers and tappers, all of them on the road to Helstrom. A tapper draws sap from trees. My guess is their packs hold more than their ledgers say.
variants_low: Cult couriers and tappers fill the lodge on the road to Helstrom. A tapper draws sap from trees. Ask them yourself.
variants_high: The lodge is full of cult couriers and tappers, all of them on the road to Helstrom. A tapper draws sap from trees. My guess is their packs hold more than their ledgers say. Sleep with your own pack under your head.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
words: Helstrom is the Argonian interior's capital. From the spring you go south-west, through Ux-Aneet, to reach it. That's why travellers like me stop in Greenspring for water and a bed. The water here is safe to drink unboiled. That's rare in these parts.
variants_low: Helstrom is the Argonian interior's capital. It lies south-west of the spring, past Ux-Aneet. Travellers stop in Greenspring for water and a bed. The water is safe unboiled.
variants_high: Helstrom is the Argonian interior's capital. From the spring you go south-west, through Ux-Aneet, to reach it. Travellers like me stop in Greenspring for water and a bed. Drink deep, because the water here is safe unboiled. That's rare in these parts.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
words: The An-Xileel are the government of Argonia. They began in the Oblivion Crisis as a party. Their party drove the Empire out of the marsh. They want Imperial ways gone from the province. They coined the word lukiul, a slur for Argonians raised in the Empire's habits.
variants_low: The An-Xileel govern Argonia. They began as a party in that crisis. They drove out the Empire and want Imperial ways gone. Lukiul is their slur for the assimilated.
variants_high: The An-Xileel are the government of Argonia. They began in the Oblivion Crisis as a party. Their party drove the Empire out of the marsh. They want Imperial ways gone from the province. They coined the word lukiul, a slur for Argonians raised in the Empire's habits. Use neither the word nor the habits here.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
words: Travellers bound for Helstrom stop here. They come for a bed and a cup of water. The cup costs nothing. Few springs in this region give water you can drink unboiled. Salt is reaching it now. The village blames the works upstream.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
words: The Empire decided against a siege of Helstrom. Our armies withdrew to it once the Battle of Argonia ended. No army has taken the city. Every load I enter goes toward it.
variants_low: Our armies withdrew to Helstrom. The Empire decided against a siege. No army has taken it.
variants_high: Once the Battle of Argonia ended, our armies withdrew to Helstrom. The Empire decided against a siege. No army has taken the city. Every load in my ledger goes toward it. I wish it well.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
words: A Hist is a great tree with a mind. Our eggs lie in a clutch at its roots. Every hatchling drinks its sap on the naming day. The minder reads the tree's signs and reports to the village how the clutch is doing.
variants_low: A Hist is a tree with a mind. Hatchlings drink its sap on the naming day. The minder reads its signs for the village.
variants_high: A Hist is a great tree with a mind. Ours stands over the spring. Our eggs lie in a clutch at its roots. Every hatchling drinks its sap on the naming day. The minder reads the tree's signs and tells the village how the clutch is doing.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
words: Ojel is what we call outsiders such as you. It carries no insult. Lukiul is a slur coined by the An-Xileel for Argonians who lived assimilated among the Empire's people. Do not say it to an Argonian's face.
variants_low: Ojel means outsider. That is you. Lukiul is a slur from the An-Xileel for assimilated Argonians. Do not say it here.
variants_high: Ojel is what we call outsiders such as you. It carries no insult. You are welcome to it. Lukiul is a slur coined by the An-Xileel for Argonians who lived assimilated among the Empire's people. Do not say it to an Argonian's face.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
words: The Mile House waystation and the Border road are Imperial work. So is the Prison road. We still use the old names. Beside the Prison road, on a dry rise, is the Tag House. The road runs toward the Rose.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
words: Tear is a town of the Dunmer on the coastal plain, north of the saltrice country. You reach it by the Tear road from Thorn. For centuries House Dres ran its slave trading out of there.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
words: Thorn is a city on our northern border, among the saltrice fields. From Thorn the Tear road leads over the border into Morrowind. House Dres raided it for slaves in the old days. Thorn's Ash-Reed Accord today quarrels over title to those fields.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
words: Vees-Wai tends our Hist and speaks for it. He reads its signs and its will. When the eggs are in trouble, or the tribe, he feels it. The Many-Root Conclave sends out minders to villages like ours and has charge of the trees.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
words: The An-Xileel govern Argonia. The Veiled Reed is their covert office. It protects the province from enemies with secrecy and coercion. Their factors walk the interior as agents. I send the ones who lodge here on before dark.
variants_low: The An-Xileel govern. The Veiled Reed is their covert office. It guards the province by secrecy and coercion. Its factors walk the interior.
variants_high: The An-Xileel govern Argonia. The Veiled Reed is their covert office. It protects the province from enemies with secrecy and coercion. Their factors walk the interior as agents. I send the ones who lodge here on before dark. Mind your talk on this road.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
words: The village stands on firm ground because the spring rises here. I am the root-herald, so I deal with the travellers bound for Helstrom. Taste the water at the pool before you speak to any of us.
variants_low: Firm ground and a spring. I am the root-herald and I trade with those bound for Helstrom. Drink at the pool or leave.
variants_high: Greenspring stands on firm ground above a good spring. I am the root-herald, so the trading is mine. Drink at the pool first. My house is on the north side of the common.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
words: Salt is in the spring water now, coming down from upstream. A little more each week. The Hist over the pool droops with it. I send travellers on before dark, because I have no time to warn each of them twice.
variants_low: There is salt in the spring. Drink it or leave it. Be gone before dark.
variants_high: Salt is reaching the spring from upstream. Taste your flask before a long road. The Hist droops over the pool. Be gone before dark. I will enter your load early.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
words: Helstrom is south-west of here, past Ux-Aneet. I give no time for it. The landing is below the huts. The road and the landing are both near the spring.
variants_low: Helstrom is south-west, past Ux-Aneet. Landing below the huts. Road by the spring.
variants_high: Helstrom is south-west, past Ux-Aneet. Take the road from the spring if you walk. Take the landing below the huts if you want the river. I give no time for either.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
words: Im-Moro pours at the stone lip and Vees-Wai tends the Hist. The families by the spring twist and mend rope for the bed-keeper to sell. Travellers I see myself, since the trading is mine.
variants_low: Im-Moro pours. Vees-Wai tends the Hist. The families mend rope. I trade.
variants_high: Im-Moro pours at the stone lip and will give you a second cup if you ask. Vees-Wai tends the Hist. The families by the spring twist and mend rope for the bed-keeper. The trading is mine, so come to me first.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
words: A load bound for Helstrom, you say. That goes in my book with your name. Water here costs nothing. A bed or a length of rope is dear. I say the price first.
variants_low: Loads for Helstrom go in my book. Water is free. Beds and rope are dear. Pay or leave.
variants_high: A load bound for Helstrom, you say. I enter it with your name. Water here costs nothing. Beds and rope are dear for most, but I will shave the price for a traveller I know.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
words: More cult couriers and tappers sleep at the lodge each month on their way to Helstrom. Haj-Tei the bed-keeper swears that a few of the silent ones are factors of the Veiled Reed. I enter their loads and send them on before dark.
variants_low: Couriers and tappers sleep at the lodge. Haj-Tei says some are factors of the Veiled Reed. Not my talk.
variants_high: More couriers and tappers sleep at the lodge each month, bound for Helstrom. Haj-Tei the bed-keeper swears a few silent ones are factors of the Veiled Reed. If you meet one, do not share his table.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
words: I am the tribe's envoy to the world beyond it. I gather news from travellers and bargain over trade for the village. The state gives the office no rank. I write the ledger of loads bound for Helstrom.
variants_low: I am the tribe's envoy. I gather news and bargain over trade. The office has no rank in the state. The ledger is mine.
variants_high: I am the tribe's envoy to the world beyond it. I gather news from every traveller and bargain over trade for the village. The state gives the office no rank. I write the ledger of loads bound for Helstrom, so bring me your news.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
words: Greenspring sits on the way to Helstrom, so travellers stop here for water and a bed. The water costs nothing and you can drink it as it comes, with no boiling. That's rare round here. The others tell me salt is reaching the spring. They blame the salt works upstream. I taste nothing wrong.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
words: The Argonian interior has its capital at Helstrom, a city that grew right into a Hist grove. Once the Battle of Argonia was over, the native armies drew back there for refuge. The Empire decided against a siege. No army has ever taken it. Travellers bound there drink at my lip first.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
words: A Hist is a huge tree. It has a mind of its own and it's older than the peoples beside it. Ours grows over my spring. On the naming day, a hatchling drinks its sap. That sap shapes the body and scales for as long as the life lasts. So we're made of the tree, plainly. I pour under it every morning.
variants_low: A Hist is a huge tree with a mind. Its sap shapes a hatchling's body and scales for life. That's all I'll say here.
variants_high: A Hist is a huge tree with a mind of its own. It's older than the peoples around it. A hatchling drinks its sap on the naming day. The sap shapes the body and scales for life. Ours is the one over my pool. Sit by the stone and look up at it a while.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
words: These are old Imperial works: the Border road, the Prison road and a waystation called the Mile House. Folk still use the old names. The Prison road leads out toward the Rose. On a dry rise next to that road sits the Tag House. Our track meets the Border road a few minutes north of the pool.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
words: Tear lies on the coastal plain, a Dunmer town on the border, with the saltrice country to its south. You reach it by the Tear road from Thorn. For centuries the slave trade of House Dres was run out of there. I only know it from travellers.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
words: Thorn is the border city in the north, among the saltrice fields. From it the Tear road goes into Morrowind. House Dres used to raid there for slaves and grew rich on the rice. These days the Thorn Ash-Reed Accord quarrels over who owns the fields.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
words: Every village Hist has a minder. He reads what the tree signals and what it wants. He feels it if trouble comes to the eggs or the tribe. The Many-Root Conclave sends such minders out to the villages. Ours is Vees-Wai, who works up by the Hist while I work below at the spring.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
words: The spring made this village. I work at the stone lip with the ladle on its cord, so a stranger gets a cup from me before anything else. Come up from the landing and you'll find the pool under the Hist, cold and clear. Taste it first. Then ask me what you like.
variants_low: This is Greenspring. The spring is at the stone lip. Drink or step aside for the next cup.
variants_high: Greenspring has the best water on the road. Come up past the spring house and I'll fill the ladle twice for you. Taste first, then ask me about anything you like.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
words: Giant wasps have nests by the huts, so leave the thatch alone. The village puts a bitterness in the cup down to the salt works upstream. Vees-Wai tastes it, as does the jar-filler. The water under my ladle comes up clean, to my tongue. Take a mouthful and judge.
variants_low: Wasps nest by the huts. The salt works upstream get the village's blame. I taste nothing wrong.
variants_high: Giant wasps nest by the huts, so mind the thatch. The salt works upstream get the village's blame for a bitterness in the cup. Vees-Wai tastes it. To me the water is clean. Drink a cup, then tell me honestly.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
words: Past Ux-Aneet and Cut-and-Carried, to the south-west, you reach Helstrom. Either way out is close. The road is a short walk from the pool. So is the river landing, down the bank to the north past the spring house. Drink before you start on that road.
variants_low: Helstrom is south-west of here, beyond Ux-Aneet and Cut-and-Carried. Road and landing are a short walk.
variants_high: Go south-west for Helstrom, beyond Ux-Aneet and Cut-and-Carried. The road is a short walk from the pool. So is the landing, north along the bank. Drink your fill before you go. The water costs nothing.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
words: Vees-Wai is our tree-minder, so he tends the Hist over my pool. Haj-Tei sells beds and rope at the lodge. Ixo-Vaal is the root-herald. He bargains with the traders. The families by the spring cook, haul water and mend rope. Sooner or later each of them comes up to my lip.
variants_low: Vees-Wai tends the Hist. Haj-Tei sells beds. The rest cook and mend. Now drink.
variants_high: Vees-Wai is our tree-minder. He tends the Hist over my pool. Haj-Tei sells beds. Ixo-Vaal bargains for the village. The spring families cook and mend. Stay a day and you'll meet them all at the lip.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
words: Water I give away, whoever climbs up for it. Beds and rope are the lodge's trade and they cost plenty, since the village settled one price together. I'm at the lip from first light. If a traveller stays for a second cup, he gets my talk too.
variants_low: Water's free. Beds and rope cost plenty at the lodge. That's all I'll say of work.
variants_high: Water I pour free, as many cups as you like. The lodge sells beds and rope at one price the village settled together. It's the same price for you as for any courier before you. I'm at the lip from first light.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
words: Hearth Heal is a small mending. I keep it with the ladle. It closes a cut and eases a bruise. Drink first. Then settle my price. I will show you how it is done.
variants_low: Hearth Heal closes a cut and eases a bruise. I teach it for a price. Pay it or step aside.
variants_high: Hearth Heal is a small mending. I keep it with the ladle. It closes a cut and eases a bruise. For you, visitor, I will show it gladly once my price is settled.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
words: Travellers who stop for water say cutters have started on the outer trees of a Hist grove inland. By grove, they mean a cluster of the great trees. Each has a mind of its own, so you can't fell one like a log. We've one over this pool. I listen when the road talks of it.
variants_low: Travellers say cutters have started on a Hist grove inland. Each tree there has a mind of its own.
variants_high: Travellers who stop for water say cutters have started on a Hist grove inland. A grove is a stand of the great trees. Each has a mind of its own. We've one over this pool, so tell me anything more you hear on the road.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
words: I'm the spring-keeper. The spring is a pool of clear water below the Hist, with a ring of boulders round it. I stand at the stone lip with the ladle on its cord. Any traveller drinks free. You taste before you speak, so I fill the ladle and put it in your hand before you've said your name.
variants_low: I'm the spring-keeper. The pool under the Hist has boulders round it. I stand at the stone lip with the ladle on its cord. Travellers drink free. Taste before you speak.
variants_high: I'm the spring-keeper. The pool of clear water below the Hist, with its ring of boulders, is mine to tend. The ladle hangs on its cord at the stone lip. Every traveller drinks free. Taste first, then speak. Do that and I'll talk till dusk.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
words: Greenspring is where travellers bound for Helstrom halt for water and a bed. The water is free to all of them. It can be drunk unboiled. Few springs here allow that. Salt is reaching the spring from the works upstream. The village blames the works.
variants_low: Travellers bound for Helstrom stop here. The water is free and drinkable unboiled. There is salt in it from upstream.
variants_high: Travellers bound for Helstrom halt at Greenspring for water and a bed. The water is free to any of them. It is safe to drink unboiled, which few springs here are. Salt is reaching it from the works upstream. The village blames the works.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
words: Helstrom is the city of the interior. Its streets grew in among the trees of a Hist grove. After the great battle, the native armies withdrew there. The Empire would not besiege it. Not one army has taken it.
variants_low: Helstrom is the city of the interior. The armies withdrew there once. No army has taken it.
variants_high: Helstrom is the city of the interior. It grew in among a grove of Hist. The native armies withdrew there after the Battle of Argonia. The Empire chose against a siege. No army has taken it. The way lies south-west.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
words: A Hist is a tree you do not cut. It has a mind and it is older than any people. We hatch near its roots. Every hatchling drinks the sap on its naming day. The sap becomes our blood and soul. At death, the spirit goes back to its Hist.
variants_low: A Hist is a tree. On the naming day, a hatchling drinks the sap. The sap is our blood and soul.
variants_high: A Hist is a tree you do not cut. It is older than any people. We hatch near its roots. On the naming day, a hatchling drinks the sap. The sap becomes blood and soul in the body. The spirit goes back to the Hist at death. Come and sit by mine, if you like.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
words: The stewards of the Hist form the Many-Root Conclave. A minder is sent to keep each tree. The Conclave sees that every Hist gets asked for consent. My work is to read the signs and the will of mine. It sent me out to this village.
variants_low: Stewards of the Hist. Their minders keep the trees. They ask each tree for its consent. I read my tree's signs. They sent me to this village.
variants_high: The Conclave is an order of Hist stewards. Its minders keep the trees. Each Hist gets asked for consent. I read the signs and will of mine. The Conclave sent me to this village. I am glad of the post.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
words: Those are old Imperial roads. The Mile House is the old waystation. People still use the names that the Empire gave them. The Tag House stands beside the Prison road on a dry rise. The old ones say the roads rotted the cargo.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads, with the old names. The Tag House stands on a dry rise beside the Prison road.
variants_high: The Prison road, the Border road and the Mile House are old Imperial roads and a waystation. People still call them by the old names. The Tag House stands on a dry rise beside the Prison road. Keep to the road and you will not lose the way.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
words: I have not walked there. Tear is a border town of the Dunmer, out on the coastal plain, a little north of the saltrice country. From Thorn, the Tear road leads there. For centuries House Dres worked its slave trade out of Tear. I have no good word for that trade.
variants_low: A Dunmer town on the northern border. House Dres ran its slave trade there.
variants_high: I have not walked there. Tear is a Dunmer town on the border, on the coastal plain north of the saltrice country. The Tear road reaches it from Thorn. House Dres kept its slave trade in Tear for centuries.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
words: Thorn is the border city of the northern saltrice fields. From Thorn, the Tear road goes into Morrowind. House Dres raided it for slaves once and grew rich on its rice. Today the Accord there disputes the title to the fields.
variants_low: Thorn is a border city by the saltrice fields. The Tear road leaves it.
variants_high: Thorn is the border city of the northern saltrice fields. The Tear road leaves it for Morrowind. House Dres raided it for slaves and profited from the rice. Now the Accord disputes the title to the fields. I would not trust a ledger from there.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
words: A tree-minder tends one Hist and speaks for it. I read its signs and its will. When the eggs are in trouble, or the tribe, I feel it. The Conclave posts minders to the villages. What the tree says to me, word for word, is not for strangers.
variants_low: A minder tends one Hist and reads its signs. He feels trouble in the eggs or the tribe. The Conclave posts him.
variants_high: A tree-minder tends one Hist and speaks for it. I read its signs and its will. I feel it when the eggs or the tribe are in trouble. The Conclave posts minders to the villages. If you see a leaf pile by the root, that is my work.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
words: The Conclave is an order of Hist stewards. It sends a minder to each village. A minder reads the signs and will of the tree. The Conclave sees that every Hist gets asked for its consent. When the eggs or the tribe are in trouble, I feel it.
variants_low: The Conclave sends minders to the villages. I read the signs of my tree. The Conclave asks each Hist for consent. I feel trouble in the eggs or the tribe.
variants_high: The Conclave is an order of Hist stewards. It sends a minder to each village. I read my tree's signs. I feel trouble in the eggs or the tribe before word reaches me. The Conclave sees that every Hist gets asked for consent. Ask me more if you wish.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
words: Greenspring is the village that stands over the spring. The Hist grows above the water. I keep the ground round its root clear. At the last dusk, I swept the leaves into a heap by the shrine.
variants_low: It is a village with a spring in it and a tree above the spring. The tree is what I keep.
variants_high: Taste the water at the clear pool under the Hist before you do anything else. That is how the village welcomes a visitor. I have swept the shrine ground today if you wish to see it.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
words: Salt is coming down into the spring from the works upstream. The village blames those works. The Hist over the water has begun to sicken. The spring-keeper will not grant it, but I taste the salt.
variants_low: The spring has salt in it. The wasps nest near the huts. That is enough danger for a stranger.
variants_high: The salt is the worst of it. Drink at the pool under the Hist anyway. I will say so if the taste turns. Walk wide of the huts, for the giant wasps nest there.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
words: Go south-west for Helstrom. You pass Ux-Aneet first, then Cut-and-Carried. The Border road is close to the spring. So is the river landing, a few steps down.
variants_low: South-west. Past Ux-Aneet and Cut-and-Carried.
variants_high: South-west for Helstrom, past Ux-Aneet and then Cut-and-Carried. Go by daylight. Fill a flask at the spring first. The water costs nothing.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
words: Im-Moro holds the ladle at the spring and the root-herald Ixo-Vaal keeps the ledger for the road to Helstrom. The families by the spring cook the meals and carry the water. They mend the rope too. I am the minder, at the tree.
variants_low: There is a spring-keeper, a root-herald, the families and me at the tree. That is the village.
variants_high: Neexa-Xuhil fills the lodge jars at the spring each morning. He tastes the salt before the rest of us do.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
words: My work is the Hist. I watch its crown and I sweep the fallen leaves from its root at every dusk. The village sells beds and rope to travellers bound for Helstrom at a price we all agreed together.
variants_low: I tend the tree. The bed-keeper sells the beds and the rope. I have leaves to sweep.
variants_high: I tend the Hist and sweep its root at every dusk. You have my leave to stand at the shrine at its foot, where the totems and candles are. Touch none of them.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
words: Travellers at the lodge talk of a Hist in the south that has gone silent. That means it no longer speaks with its tribe. It can happen when the tree is sick, or when it closes itself away from the rest of the Hist. At the last dusk my own tree was still speaking.
variants_low: A Hist in the south has gone silent. That is all I heard.
variants_high: Travellers say a Hist in the south has gone silent. It no longer speaks with its tribe. A tree may do that when it is sick or when it shuts itself away from the others. I keep a close watch on mine. You are welcome to ask me what I see.

speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
words: I tend the village Hist. It is a great tree and it has a mind of its own. At each dusk, I sweep the fallen leaves off its root. The Many-Root Conclave sent me here. They are the Hist stewards.
variants_low: I tend the Hist, a tree with a mind. I sweep its leaves at dusk. The Conclave sent me. Its stewards keep the trees.
variants_high: I tend the village Hist. It is a great tree that has a mind. Every dusk, I sweep the fallen leaves from its root. The Conclave of Hist stewards sent me here. My house stands beside the tree.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.flotilla-speaker
words: It's the floating quarter off Lilmoth's east bank. I speak for it. Four old hulls that carried cargo ashore now serve as our houses, lined along a single timber pier. The market rafts lie across the planks from us. The crews would vote the quarter a fair place to live.
variants_low: The floating quarter off the east bank. Four old hulls as houses on one pier, rafts across the planks.
variants_high: It's the floating quarter off Lilmoth's east bank, shore-foot. Four old hulls that carried cargo ashore now serve as our houses, lined along a single timber pier. The market rafts lie across from us. Walk over, I'll vouch for you at the first raft.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.flotilla-speaker
words: Lilmoth is the southern port. It's built over shallow water, which is why big ships anchor out and we carry their cargo in from the deep. Merchants sit on its council to rule the port. They write to me when they want something. Umbriel, the flying city, destroyed it in 4E 48. What stands now went up smaller.
variants_low: Lilmoth is the southern port on shallow water. Merchants rule it. Umbriel destroyed it in 4E 48. It was rebuilt smaller.
variants_high: Lilmoth is the southern port, shore-foot, built over shallow water. That's why we carry the cargo in from the anchorage. Merchants sit on its council to rule. Umbriel, the flying city, destroyed it in 4E 48. It went up smaller after. Walk the track to see it.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.flotilla-speaker
words: The Reed-Sail Compact runs the boats, up the rivers and along the coast. It's the guild that gathers the crews, the routes and the ferries. The pirates they call the Salt-Teeth sail among its crews, so a good name on a hull can cover a raider. Ask whose hull it is before you pay for passage.
variants_low: The Compact is the boat guild. It runs the river and coast boats. Salt-Teeth pirates sail among them. Be careful.
variants_high: The Compact runs the boats on the rivers and the coast, shore-foot. It's the guild of the crews, the routes and the ferries. Pirates they call the Salt-Teeth sail among its crews. I'll point you to an honest hull if you tell me where you're bound.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.flotilla-speaker
words: The Compact is our guild. It covers the boat crews, the routes they run and the ferries. I hold the speaker's post in it here. A council at Lilmoth once tried to license the cargo boats. I called the vote. The crews answered with two weeks of stoppage.
variants_low: The Compact is the guild of the boat crews. A council licensed nothing. Two weeks of stoppage settled that.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.n1
words: Four of us hands sleep in the bunks below the foredeck, all in a row. I like it there. When the council tried to write a licence for our work, we stopped the port. It lasted two weeks.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.n1
words: A big ship stays out in deep water, because Lilmoth has no dock for her. We row out to her anchorage and fetch what she carries.
variants_low: Lilmoth has no dock for a big ship. We fetch the cargo from where she anchors.
variants_high: A big ship stays out in deep water, because Lilmoth has no dock for her. We row out to her anchorage and fetch what she carries. If you want passage out there, the master is Xal-Jei.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.n1
words: No deep hull can dock at Lilmoth. So the lighter goes out to the anchorage and I haul the loads down into her belly. After that, we pole her home. I do it all on bare planks.
variants_low: No deep hull can dock at Lilmoth. I haul loads from the anchorage into the lighter.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.n2
words: We are the Lighter Flotilla. Four old hulls that used to ferry cargo are our houses now. They lie side by side along a timber pier off Lilmoth's east bank. The market rafts float on the far side of it.
variants_low: Four old hulls on a pier, with market rafts across it. That is the flotilla.
variants_high: We are the Lighter Flotilla. Four old hulls that used to ferry cargo are our houses now. They lie side by side along a timber pier off Lilmoth's east bank. The market rafts float on the far side of it. Walk the planks and I'll name you the knots on each hull.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.n2
words: Lilmoth is the port. Our pier starts from its east bank. It stands on shallow water. The big ships anchor far out and small boats ferry the cargo to the quay. speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.n2
words: To an Argonian, ojel means an outsider and carries no insult. You are one. The word to avoid is lukiul. The An-Xileel coined that slur for Argonians raised outside Black Marsh. They cannot hear the Hist. I do not say it on this deck. Who sided with whom in Lilmoth in forty-eight, I do not say either.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.n2
words: Cargo does come ashore at night, past my moorings. It never crosses the quay. I'm laying a short splice in a haul line as I tell you. Those loads are settled at the dice tables on the Outside Barge. The tariff men don't pass my moorings, so they hear nothing of it.
variants_low: Cargo comes ashore at night, off the quay. It's settled at the dice tables on the Outside Barge. I've a splice to finish.
variants_high: Cargo does come ashore at night, past my moorings. It never crosses the quay. I'm laying a short splice in a haul line as I tell you. Those loads are settled at the dice tables on the Outside Barge. Go after dark and watch the dice first, walker. I'll mend your strap meanwhile.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.n2
words: I mend nets on the deck of the south hull, so I'll start with the hulls. Four tarred working boats lie bow-in along this pier, each one a home moored for good. There's a split in the third strand of a haul line in my lap right now. The rafts across the pier are the market. Go there with coin.
variants_low: Four hulls, moored as houses along this pier. The market rafts are across it. I have a split strand to finish.
variants_high: Four tarred hulls lie bow-in along this pier, all moored as houses. I'm on the south one with a split haul line in my lap. Bring me a frayed strap and I'll mend it while you look. The rafts across the pier sell what the tariff line never sees.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.n2
words: Slaughterfish swim thick below the hulls here. The osheeja gar prowl there too. When I work the low end of a net, where the mesh trails toward the water, I sit well back from the deck's edge.
variants_low: Slaughterfish below the hulls. Osheeja gar too. Stay off the edge.
variants_high: Slaughterfish swim thick below the hulls here. The osheeja gar prowl there too. Tie your pack to the rail with a cord. I'll lend you one, so nothing dangles over the side.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.n2
words: From the foot of the pier, a landing stage runs out over the reed shallows to the Lilmoth track. Boats for the anchorage and boats for Archon both leave from the planks beside my hull. South along the track, a few minutes on foot, is the divers' yard. I like to see a walker go off the right way.
variants_low: Landing stage, then the Lilmoth track. Boats for the anchorage and Archon leave from the pier.
variants_high: From the foot of the pier, a landing stage runs out over the reed shallows to the Lilmoth track. Boats for the anchorage and for Archon leave from the planks beside my hull. If the track is too far tonight, the trade ship at the pier head has bunks to let.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.n2
words: The Compact holds the three posts here. I belong to no guild, so I pay it no share. I mend for whoever brings a net. At dusk, the hands cook on deck, hull beside hull. The smoke reaches my stool by the south rail before the lamps are lit.
variants_low: The Compact holds the posts. I pay it no share. Bring a net or go.
variants_high: The Compact holds the three posts here. I belong to no guild, so I pay it no share. I mend for whoever brings a net. That includes you. Sit on the rope coil if you want to talk.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.n2
words: Lilmoth sits on shallow ground, so a big ship cannot dock at its quay. She anchors far out in the bay and the lighters go out to her. I don't haul. I mend the lines and nets the haulers tear. The tariff men do not pass our moorings. That suits a net-mender fine.
variants_low: A big ship cannot dock at Lilmoth. The lighters go out to her. I mend, I don't haul.
variants_high: Lilmoth sits on shallow ground, so a big ship cannot dock at its quay. She anchors far out in the bay and the lighters go out to her. I mend what the haulers tear. Come at dusk, once the lines are tied off. I splice then.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.n2
words: I make torn nets sound again. Worn gear too. I do it in the open on the deck of the south hull, where anyone passing can watch my hands. Anyone may bring me a net. This tear in my lap is a hand-span long. I'll give you its worth before I start.
variants_low: I make torn nets sound again. I do it in the open. Anyone may bring a net, you too.
variants_high: I make torn nets sound again. Worn gear too. I do it in the open on the deck of the south hull, where anyone passing can watch my hands. Anyone may bring me a net. Bring yours and I'll show you the knot as I tie it.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.purser
words: Off Lilmoth's east bank lies a floating quarter, the Lighter Flotilla. Four hulls sit in a row beside one timber pier. Those are houses now. On the pier's far side float the market rafts. For anything the tariff line misses, I'd start there.
variants_low: Four hulls beside a timber pier off Lilmoth's east bank, now houses. The market rafts float on its far side.
variants_high: Off Lilmoth's east bank lies a floating quarter, the Lighter Flotilla. Four hulls sit in a row beside one timber pier. Those are houses now. The market rafts float on the pier's far side. Start there for anything the tariff line misses, customer.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.purser
words: Lilmoth is built over shallow water. A big ship can't dock there, so it anchors out and small boats ferry its cargo to shore. Merchants sit on the council that runs the town. In 4E 48, the flying city Umbriel wrecked it. It was rebuilt smaller.
variants_low: Lilmoth stands over shallow water. Merchants on the council run it. Umbriel wrecked it in 4E 48. It was rebuilt smaller.

In 4E 48, the flying city Umbriel wrecked it. It was rebuilt smaller, customer. The ledgers are tidier for it.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.purser
words: The Compact is the guild of the boatmen, their routes and their ferries. Along the rivers and the coast, its members run the boats. The Salt-Teeth, a pirate band, sail under its name too. A hull wearing the Compact's mark can still be a raider's.
variants_low: A guild of boats. Pirates sail in it. Draw your own line.
variants_high: The Compact is the guild of the boatmen, their routes and their ferries. Along the rivers and the coast, its members run the boats. The Salt-Teeth, a pirate band, sail under its name too. A hull wearing the Compact's mark can still be a raider's. Look at the cargo before you trust the paint.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.purser
words: The Compact has its monopoly because it can stop the port. The council knows it. I only know the ledger side. The ledger says that stoppage was dear.
variants_low: The Compact stops the port when it likes. That is all.
variants_high: The Compact has its monopoly because it can stop the port. The council knows it. I only know the ledger side. I'd call that stoppage dear. The figure stays in my book.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.purser
words: The flotilla speaker, Opens-The-Books, keeps a tally of her own. It lists cargo that left a hull and never reached the quay. I'd have that tally in my hands. Take it from her unseen, then bring it to me.
variants_low: The speaker keeps a tally of cargo that never reached the quay. Bring it to me unseen.
variants_high: The flotilla speaker, Opens-The-Books, keeps a tally of her own. It lists cargo that left a hull and never reached the quay. I'd have that tally in my hands. Take it from her unseen, then bring it to me.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.purser
words: Is that the tally? Cargo off a hull, never on the quay. Yes, that's the line I wanted. Pass it across low, under my book. Keep your voice down while you do.
variants_low: That's the tally. Pass it across low, under my book.
variants_high: Is that the tally? Cargo off a hull, never on the quay. Yes, that's the line I wanted. Pass it across low, under my book. You've done well, customer. Keep your voice down on the way out.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.purser
words: I'm the purser on the Alten Meerhleel trade ship, so the pier head is where I sit and count. Off Lilmoth's east bank, a single timber pier carries the whole row of hulls, bow-in on its south side. Most are tarred black and few would pass a survey. They float, all of them. People live in each one. At dusk, I like the masts with the cooking smoke between them.
variants_low: The pier is public. My counter is not a place to loiter.
variants_high: I'm the purser on the Alten Meerhleel trade ship, so the pier head is where I sit and count. Off Lilmoth's east bank, a single timber pier carries the whole row of hulls, bow-in on its south side. Most are tarred black, but they float and they're warm inside. Come at dusk, when the smoke rises between the masts.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.purser
words: Slaughterfish and osheeja gar prowl under the planks and around the hulls. A bale that goes over the rail is struck from my book that same minute.
variants_low: Fish in the water. Keep off the edge.
variants_high: Slaughterfish and osheeja gar prowl under the planks. Lean over the rail for a dropped bale and you'll be struck from my book that same minute. I'd rather sell you a new bale.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.purser
words: Walkers leave by the landing stage from the pier foot, across the reeds to the Lilmoth track. By water, you board at the pier for the anchorage or for Archon. Along that track south, a few minutes' walk, you reach Under-Yard.
variants_low: Stage for the track. Pier for the boats.
variants_high: Walkers leave by the landing stage from the pier foot, across the reeds to the Lilmoth track. By water, you board at the pier for the anchorage or for Archon. Along that track south, a few minutes' walk, you reach Under-Yard. I like the walk.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.purser
words: The boatmen live aboard the hulls they work. I have one of the three posts the Compact fills here, the purser's. The lighter people back one another because the city needs them all at once. I counted what the stoppage cost us, line by line. The total stays in my book. Ask me a price instead, because those I say aloud.
variants_low: They live on their hulls. I count the ship's books, not their business.
variants_high: The boatmen live aboard the hulls they work. The purser's post is mine. They back one another because the city needs them all at once. I counted what that stoppage cost, line by line. The total stays in my book. Ask me any price you like. Those I say aloud.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.purser
words: Nothing off the anchorage gets to Lilmoth except down in a lighter's hold. My own ship's stores go ashore that way as well. I tick each lot off my book at the pier head before it goes down the side. What I sell from the stores below stays out of the tariff line, so my counter is busier than the quay clerks like.
variants_low: Cargo goes ashore in a lighter. That is all I'll say for free.
variants_high: Nothing off the anchorage gets to Lilmoth except down in a lighter's hold. My stores go that way too. I tick each lot off my book before it goes down the side. Buy from my counter and the tariff clerks never see the sum. It suits us both.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.lighter-flotilla.purser
words: I keep the books for the trade ship. Goods come aboard. Goods go out. I write every line. I sell the ship's goods untaxed from my counter. Anyone who pays the fare gets a bunk below deck. Bunks let, bunks empty, goods received, goods sold. I read the page that way each evening.
variants_low: Books, stores, bunks. Pay the fare or go.
