speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n1
words: Long-Water Hold is where a settled Naga tribe lives, far in the marsh on firm ground. The poling route through the deep swamp passes its landing. Loaded craft can tie up there because the water is deep. Its people look after a Hist and live by their fields. They are after the road trade. They fall out with kin of theirs who belong to no tribe and rob that road.
variants_low: Long-Water Hold is a settled Naga village on firm ground by the poling route. Deep landing. They look after a Hist. They fall out with their tribeless kin over the road trade.
variants_high: Long-Water Hold is where a settled Naga tribe lives, far in the marsh on firm ground. The poling route through the deep swamp passes its landing. Loaded craft can tie up there because the water is deep. Its people look after a Hist and live by their fields. They are after the road trade. They fall out with kin of theirs who belong to no tribe and rob that road. Sell there if you can, friend.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n1
words: A Naga is an Argonian of the tall kind with an adder's look. Stand one of us up and he's near eight feet, sometimes seven, with a very wide mouth full of needle fangs. We live far in the deep marsh. Some Naga rob roads. Others don't. Plenty of Argonians hate us anyway. Plenty don't.
variants_low: Naga are tall Argonians, adder-like, from the deep marsh. Not all rob roads. Not all Argonians hate us.
variants_high: A Naga is an Argonian of the tall kind with an adder's look. Stand one of us up and he's near eight feet, sometimes seven, with a very wide mouth full of needle fangs. We live far in the deep marsh. Some Naga rob roads, but plenty don't. You'll meet Argonians who hate us and others who don't, friend. Judge them one at a time.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n1
words: Surveyors from the Empire marked out the North Cut as a road, going north out of Stormhold to reach the Tear road. They gave up after four kilometres. The land beside it stays empty. The villagers cut stone from it for their yards. The water off it runs down over two fields and a hamlet.
variants_low: The North Cut is a road the Empire's surveyors gave up on after four kilometres. Villagers cut stone from it.
variants_high: Surveyors from the Empire marked out the North Cut as a road, going north out of Stormhold to reach the Tear road. They gave up after four kilometres. The land beside it stays empty. The villagers cut stone from it for their yards, so you may meet them there. The water off it runs down over two fields and a hamlet.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n1
words: The Prison road and the Border road were laid by the Empire. The Mile House was its waystation. People still use the old names for all three. Follow the Prison road and it leads to the Rose. On a dry rise by that road sits the Tag House.
variants_low: Prison road, Border road, Mile House: old Imperial names, still used. The Prison road leads to the Rose. The Tag House sits on a dry rise by it.
variants_high: The Prison road and the Border road were laid by the Empire. The Mile House was its waystation. People still use the old names for all three. Follow the Prison road and it leads to the Rose. On a dry rise by that road sits the Tag House, a good place for a rest, friend.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n1
words: A Naga with no tribe is a tribeless one. Naga are the tall, adder-like Argonians. Most of the brigands in the marsh come from them. They work the tracks when merchants are on foot. One of those bands is Cut-Rope's raiders. I'd sooner you didn't take them for the same as us.
variants_low: Tribeless Naga belong to no tribe. Most of the marsh's brigands are tribeless, adder-like and tall. Cut-Rope's raiders are one band.
variants_high: A Naga with no tribe is a tribeless one. Naga are the tall, adder-like Argonians. Most of the brigands in the marsh come from them. They work the tracks when merchants are on foot. One of those bands is Cut-Rope's raiders. Don't take them for the same as us, friend. We cut a stick and they cut nothing.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n1
words: Two marks on a stick, that's what this camp is worth to a stranger. I'm the lieutenant here. I cut the receipts. We sit on a bench above the Mile House track, where it bends round a pond. A traveller coming down is under our eyes before the first tent shows to him. The smoke gives us away, I grant that. He is standing at the gate before he smells it.
variants_low: This is a camp on a bench above the Mile House track. I cut the receipts here. Come down the bend and we see you first. That's all you need.
variants_high: One mark on a stick is all I ask of you, friend of the gate. I'm the lieutenant here, so I cut the receipts. We sit on a bench above the Mile House track, where it bends round a pond. From the watch we see you coming long before you see a tent. Sit at the fire a while, the smoke is the worst of it.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n1
words: A dead walker brings his whole tribe up the bank against this camp. So we take the load and let him go. The killing on these tracks is Cut-Rope's raiders. The settled tribes lay it at our gate. Death hoppers and hackwings nest round the pond. A crocodile lies in the water.
variants_low: A dead walker brings his tribe against us, so we kill none. Cut-Rope does the killing. There's a crocodile in the pond.
variants_high: A dead walker brings his tribe up the bank against this camp, so we take the load and let him go. Cut-Rope's raiders do the killing on these tracks. The settled tribes blame us for it, as you'll hear. Go round the pond wide. Death hoppers and hackwings nest there. A crocodile lies in the water.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n1
words: You turn off the track for our path at the cane gate, between the two totems. One of the band stands there. Carry on along the track, past us, to the Polers' Camp. The guides there pole travellers down to Dead-Water Village.
variants_low: Our path starts at the cane gate. One of the band stands by the totems. The track goes on to the Polers' Camp.
variants_high: You turn off the track for our path at the cane gate, between the two totems. One of the band is always posted there. Carry on along the track to the Polers' Camp. The guides there pole travellers down to Dead-Water Village. Tell them the lieutenant sent you.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n1
words: Six of us live here. I cut the receipts. The other five take turns at the gate, the bend and the fire. Whoever's off sleeps in the hide tent. Strangers get fed, watched and sent down the track. Most can't read a body, so a raised hand sends them running.
variants_low: Six live here. The five others work in turns. I cut the receipts. Strangers are fed and sent down the track.
variants_high: Six of us live here. I cut the receipts. The other five take turns at the gate, the bend and the fire, so no post stands cold. Strangers get fed at our fire and watched, then sent down the track. Raise a hand slowly if you want to be friendly. Most travellers don't read a body.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n1
words: A fat load is four marks and a long cut. My work is the stopping of loads. The band takes the cargo off a walker's back, then he goes free. I cut a stick for what was taken and split it down the middle. He leaves with one half as his receipt. The other half hangs on the board under the watch. Bux-Xeek smokes the hides, if you ever want to ask him.
variants_low: I cut a stick for every load. The band takes the cargo. You get half the stick. Leave the other half on the board alone.
variants_high: A fat load is four marks and a long cut. I'm the one who cuts them. The band takes the cargo at the gate, then the walker goes on his way with a stick split down the middle as his receipt. The other half hangs on the board under the watch. Bring me a clean hide to trade next time and I'll cut the stick short.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n1
words: I give the orders here. They're few. The load is taken, the walker goes free. Every load gets its stick as a receipt. We kill no walker, since his tribe would come for the camp. Walkers we've robbed return the season after.
variants_low: I give the orders. Take the load, cut the stick, let the walker go. No killing, or his tribe comes for us. He returns next season.
variants_high: I give the orders here. They are simple. Take the load. Let the walker go free with a stick as his receipt. Kill him and his tribe comes for the camp. Walkers we've robbed return the season after, so be fair with them. They pay us again.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-2
words: I smoke the hides here, over the camp's one fire. The tents sit on a bench above the track, so we see walkers round the pond long before they find us. I'm at the racks from first light, tending the smoke. A hide comes off thick, thin, cured or spoiled. I can tell which by the smell before I touch it.
variants_low: The camp is on a bench over the track. That is all a stranger needs. I have hides on the rack and no time to describe them.
variants_high: Sit, if you like. The tents are on a bench above the track. From the fire I watch walkers come round the pond. I'm the camp's seller. You are talking to the right man, so ask about hides and I will show you the best rack first.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-2
words: A dead walker brings his tribe against the camp, so we take the cargo and let him go. Cut-Rope's raiders kill on the same tracks. The settled tribes blame us for the bodies. Round the pond a crocodile lives. Death hoppers and hackwings den in the reeds. I've no reason to go near the water.
variants_low: A dead walker brings his tribe against us. So he lives. The pond has a crocodile and worse. Stay off the bank.
variants_high: I'll tell you plainly. If we kill a walker, his tribe comes against the camp. We take the load and cut the stick instead. The real trouble is Cut-Rope's raiders on the same tracks. Then there is the pond, with a crocodile, death hoppers and hackwings in the reeds. Stay on the track.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-2
words: The camp's way in is a cane gate with a totem on each side. One of the band stands among the totems there. He will stop you. Beyond the gate the walked ground goes on to the Polers' Camp, where guides pole travellers to Dead-Water Village.
variants_low: Beyond the gate the walked ground goes to the Polers' Camp. Guides there pole you to Dead-Water Village. One of the band is at the totems. Don't walk past him.
variants_high: Look for the cane gate between two totems. One of the band stands there, so stop and show your hands. Beyond us the walked ground goes on to the Polers' Camp. Guides there pole travellers to Dead-Water Village.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-2
words: We are six here. The lieutenant cuts the receipts. The five of the band share the watch, the racks and the cane gate by turns. Then we sleep in the hide tent. The settled tribes call us killers from their villages. I would like to see one of them stand a turn at my fire.
variants_low: Six live here. The band works in turns. The settled tribes tell lies about us.
variants_high: There are six of us. Heita-Kai cuts the receipts. The five of the band share the watch, the racks and the cane gate by turns. I like a buyer at my fire. The tribes in their villages will tell you we are killers. They have never stood a turn out here.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-2
words: At the gate, the walker hands over his cargo. Then he goes on his way. The lieutenant cuts a notched stick for each load and gives it to him as a receipt. My part is the hides. I smoke them over the one fire and set the best aside to sell. Thick or thin, cured or spoiled, I grade each before it goes on the rack.
variants_low: The lieutenant cuts a notched stick for every load we take. The walker carries it off as his receipt. Hides are my work. I'm busy.
variants_high: Every load we take gets a notched stick, cut by the lieutenant. The walker leaves with it as his receipt. Me, I'm the seller. I smoke the hides and set the best ones aside for a buyer who asks. Come to the fire and I'll lay out what I have.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-2
words: Five of us share the posts around the day. One stands among the totems at the gate. Another is up on the scaffold watching the bend. He whistles the moment a walker shows below. I have the fire. I smoke hides there while the rest sleep. I grade each hide as it comes off.
variants_low: Five of us. One at the gate totems, one on the bend. The one on the bend whistles at walkers. I'm at the fire.
variants_high: We are five. We share the posts. One stands among the totems at the gate. One watches the bend and whistles at the first walker. I smoke hides at the fire while the others sleep. When you want to see a rack, come by the fire.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-3
words: Long-Water Hold is a village of settled Naga. It stands deep in the marsh on firm ground. It sits on the poling route that most of the inner swamp uses. The landing is deep enough for loaded craft. The people tend a Hist and their fields. They want traffic on the road. Their tribeless kin rob that road. The two sides quarrel.
variants_low: A settled Naga village on the busy poling route. They tend a Hist. They quarrel with the kin who rob the road.
variants_high: Long-Water Hold is a village of settled Naga, deep in the marsh. The busiest poling route of the inner swamp runs by it. Its landing takes loaded craft. They tend a Hist and fields. They want caravans on the road. Their tribeless kin rob that road, so the two sides quarrel.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-3
words: Naga are Argonians, but tall ones. Many stand seven feet or more. Their wide mouths are full of needle fangs. Far from the roads, down in the marsh, that is their home. Some are brigands. Some are not. Some Argonians hate them. Not all do. I slept badly, so ask me the rest later.
variants_low: Tall adder-like Argonians with needle fangs. They live deep in the marsh. Not all are brigands.
variants_high: Naga are the tall Argonians, adder-like, with wide mouths full of fangs. They live deep in the marsh. Brigands are some of them. Hatred of them is some of the marsh, not all of it.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-3
words: Imperial surveyors began the North Cut as a road out of Stormhold, heading north to meet the Tear road. They gave up after four kilometres. No village stands on it now. Villagers dig its stone for their yards. Now it drains water onto a hamlet and two fields.
variants_low: An Imperial road, given up after four kilometres. Villagers quarry its stone. It drains onto two fields and a hamlet.
variants_high: The North Cut began as a road the Imperial surveyors drove north from Stormhold. It was meant to reach the Tear road. They quit after four kilometres. Villagers dig its stone for their yards. Now it drains water onto a hamlet and two fields.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-3
words: The Prison road is an old Imperial road. People still use its old name. They use the old name for the Border road too. Follow the Prison road and it leads to the Rose. Beside it sits the Tag House, up on a dry rise.
variants_low: An old Imperial road, still called by its old name. It leads to the Rose. The Tag House is up on a rise beside it.
variants_high: The Empire cut the Prison road long ago. People keep the old names for it and for the Border road. It leads to the Rose. The Tag House sits up on a dry rise beside it. Sleep there if the ground is wet.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-3
words: Naga with no tribe are tall adder-like Argonians. The marsh's brigands are mostly of them. A good many work the tracks when merchants are walking. Cut-Rope's raiders are one such band. They kill where we do not.
variants_low: Adder-like Argonians with no tribe. Most brigands are of them. Cut-Rope's raiders are one band.
variants_high: The tribeless are tall adder-like Argonians who belong to no tribe. The marsh's brigands mostly come from them. A good many work the tracks when merchants are walking. Cut-Rope's raiders are one band. Walk with care on their stretches.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-3
words: This is the bench over the pond where the track bends. Walkers come round the water and see reeds. We see them first. I slept two hours between watches last night. The tent fills with rack smoke. I like the place less than the rest of the band do.
variants_low: A bench over a pond. Smoke in the tent. Ask the others if you want praise for it.
variants_high: It's the bench over the pond where the track bends. Walkers see reeds. We see them. The tent is full of rack smoke, so I sleep badly here. The air by the fire is better than in my tent, if you want to sit a while.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-3
words: Kill a walker and his tribe comes up the bank after us. So we take his cargo. He keeps walking. Cut-Rope's raiders do their killing on these same tracks. The settled tribes blame us for it. A croc, hoppers and hackwings have dens round the pond. I keep out of those reeds.
variants_low: Kill a walker and his tribe comes. The pond has a croc and hoppers. Stay out of the reeds.
variants_high: A dead walker brings his tribe up the bank, so we take cargo and let him go. Cut-Rope's raiders kill along these tracks. The blame lands on us. A croc, hoppers and hackwings den round the pond. Stay on the track there, guest. They seldom come up to it.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-3
words: Our path leaves the track at the cane gate, with a totem on each side. Follow the track on and you reach the Polers' Camp. Their guides take travellers down the water by pole to Dead-Water Village. I don't know the poling. I've only heard where it ends.
variants_low: Past the gate the track goes to the Polers' Camp. Their guides pole on to Dead-Water Village.
variants_high: The cane gate between the two totems is our path. The track goes on past it to the Polers' Camp. The guides there pole travellers to Dead-Water Village. I haven't been. The way is plain enough to follow.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-3
words: Six of us live at this camp. Heita-Kai is the lieutenant who cuts the receipts. The other five are the band. We share out three posts by turns. Strangers walk down the track and can't read a body, so we feed them and watch them go. Today I slept four hours.
variants_low: Six of us. A lieutenant, five in the band. Strangers get fed and watched.
variants_high: Six live here. Heita-Kai is the lieutenant. The other five are the band, so we trade the three posts round. A stranger who can't read a body is fed first. Then he is sent on his way. Sit down and I'll tell you who has the watch.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-3
words: The lieutenant takes cargo off walkers. She cuts each one a stick for it. I take whatever turn the band gives me at the gate, the fire or the bend. The best of the smoked hides are put aside to trade. That part I don't mind.
variants_low: Cargo comes off walkers. They get a stick. I take my turn. Then I sleep.
variants_high: The lieutenant takes cargo off walkers and cuts each one a stick for it. My turns come at the gate, the fire or the bend. The best smoked hides go aside to trade. Ask me what they cost. I like a buyer.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-3
words: We work in turns. One of us stands the bend. When a walker shows below, he whistles. Another smokes hides over the fire while the rest sleep. That is the turn I like best. I had five hours before the whistle woke me today.
variants_low: The bend has a watcher who whistles when a walker shows below. Hides get smoked at the fire while the rest sleep. I sleep.
variants_high: We work in turns. A watcher stands the bend. He whistles the moment a walker shows below. Another smokes hides over the fire while the rest sleep. Take the fire turn with me some evening. I'll show you how the hides are hung.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-4
words: Long-Water Hold is a village in the deep marsh. Its Naga are settled, with a Hist and fields to tend. The ground there is firm. The chief route of the polers through the inner swamp passes it. They want the road's trade, so they quarrel with the tribeless kin who rob the road.
variants_low: A Naga village in the deep marsh. Its people are settled, with a Hist and fields. The chief route of the polers through the inner swamp passes it. They quarrel with the tribeless kin who rob the road they want for trade.
variants_high: Long-Water Hold lies deep in the marsh. A settled Naga tribe lives there on firm ground, tending a Hist and fields. The polers' chief route through the inner swamp passes its landing. Loaded craft tie up there easily. The tribe wants the road's trade, so it quarrels with the tribeless kin who rob the road.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-4
words: A Naga stands seven or eight feet tall, with a wide mouth full of needle fangs. The deep marsh is where our kind lives. Not every Naga robs on the roads. The inner swamps belong to the Naga-Kur.
variants_low: Naga are tall, seven or eight feet, with needle fangs. They live in the deep marsh. Not every Naga robs on the roads.
variants_high: A Naga stands seven or eight feet tall, with a wide mouth full of needle fangs. The deep marsh is where our kind lives. Not every Naga robs on the roads. The inner swamps belong to the Naga-Kur. The tribeless ones are the road robbers.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-4
words: The North Cut is an old Imperial road. Surveyors began it at Stormhold and drove it north toward the Tear road. They quit once four kilometres lay behind them. No residents live on it. Villagers cut stone from it to pave their yards. Its water drains down to a hamlet and two fields.
variants_low: An old Imperial road, begun at Stormhold and driven north toward the Tear road. The surveyors quit once four kilometres lay behind them. Villagers cut its stone. Water from it drains down to a hamlet and two fields.
variants_high: The North Cut is an old Imperial road. Surveyors began it at Stormhold and drove it north toward the Tear road. They quit once four kilometres lay behind them, so no residents live on it. Villagers cut stone from it to pave their yards. Its water drains down to a hamlet and two fields.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-4
words: We say ojel for an outsider, any outsider. It is a plain word with no insult in it. Lukiul is a different word. The An-Xileel coined it as a slur for Argonians hatched far from Black Marsh, because those cannot hear the Hist.
variants_low: Outsider. Plain word, no insult. Lukiul is the slur, the An-Xileel's, for Argonians hatched far from Black Marsh who cannot hear the Hist. Do not use it.
variants_high: Ojel means outsider in Jel, our tongue. It carries no insult, so take no offence from me. Lukiul is the word to avoid. The An-Xileel coined it as a slur for Argonians hatched far from Black Marsh, who cannot hear the Hist.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-4
words: Imperial work, all of it. The Prison road and the Border road are roads. The Mile House is a waystation. People use the old names still. The Prison road heads for the Rose. A Tag House stands on a dry rise next to it.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads and a waystation, still known by their old names. The Prison road heads for the Rose. A Tag House stands on a dry rise next to it.
variants_high: Imperial work, all of it. The old ones say the roads rotted the cargo. The Prison road and the Border road are roads. The Mile House is a waystation. People use the old names still. The Prison road heads for the Rose, with a Tag House on a dry rise next to it.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-4
words: Naga are an Argonian breed, tall and adder-like. Tribeless Naga belong to no tribe. Many of them rob merchants who walk the tracks. Cut-Rope's raiders make up one such band. This camp is tribeless too, but we take cargo and leave the walker breathing.
variants_low: Naga are a tall, adder-like Argonian breed. Many belong to no tribe and rob merchants on the tracks. Cut-Rope's raiders make up one such band.
variants_high: Naga are tall, an adder-like breed of Argonian. The tribeless ones belong to no tribe. Many rob merchants who walk the tracks. Cut-Rope's raiders make up one such band. If they stop you on the track, give up the load and walk away quickly.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-4
words: The camp sits on the bench above the pond, at the blind bend of the track. I sit at that bend by day and chip flint. A walker is in my sight a long while before the camp is in his.
variants_low: A camp on the bench over the pond. Look up from the track if you want to see it. Most walkers do not.
variants_high: This is the bench over the pond, the best seat on the track. From the bend I watch walkers a long while before they know we are here. Sit by the fire if you like. Mind the flint chips.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-4
words: By day, I sit at the bend and flake flint. I have found walkers dead on these tracks from there. Cut-Rope's raiders killed them. The settled tribes put the blame on the camp. The pond has a crocodile. Hackwings and death hoppers den there.
variants_low: Cut-Rope's raiders kill walkers on these tracks. The camp gets the blame. Stay off the pond bank, there are teeth in it.
variants_high: I sit at the bend by day, so I see what lies on the track. Cut-Rope's raiders leave walkers dead there and the settled tribes blame the camp. The pond has a crocodile. Hackwings and death hoppers den there too, so stay on the track.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-4
words: Take the track on past the bend until you reach the Polers' Camp. The guides there pole travellers by water to Dead-Water Village. I would sooner see you walking to them than standing at our gate.
variants_low: Along the track to the Polers' Camp. Their guides pole on to Dead-Water Village. Not through our gate.
variants_high: Go along the track to the Polers' Camp, a walk worth making. Their guides pole people on to Dead-Water Village. Leave before dark and the bend will let you pass quietly.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-4
words: Six live on this bench. Heita-Kai is the lieutenant. Jeen-Ozzu, Bux-Xeek, Okan-Leel and Im-Jei are band, as I am. Six is already as many people as I care to know.
variants_low: Six of us. Heita-Kai is the lieutenant. The rest are band.
variants_high: Six live here. Heita-Kai is the lieutenant. The four beside me in the band are Jeen-Ozzu, Bux-Xeek, Okan-Leel and Im-Jei. If you want a trade, find Bux-Xeek at the fire.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-4
words: I work flint by the fire in the evening, knapping blades for the camp. Give me one and my thumb goes to the edge before my mouth opens. A flake that bites is good. A flake that slides is waste.
variants_low: Flint, by the fire, in the evening. That is my part of the work.
variants_high: In the evening, I knap flint by the fire, blades for the camp's work. Bring me yours and my thumb will go along the edge, then I will tell you true what it is worth.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-4
words: One of the band smokes the hides at the fire while the others sleep. Flint flakes pile at my feet in the evening by the same fire. Every blade I make gets my thumb along the edge before it leaves my hand.
variants_low: One of us smokes hides at the fire while the others sleep. I flake flint.
variants_high: One of the band smokes hides at the fire while the others sleep. I work beside them with my flint, so the chips fall where the smoke is thick. Come by in the evening and I will show you a good edge.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-5
words: Long-Water Hold lies in the deep marsh. A settled Naga tribe lives there on firm ground, beside the chief poling route. Its landing takes loaded craft. The settled Naga are at odds with their tribeless kin, who work that route.
variants_low: A settled Naga tribe lives there, on firm ground by the chief poling route. The landing takes loaded craft. They are at odds with their tribeless kin.
variants_high: Long-Water Hold lies in the deep marsh. A settled Naga tribe lives there on firm ground, beside the chief poling route. Its landing takes loaded craft. The settled Naga are at odds with their tribeless kin, who work that route.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-5
words: A Naga is an Argonian built like an adder, seven or eight feet tall, with a wide mouth of needle fangs. We live in the deep marsh. Not every Naga robs a road. Some Argonians hate us. Others do not.
variants_low: Naga are tall adder-like Argonians, seven or eight feet, fanged. We live in the deep marsh. Not every Naga robs. Not every Argonian hates us.
variants_high: A Naga is an Argonian built like an adder, seven or eight feet tall, with a wide mouth of needle fangs. We live in the deep marsh. Not every Naga robs a road. Some Argonians hate us. Others will share a fire with you.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-5
words: Imperial surveyors drove a road out of Stormhold, aiming at the Tear road. After four kilometres, they quit. No residents live along it. Village crews cut stone from it for their yards. Rain runs off the cut into two fields and a hamlet.
variants_low: Surveyors drove it out of Stormhold, aiming at the Tear road. They quit at four kilometres. No residents. Village crews take its stone. Rain runs into two fields and a hamlet.
variants_high: Imperial surveyors drove a road out of Stormhold, aiming at the Tear road. After four kilometres, they quit. No residents live along it to feed you. Village crews cut stone from it for their yards. Rain runs off the cut into two fields and a hamlet.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-5
words: Imperials laid the Prison road and the Border road. They also raised the Mile House as a waystation. People still use those old names. Follow the Prison road and it leads toward the Rose. Up on a dry rise by that road sits the Tag House.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads and a waystation: the Prison road, the Border road, the Mile House. People use the old names. The Prison road leads toward the Rose. The Tag House sits up on a dry rise by it.
variants_high: Imperials laid the Prison road and the Border road. They also raised the Mile House as a waystation. People still use those old names. Follow the Prison road toward the Rose. Up on a dry rise by that road sits the Tag House. Bring dry boots.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-5
words: A Naga is an Argonian of the tall, adder-like breed. The marsh's brigands are mostly Naga with no tribe at all. Many take loads off the tracks while merchants are on them. Cut-Rope's raiders are a band of that kind.
variants_low: Naga: tall, adder-like Argonians. Most marsh brigands are tribeless Naga, tied to no tribe. Many rob the tracks. Cut-Rope's raiders are a band of that kind.
variants_high: A Naga is an Argonian of the tall, adder-like breed. The marsh's brigands are mostly Naga with no tribe at all. Many take loads off the tracks while merchants are on them. Cut-Rope's raiders are a band of that kind. We take less than they do.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-5
words: The best post in the deeps is the bend above the pond. I stand it. Raiders camp on the bench behind me. The track curves round the water below, so I see a walker before he sees one tent.
variants_low: A raiders' camp on a bench above a pond. The track curves below it. That is all.
variants_high: Stand here a while and watch the bend with me. Raiders camp on the bench behind us, above the pond. I see a walker on the track long before he sees a tent. Yesterday I picked one out at two hundred paces.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-5
words: Nothing rounds the bend before I whistle. One crocodile lairs by the pond, with death hoppers and hackwings among the reeds. We take a walker's cargo and seldom his life. A dead walker brings his tribe. Cut-Rope's raiders work the tracks here.
variants_low: Dens round the pond. Cut-Rope's raiders on the tracks. I whistle first.
variants_high: Stay out of the reeds. One crocodile lairs by the pond, with death hoppers and hackwings among the reeds. We take a walker's cargo and seldom his life. A dead walker brings his tribe up the bank. Cut-Rope's raiders work the tracks here too.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-5
words: The camp path leaves the track at the cane gate, between two totems. Go on along the track as far as the Polers' Camp. Its guides take travellers by pole to Dead-Water Village.
variants_low: Cane gate, two totems. The track runs on to the Polers' Camp. Its guides take travellers by pole to Dead-Water Village.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-5
words: Six live here. Heita-Kai is the lieutenant and cuts the receipts. Five of us take turns at the gate, at the fire and on the bend. Most outsiders cannot read body speech. We watch them, feed them and send them down the track.
variants_low: Six live here. Heita-Kai is the lieutenant. The rest of us take turns. Outsiders stare at us.
variants_high: Six live on the bench. Heita-Kai is the lieutenant and cuts the receipts. Five of us share the band. We take turns at the gate, at the fire and on the bend. I like the bend best. Most outsiders cannot read body speech, so I wave slowly.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-5
words: I watch the bend from the scaffold and whistle the moment a walker shows below. The others take his cargo and wave him down the track. The lieutenant cuts a notched stick for the load. He leaves with it as a receipt.
variants_low: I whistle at the bend. The lieutenant cuts the sticks. Ask her about the rest.
variants_high: I watch the bend from the scaffold and whistle the moment a walker shows below. The others lift his cargo and wave him down the track. Bux-Xeek smokes hides at the fire and sets the best aside for trade, if you want to buy.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2-5
words: Our work goes by turns. The camp is always watched. One of us stands at the totems by the gate. I take the bend and whistle the moment a walker shows below. A fourth smokes hides over the fire while the rest sleep.
variants_low: Our work goes by turns. I have the bend. Ask the others about the rest.
variants_high: Our work goes by turns. The camp is always watched. One of us stands at the gate totems. I take the bend, the best post of the five. I whistle the moment a walker shows below. A fourth smokes hides over the fire while the rest sleep.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2
words: Long-Water Hold belongs to a settled Naga tribe. Their village is deep in the marsh on firm ground, right on the chief poling route through the inner swamp. Loaded craft can tie up at their landing. They keep a Hist, fields and villages. The road trade is what they're after. They quarrel with us, their kin without a tribe, for robbing that road.
variants_low: Long-Water Hold is a settled tribe's village on the main poling route. They quarrel with us.
variants_high: Long-Water Hold belongs to a settled Naga tribe. Their village sits on firm ground on the chief poling route through the inner swamp. Loaded craft can tie up at their landing. They keep a Hist, fields and villages. The road trade is what they're after. They quarrel with us over it.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2
words: We're Naga. A grown one stands seven feet or eight, long in the body like an adder, with needle teeth in a wide mouth. Our people keep to the deep marsh. Not all of us rob. The settled tribes farm and tend their Hist. They still blame us for every body on the track.
variants_low: Naga are tall and have fangs. Most live in the deep marsh. Not all of us rob.
variants_high: Naga stand seven feet or eight, long like an adder, with needle teeth. We keep to the deep marsh. Not all of us rob. I'll say that to anyone who sits by our fire.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2
words: Imperial surveyors started the North Cut at Stormhold, heading north for the Tear road. They quit at the four-kilometre mark. It has no residents. Villagers cut stone from it for their yards. The cut drains off into two fields and a hamlet.
variants_low: The North Cut is a road the Empire dropped after four kilometres. Villagers cut stone from it.
variants_high: Imperial surveyors started the North Cut at Stormhold, heading north for the Tear road. They quit at the four-kilometre mark. It has no residents. Villagers cut stone from it for their yards. It drains off into two fields and a hamlet.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2
words: The Empire laid the Prison road and the Border road. The Mile House is a waystation on them. They're old now. Folk here keep using the Imperial names. The Prison road heads for the Rose, with the Tag House on a dry rise beside it.
variants_low: The Prison road is an old Imperial road. It heads for the Rose. The Tag House is beside it.
variants_high: The Empire laid the Prison road and the Border road. The Mile House is a waystation on them. They're old now. Folk here keep using the Imperial names. The Prison road heads for the Rose, with the Tag House on a dry rise beside it. Walk it by day, guest.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2
words: I'm tribeless, like the rest of the band. A tribeless Naga belongs to no tribe. Naga are the tall adder-bodied Argonians. Most brigands in the marsh come from our number. Plenty work the tracks when merchants are walking them. Cut-Rope's raiders are one such band. They kill walkers where we only take cargo.
variants_low: Tribeless Naga have no tribe. Most brigands are our kind. Cut-Rope is a band of them.
variants_high: We're tribeless Naga, the tall adder-bodied Argonians with no tribe. Most brigands in the marsh come from our number. Plenty work the tracks when merchants walk them. Cut-Rope's raiders are one band of us. We cut a stick. They cut a throat.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2
words: I keep the gate for the camp. That's the cane gate between the two totems, where our path leaves the track. The tents sit up on a bench over the track, with the pond below. I tell the totems what comes round that pond. They've never missed a walker yet.
variants_low: The tents are up on the bench over the track. Go and look. I've a gate to hold.
variants_high: I'm glad of a face I know. Our tents sit on a bench above the track, with the pond below. Walkers come into view before they see us. Come round the pond by daylight. I'll tell the totems you're friendly.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2
words: We take cargo and let the walker go. A dead walker brings his tribe down on the camp. Cut-Rope's raiders rob those tracks too. The settled tribes blame us for their dead. The pond has dens of death hoppers, hackwings and one crocodile. They're a nuisance to us.
variants_low: Keep to the track. A dead walker brings his tribe. Cut-Rope kills on it. The pond has dens.
variants_high: We take cargo and let the walker go. If he dies, his tribe marches on us. Cut-Rope's raiders kill on the same tracks. The settled tribes blame us for it. Keep clear of the pond edge. Hoppers, hackwings and a crocodile have dens there.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2
words: I'm the one at the totems, so you'll meet me first. Our path leaves the track at the cane gate. If you're not coming up, keep to the track past the pond. It carries you to the Polers' Camp. The guides there pole walkers on to Dead-Water Village.
variants_low: The track goes on past the gate. Follow it. I'm at the totems.
variants_high: I stand at the totems by the cane gate, where our path leaves the track. Walk on past the pond. The track brings you to the Polers' Camp. The guides there pole walkers on to Dead-Water Village. Go in daylight, guest.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2
words: Six of us live here. Heita-Kai is the lieutenant. The band passes the posts round in turns. Mine come at dusk and in the dark. Okan-Leel stands the dark with me. Strangers shout at the gate and can't read a raised hand. I feed them and send them down the track.
variants_low: Six of us live here. The band works in turns. I don't talk about walkers.
variants_high: Six of us live here under Heita-Kai, the lieutenant. The band passes the posts round in turns. Okan-Leel stands the dark with me. Walkers who sit quiet at the gate get fed and sent off kindly. I'll feed you if you wait.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2
words: I stand the gate while the band lifts cargo off walkers. The lieutenant cuts a notched stick for every load. The walker carries it away as his receipt. I keep the gate at night. From there I've watched good loads walk past stretches of track we don't work. The lieutenant gives no reason.
variants_low: Loads come off walkers, each with a stick. That's all you need. The stretches we leave idle are my business.
variants_high: Come by the gate in daylight. I'll show you a stick. The lieutenant cuts one notched stick for every load the band lifts. The walker takes it away as his receipt. At night, I watch good loads pass stretches we leave idle. I'd work every one of them.

speaker: npc.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-north.n2
words: I'm one of the band, five of us under Heita-Kai. We take turns. The camp always has a watcher. My turns are at the totems on the gate, where I give them the news of the track. They've never argued back. I like that in a listener.
variants_low: The band works in turns. I'm at the totems. Leave me be.
variants_high: Five of us make the band under Heita-Kai. We take turns. The camp always has a watcher. I stand at the totems on the gate. I'd sooner be there than anywhere. Come up in the evening. I'll tell them you're welcome.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-2
words: Alten Corimont? A river port, eastern Shadowfen. Argonian pirates and smugglers run it, taking no side. Any crew can tie up. The gangs are hired off its docks.
variants_low: A river port, eastern Shadowfen. Pirates and smugglers run it, taking no side. Gangs are hired off its docks.
variants_high: A river port, eastern Shadowfen. Argonian pirates and smugglers run it, taking no side. Any crew can tie up. Gangs are hired off its docks. Ask for the harbour.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-2
words: A dredging gang's families live in this camp, on the dry slope below the Border road. The hatching shed stands on the top terrace, the clutch inside it.
variants_low: A camp for a dredging gang's families below the Border road. The clutch is in the hatching shed on the top terrace. Leave it be.
variants_high: A dredging gang's families live in this camp, on the dry slope below the Border road. The hatching shed stands on the top terrace. Leave a cup of water at its door.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-2
words: Imperial work, all of it: Prison road, Border road, Mile House waystation. The old names stuck. Toward the Rose goes the Prison road, the Tag House on a dry rise beside it.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads and a waystation: Prison, Border, Mile House. The names are old. Toward the Rose goes the Prison road. The Tag House sits on a dry rise by it.
variants_high: Imperial work, all of it: Prison road, Border road, Mile House waystation. The old names stuck. Toward the Rose goes the Prison road, the Tag House on a dry rise beside it. Mind the mud.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-2
words: A dredging gang's families sleep here, on a dry slope below the Border road. I cook here, I haul water here, I say the shed names here.
variants_low: A dredging gang's families sleep here, on the slope below the Border road. That is all there is to see.
variants_high: A dredging gang's families sleep here, on a dry slope below the Border road. Come to the east shed at dusk, walker. A pot is on the fire.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-2
words: Gar and slugs stay in the shallows. The danger is the debt. Food goes onto it, sickness goes onto it, a snapped spade goes onto it.
variants_low: Nothing on the slope. The debt is the danger. Meals go onto it, fever goes onto it, broken tools go onto it.
variants_high: Gar and slugs stay in the shallows, so wade there only by day. The danger is the debt. A meal goes onto it, a fever, a snapped spade.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-2
words: Up past the shed door is the Border road. Down the stair is the water. Out the gang walk is Alten Corimont. The west roots are a climb.
variants_low: Up is the road. Down is the water. Pick one.
variants_high: Up past the shed door is the Border road. Down the stair is the water. The gang walk goes to Alten Corimont. Go slowly on the stair with a pack, walker.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-2
words: The roll is the list of hands who owe the house. Every family here has a name on it. I know each by the hand on the roll.
variants_low: The roll lists the hands who owe the house. Every family here has a name on it. Ask no further.
variants_high: The roll is the list of hands who owe the house. Argonian families and Khajiit families, all of us have a name on it. Sal-Sei tends the shed.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-2
words: The gang digs the channel from the barge, down the stair. The roll is read aboard it. Up here no name is called. We cook, we haul water.
variants_low: Down on the barge, the roll is read there. Never up here. Ask the overseers about the rest.
variants_high: The roll is read out on the barge, so we hear no name up here. If you walk down to the pier, mind the planks. They are wet before dawn.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-2
words: Hands who owe House Dres dredge the channel off the barge. Once the shift ends, they sleep on land with the family. I say the shed names then.
variants_low: A hand dredges the channel off the barge. He sleeps on land with the family. That is the work.
variants_high: Hands who owe House Dres dredge the channel off the barge. At night, they sleep on land with the family. Come by the east shed after a shift and you will hear the names.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-3
words: Alten Corimont is a port on a river in the east of Shadowfen, where a waterway goes out to the sea. Pirates and smugglers of our people run it. They stay out of every war, so any crew ties up at its docks. The channel gangs are hired there.
variants_low: Alten Corimont is the port downriver. Argonian smugglers run it. It takes no side.
variants_high: Alten Corimont stands on a river in the east of Shadowfen, on a waterway that goes out to the sea. Argonian pirates and smugglers run it. They stay out of every war, so any crew ties up at its docks. The channel gangs are hired there.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-3
words: The gang's families sleep on firm ground with the marsh below and the Border road above. The camp is forty years old. Only the top terrace stays dry, so the hatching shed stands there. The clutch lies in it. That is why the families stay.
variants_low: Gang Ground is the camp of the gang's families. The clutch is in the shed at the top.
variants_high: The gang's families sleep on firm ground with the marsh below and the Border road above. The camp is forty years old. Only the top terrace stays dry, so the hatching shed stands there. The clutch lies in it. The families stay for the eggs.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-3
words: The Empire built the Border road above us, the Prison road and the Mile House waystation. People still use the old names. The Prison road heads for the Rose. The Tag House sits on a dry rise beside it.
variants_low: The Border road and the Prison road are old Imperial roads. I have not walked the second.
variants_high: The Empire built the Border road above us, the Prison road and the Mile House waystation. People still use the old names. The Prison road heads for the Rose. The Tag House sits on a dry rise beside it. I know only the Border road.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-3
words: The roll is the gang's list of those who owe. Talk at the fire is that more grown ones go downriver on it every year. Its names are called on the barge. I don't know where downriver ends.
variants_low: Talk is that more grown ones go downriver every year. I know nothing else.
variants_high: Talk at the fire says more of the grown ones go downriver every year. The roll is the list of the gang's debtors. It is called aboard the barge only. Deesh-Duun mends nets at the shed corner and hears the rest.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-3
words: The gang's families sleep on this slope. At the top, the clutch lies in the hatching shed, with the Border road just above it. I sleep in the west shed wearing my boots. The road is a short climb up the bank.
variants_low: Gang families sleep here. The clutch lies in the hatching shed at the top. I have nothing more for a walker.
variants_high: The gang's families sleep on this slope. At the top, the clutch lies in the hatching shed, kept warm all night. The cookfire below it is the best place to sit. The Border road is above for a walker who needs it.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-3
words: Slugs and gar stay in the shallows. The debt is the danger. I have seen a bowl of fish go onto it, then a fever, then a cracked haft. I sleep with my boots on and the Border road above me.
variants_low: Gar and slugs stay in the water. The debt is the danger. Food, fever, broken tools: all of it is added.
variants_high: Gar and slugs stay in the shallows, so the slope is safe to walk. The debt is what bites. A bowl of fish, a fever and a cracked haft all went onto one sum in the west shed this season.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-3
words: Up from the shed door is the Border road. Down the terraces are the landing dock and the pier of the barge. That way ends at the barge. For Alten Corimont, cross the boardwalk, take the Border road, then two tracks, a few minutes each.
variants_low: Up is the Border road. Down is the dock.
variants_high: Up from the shed door is the Border road. Down the terraces are the landing dock and the pier of the barge. Alten Corimont is the port, a few minutes to each turning: boardwalk, road, then two tracks. The roots on the west bank climb out too.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-3
words: Argonian and Khajiit families live here, each with a hand on the roll. Two overseers write their debts for the house, in the hut by the cookfire. I sit at the fire and see the doors they walk past.
variants_low: Argonian and Khajiit families live here. Two overseers write the debts. I have no more to say of them.
variants_high: Argonian and Khajiit families live here, cooking side by side. Two overseers write the debts for the house. Tsanji carries water past their door, if a walker wants a face to ask.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-3
words: The gang dredges the port channel off the barge that lies under the camp. The roll is called on the barge deck. Up here no name is heard. We learn who stood in the line when they climb the stair at dusk.
variants_low: The gang dredges off the barge. The roll is called there. I don't hear it from here.
variants_high: The gang dredges the port channel from the barge under us. The roll is called on its deck, so the camp learns the names at dusk from the hands. Come to the fire then and watch who climbs the stair.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-3
words: A hand digs silt out of the channel from the barge all day, then sleeps on land with his family. The house adds his food to the debt. It adds his fever and any tool he breaks.
variants_low: A hand digs all day and sleeps on land with his family. Food, sickness, broken tools: all of it goes to the debt.
variants_high: A hand digs from the barge, then sleeps on land with his family at the fire. The house adds his food to the debt, then his fever, then any tool he breaks. Dives-Without-A-Rope says the families' names in order after each shift.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-4
words: A river port in the east of Shadowfen, where the waterway runs down to the sea. Argonian smugglers and pirates run the docks. They'll sell to any crew and won't pick a side in a quarrel. The gangs who dredge the lower channel are hired through those same docks.
variants_low: A pirate port on the river to the sea. Smugglers run the docks. Dredging gangs are hired there.
variants_high: Friend, it's a river port in the east of Shadowfen, where the waterway runs down to the sea. Argonian smugglers and pirates run the docks. They'll sell to any crew and won't pick a side in a quarrel. The dredging gangs of the lower channel are hired through those docks.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-4
words: The camp stands on firm earth where the Border road ends and the marsh starts. Forty years it has been there, with a dredging gang's families in it. The highest terrace is dry, so they built a hatching shed there. The gang's eggs lie in it. The families stay for those eggs.
variants_low: A dredging gang's camp, forty years old, on firm earth. The eggs in the hatching shed keep the families here.
variants_high: Friend, the camp stands on firm earth where the Border road ends and the marsh starts. It's forty years old, with a dredging gang's families in it. The highest terrace is dry enough for a hatching shed, so the gang's eggs lie there. They are why the families stay.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-4
words: The Border road passes over our roofs. Another road heads to the Rose. Ri'Sakka has seen the Tag House by that road, on higher ground. The Mile House is a waystation. All three are old Imperial work. People still call them by the old names.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads and a waystation. We use the old names still.
variants_high: The Border road passes over our roofs, friend. Another road runs toward the Rose, with the Tag House by it on higher ground. The Mile House is a waystation. All three are old Imperial work. People call them by the old names still.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-4
words: It's the camp where the dredging gang's families live. Ri'Sakka patches the sleeping mats here, with reed from the store, so he knows every shed from the inside. The warmest roof is the hatching shed, up on the highest terrace. The gang's clutch lies there.
variants_low: A camp for the gang's families. The clutch is in the hatching shed up top. Ri'Sakka has mats to patch.
variants_high: It's the camp where the dredging gang's families live, friend. Ri'Sakka patches the sleeping mats here, with reed from the store, so he can find you a dry corner. The warmest roof is the hatching shed, up on the highest terrace, where the gang's clutch lies.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-4
words: Little hunts the slope. Gar and slugs stay in the shallows. Torchbugs drift over the reeds, so a mat-patcher sleeps easy. The debt is what bites. Food, sickness and broken tools are all added to it, faster than the gang can work it off.
variants_low: Gar in the shallows, torchbugs in the reeds. The debt is worse. Food, fever and broken tools go on it.
variants_high: Little hunts the slope, friend. Gar and slugs stay in the shallows, torchbugs drift over the reeds. The debt is what bites. Food, sickness and broken tools are all added to it, faster than the gang can work it off.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-4
words: Up past the hatching shed door is the Border road. Down the stair is the landing, with the barge pier beside it. For Alten Corimont, cross the boardwalk south-west, then the Border road north, then the tracks east and south, a few minutes at each turn. The west bank roots are a hard climb with a pack.
variants_low: Up is the road. Down the stair is the pier. Alten Corimont is the boardwalk south-west, then road and tracks.
variants_high: Up past the hatching shed door is the Border road, friend. Down the stair is the landing, with the barge pier beside it. For Alten Corimont, cross the boardwalk south-west, then the Border road north, then the tracks east and south. A few minutes at each turn.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-4
words: Argonian families and Khajiit families share the terraces. The clutch-keeper minds the shed. Two overseers write the debts. The roll is the list of hands who owe the house, with a family behind each name. The shed families count Ri'Sakka a hand, not kin. He patches their mats all the same.
variants_low: Argonians and Khajiit, two overseers, a clutch-keeper. The roll is the list of hands who owe the house. Ri'Sakka patches mats.
variants_high: Argonian families and Khajiit families share the terraces, friend. The clutch-keeper minds the shed. Two overseers write the debts. The roll is the list of hands who owe the house, with a family behind each name. Ri'Sakka patches mats for all of them, kin or hand.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-4
words: The gang works the port channel from the barge, down at the pier. The roll is read there before each shift, every name and what he owes. It is not read up in the camp. The families get it secondhand from whoever walks back, while I patch their mats.
variants_low: The gang dredges from the barge. The roll is read there, not here. Ask the hands.
variants_high: The gang works the port channel from the barge, down at the pier. The roll gets read there before each shift. The families up here only hear it secondhand from whoever walks back, friend. Ri'Sakka patches the mats while they wait.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-4
words: I patch mats for the hands who do it, so I see them come in at dusk. Dredging is wet, heavy work. The house writes the meals against a hand, then the fevers, then every spade that cracks in the silt. A hand can work the whole season and owe more at the end of it.
variants_low: Wet, heavy work, dredging. The house adds the meals, the fevers and the broken spades to what a hand owes.
variants_high: I patch mats for the hands who do it, friend, so I see them come in at dusk. Dredging is wet, heavy work. The house writes the meals against a hand, then the fevers, then every cracked spade. A hand can work the whole season and owe more at the end.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-5
words: Alten Corimont is a port on a river in eastern Shadowfen. Argonian pirates and smugglers run it. It takes no side in a war. Any crew may tie up there. The gangs that dredge the lower channel are hired from its docks. Bring coin.
variants_low: A river port in eastern Shadowfen. Pirates run it. Bring coin.
variants_high: Alten Corimont is a port on a river in eastern Shadowfen. Argonian pirates and smugglers run it. It takes no side in a war, so any crew may tie up. The gangs that dredge the lower channel are hired from its docks. Khajiit hulls put in there as well.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-5
words: A dredging gang's families live in the camp. It is forty years old. It stands on firm ground, with the Border road above and the marsh below. On the dry top terrace, a hatching shed holds the clutch. The families stay for the eggs.
variants_low: A dredging gang's families live here. The clutch is in the shed on the top terrace.
variants_high: It is the camp of a dredging gang's families. The top terrace is dry, so the hatching shed stands there with the clutch inside. This one carries water up to that door each morning. The Border road is above and the marsh is below.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-5
words: Two old Imperial roads are the Prison road and the Border road. The Mile House is a waystation from the same time. Folk still use the old names. The Tag House stands on a dry rise beside the Prison road.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads. The Tag House stands by the Prison road.
variants_high: Two old Imperial roads are the Prison road and the Border road. The Mile House is a waystation from the same time. Folk still use the old names. The Tag House stands on a dry rise beside the Prison road. The Prison road runs toward the Rose.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-5
words: Gang Ground is where the dredging gang's families live. The camp sits on firm ground, with the Border road above it and the marsh below. This one carries water up the slope each morning. A full jar is a long climb.
variants_low: It is the gang's camp, on firm ground under the Border road. This one has a jar to carry.
variants_high: Gang Ground is where the dredging gang's families live, on a slope of firm ground below the Border road. Come up to the cookfire, walker. This one will find you a cup of water.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-5
words: Little hunts this slope. The slugs and gar stay in the shallows. The torchbugs stay in the reeds. The climb with a full jar is the hard part. The overseers' ledger bites harder than any gar.
variants_low: Not much. Slugs and gar stay in the water. Walk the slope and you will be fine.
variants_high: Stay on the terraces and the paths, walker. You will meet nothing worse than a torchbug. The slugs and gar stay in the shallows and the torchbugs in the reeds.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-5
words: From the hatching shed, a way climbs to the Border road. Another goes down the slope to the landing and the pier. Alten Corimont is four short stretches of a few minutes each, starting with the boardwalk south-west.
variants_low: Up from the shed is the Border road. Down is the landing and the pier.
variants_high: Up from the hatching shed you reach the Border road. Down the stair are the landing and the pier by the barge. Alten Corimont is four short stretches of a few minutes each, starting with the boardwalk south-west. This one can point you at the boardwalk.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-5
words: Families of the hands live here, Argonian and Khajiit. Sal-Sei tends the clutch in the warm shed. Llarvi Maryon and Nesh-Neel are the two overseers who write up the gang's debts. The House adds to them faster than the gang can dig.
variants_low: Families, Argonian and Khajiit. Sal-Sei tends the shed. Two overseers write up the debts.
variants_high: Argonian and Khajiit families share the camp. This one is glad of the company. Sal-Sei tends the warm shed. Llarvi Maryon and Nesh-Neel are the two overseers who write up the gang's debts. Nesh-Neel walks the yard at dusk.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-5
words: The gang digs out the port channel. They go aboard the barge at the foot of the slope. The roll is read on that barge, not in the camp, so the names stay down there. This one stays up here with the water jars.
variants_low: The roll is read on the barge, not up here. The channel is the gang's work. Mine is the water.
variants_high: The gang digs the port channel off the barge down at the pier. At the start of a shift, they hear the roll read on the barge, not up at the camp. The pier is a short way down if you want to see it.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1-5
words: Hands in a gang are in debt to House Dres. They dig the channel to work it off. The House adds to the sum faster than they dig. This one carries water up for the families while the hands are away.
variants_low: The hands owe House Dres. They dig to work it off. That is all this one will say.
variants_high: Hands in a gang are in debt to House Dres. They dig the channel to work it off. The House adds to the sum faster than they dig. This one carries water up for the families. A full jar is always welcome.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1
words: Alten Corimont lies on a waterway in eastern Shadowfen, a port for river boats. Argonian pirates and smugglers run it. It sides with no war, so any crew may tie up. Gangs like ours are hired from its docks.
variants_low: River port in eastern Shadowfen. Argonian pirates and smugglers run it. It sides with no war. Gangs get hired at its docks. I do not go.
variants_high: Alten Corimont is a river port in eastern Shadowfen. Argonian pirates and smugglers run it. It sides with no war, so any crew may tie up. Dredging gangs are hired at its docks. Ask there.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1
words: A dredging gang's families live in Gang Ground, on firm earth under the Border road with the marsh at the foot. The clutch lies in the warm shed on the top terrace. That keeps the families here.
variants_low: Camp of a dredging gang's families. Firm earth under the Border road, marsh at the foot. The clutch is in the top shed. Leave the fire be.
variants_high: Gang Ground is a dredging gang's camp, on firm earth under the Border road with the marsh at the foot. The clutch lies in the warm top shed. Stand at the door and hear it hum.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1
words: The Empire laid the Prison road and the Mile House waystation, with the Border road too. Folk keep the old names. The Prison road heads for the Rose. A dry rise beside it holds the Tag House.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads and a waystation, the Mile House. Folk keep the old names. Prison road heads for the Rose. Tag House sits on a rise by it.
variants_high: The Empire laid the Prison road, the Mile House waystation and the Border road. Folk keep the old names. The Prison road heads for the Rose, with the Tag House on a dry rise by it.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1
words: A dredging gang's families sleep here. Firm ground, with the Border road above and the marsh below. Poor camp, kept clean. I carry fish heads up to the shed.
variants_low: Families of a dredging gang sleep here. Border road above, marsh below, firm ground in the middle. Nothing to see. Fish heads wait on me.
variants_high: A dredging gang's families sleep here. Firm ground, Border road above, marsh below. The paths are swept, the thatch mended. Warm yourself at the cookfire.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n1

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n3-2
words: The gang dredges the port channel, working off the barge down at the water. The roll gets read out on the deck before a shift. It isn't read up here, because I won't have names said over the families' cooking pots. The channel work does wear a debt down in time.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.n3
words: Little hunts the slope. By my tally, the shallows hold six torchbugs, three gar and two slugs. They stay down there. The real cost up here is a broken tool. Every snapped spade or hoe goes on the debt. Then the debt grows with it.

words: The talk at my nets is that the roll sends more grown hands downriver every year. It lists the gang's debtors. Its names are called aboard the barge, never up in the camp. speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.npc-opening-witness
words: I mend nets at the corner of the west shed, where every family walks past me. Up the slope, on the top terrace, stands the hatching shed with the eggs in it. words: Not much hunts the slope. I've sat here long enough to say so. Slugs and gar keep to the shallows. Torchbugs hang over the reeds. None of them has torn a net of mine. What bites is the book. Every broken tool is written against the gang. The house adds faster than the hands can dredge.

words: From the hatching shed you go up to the Border road. Going down, take the stair to the landing, with the barge pier beside it. If you want Alten Corimont, take the gang walk. speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.npc-opening-witness
words: Argonian families live here. Khajiit families do too. Each has a hand on the roll. Tsanji's people carry the water up. The family with Ties-The-Loose-Plank on the roll saves the fish heads. words: The hands go down to the barge when every shift begins and dredge the port channel. I never go aboard. My work is netting, which is small beside theirs. speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.opening-work-camp.npc-opening-witness
words: I know each family in this camp and every name on the roll. The roll is the house's list of the hands that owe it. Its names are called aboard the barge and nowhere in the camp. speaker: npc.saxhleel-coast.pearl-lots.n1-2
words: The Counted Lots are the pearl beds off this spit, each a numbered stretch of seabed. Diver families have a lot from their parents by inheritance. Pay is best on the deep lots. They kill divers too. The tally book takes the pay. The deaths go into it as well. Small shells, middling shells, good shells: I grade them all.
variants_low: Pearl beds off the spit, numbered, held by diver families. Deep lots kill divers.

speaker: npc.saxhleel-coast.pearl-lots.n1-2
words: Every lot out there is a numbered stretch of seabed with a buoy over it. I grade what the divers bring up, here on the spit, into baskets by size. Size sets the price in Archon.
variants_low: Numbered lots, buoys over each. Mind the baskets, I grade the catch here.

speaker: npc.saxhleel-coast.pearl-lots.n1-2
words: The deep lots pay best. They kill divers too. Jellies drift over the beds, so watch the water around the buoys before you step off the spit.

words: It's a halt in a sheltered cove, so boats off the sea put in here to get out of the swell. I gather herbs along the shore and sort the bundles by smell, the sharp ones from the sweet. I love this place, the plank walk and the piles and the wet-reed smell that gets into everything I carry.

words: Archon, the province's legal harbour, is the port in the east. The marsh runs up behind the city, with beaches to the south. Families of pilots steer the ships through the estuary. Past the headland, the harbour authority has no say. I only know it from crews who sail past.
variants_low: Archon's the eastern port, the legal harbour. Marsh behind it, beaches south. Pilot families steer the ships. The authority stops at the headland.
variants_high: Archon, the province's legal harbour, is the port in the east. The marsh runs up behind the city, with beaches to the south. Families of pilots steer the ships through the estuary. Past the headland, the harbour authority has no say. Ask a crew just in off the Padomaic run, because they've seen it.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n2
words: The Empire built the Prison road and the Border road. It put the Mile House on them as a waystation. Folk go on using the old names, though the Empire is gone. The old ones say the cargo rotted on those roads. The Prison road heads toward the Rose. Beside it, up on a dry rise, stands the Tag House.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads and a waystation. Folk still use the old names. The Prison road heads toward the Rose. The Tag House stands by it.
variants_high: The Empire built the Prison road and the Border road. It put the Mile House on them as a waystation. Folk go on using the old names. The Prison road heads toward the Rose. Beside it, on a dry rise, stands the Tag House. Take a dry day for it.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n2
words: Riverwalk is a stop where boats shelter in a cove off the sea. Nothing grows here, so every meal comes in off the boats. The village feeds each crew and gives them a bunk. The ferry stage is out on the islet. You walk the planks from the shore houses to reach it.
variants_low: A stop in a cove. Nothing grows here. Follow the planks to the stage.
variants_high: Riverwalk is a stop where boats shelter in a cove off the sea. Nothing grows here, so the meals come off the boats. We feed each crew and give them a bunk. Walk the planks from the shore houses to the ferry stage. I'll show you the raft.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n2
words: The Dunmer town of Tear sits on flat land by the coast, north of where the saltrice grows. The Tear road brings you there from Thorn. The slave trade of House Dres worked out of Tear for centuries.
variants_low: Tear's a Dunmer town on the border. The Tear road reaches it from Thorn. House Dres traded slaves from there.
variants_high: The Dunmer town of Tear sits on flat land by the coast, north of where the saltrice grows. The Tear road brings you there from Thorn. The slave trade of House Dres worked out of Tear for centuries. Keep your papers close if you go.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n2
words: Thorn is the border city, up at the north end of the fields where the saltrice grows. A road called the Tear road leaves it for Morrowind. House Dres raided Thorn for slaves and grew rich on its rice. Now the Thorn Ash-Reed Accord quarrels over whose title to the fields is good. Its agents wade out to our spit to shout about the toll.
variants_low: Thorn is a border city in the north, among the saltrice fields. The Tear road leads out of it. House Dres raided it for slaves. Its Accord argues over title to the fields.
variants_high: Thorn is the border city, up at the north end of the fields where the saltrice grows. A road called the Tear road leaves it for Morrowind. House Dres raided Thorn for slaves and grew rich on its rice. Today the Thorn Ash-Reed Accord quarrels over whose title to the fields is good. Walk there if you want to hear it.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n2
words: I pole the raft that carries loads out to the stage, so I know this water better than most. Riverwalk is a stop for boats, set in a sheltered cove off the sea. The swell never finds them here. The boards over the water are all different ages. I hum my way across them.
variants_low: Riverwalk is a stop for boats in a cove. The planks will show you the rest.
variants_high: Riverwalk is a stop for boats in a good cove. Sit on the stage when the water goes flat at dusk and watch the boats come. Ask Deesh-Ra for a bowl first. She likes a stranger fed.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n2
words: The water itself won't hurt you. Silt will. Every morning before the first boat, one of us pushes a pole into the mud along the way across the cove to feel how near the bottom has come. Some mornings it's me. If the cove keeps filling, the boats will tie up on another shore.
variants_low: Water's safe. Silt isn't. Mind where you step off the boards.
variants_high: The water is safe, truly. Silt is what worries us. If you want to see it sounded, come down to the boards before the first boat and I'll let you push the pole.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n2
words: The Tear road leaves the village westward. Thorn is a short walk along it. Past Thorn it carries on into Morrowind. For Hissmir you want a canoe from the ferry stage on the islet. I pole the raft there but I don't pole canoes.
variants_low: Thorn's west along the Tear road. The road goes on into Morrowind. Hissmir's by canoe from the stage.
variants_high: Thorn is west, a short walk along the Tear road. The road goes on past it into Morrowind. For Hissmir, take a canoe from the islet stage. Pay Deesh-Ra there and eat before you go, because she'll insist.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n2
words: The herb family has the long house, the big plank one standing in the shallows. My crew takes bunks at the crews' house, back on the spit. Lifts-Two-Traps runs the toll post with Reaches-The-Shore-Last and Runs-The-Line-Out beside him. Strangers get fed and watched here, then sent on their way.
variants_low: Herb family in the long house, crews at the crews' house, toll people at the post. Keep clear of the toll people.
variants_high: The herb family has the long house. They feed you well. My crew takes bunks at the crews' house on the spit. Lifts-Two-Traps runs the toll post. Greet Deesh-Ra at the stage shelter first, because she likes to know who has eaten.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n2
words: A toll is charged on every boat that goes into the pilgrim water, the channel up to Hissmir. My crew poles the raft through it each crossing. The toll comes out of our share. Thorn's field-owners and Hissmir's stewards both say the coin is theirs. This morning I watched the toll-holder write our raft on his slate again.
variants_low: There's a toll on boats entering the pilgrim water. It comes out of the crew's share. Pay it at the post on the spit.
variants_high: A toll is charged on every boat that enters the pilgrim water. It comes out of our share. If you are bound that way, pay the toll-holder on the spit first. It saves you a quarrel at the stage.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n2
words: Poling is honest work when all three of us hold one pace. We push the raft along the channel and load her at the stage as we go. The village gives every crew a meal and a bunk. I'll grant that's a fair bargain.
variants_low: We pole and load the boat along the channel. The village gives us a meal and a bunk.
variants_high: Poling and loading the boat along the channel is the whole job. Learn the grip on the pole and you'll eat well here. The village gives every crew a meal and a bunk.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n3-2
words: Archon is the province's legal harbour, a port in the east. Marsh lies to its north and beaches to its south. Pilot families guide ships in through the estuary. The harbour's authority ends at the headland.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n3-2
words: The Prison road and the Border road are old Imperial roads. The Mile House is an old waystation on them. Folk use the Imperial names still. The Prison road heads toward the Rose. On a dry rise by its side stands the Tag House.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n3-2
words: Riverwalk is where boats halt in a sheltered cove of the sea, east of Thorn. Nothing grows here, so we buy food off the boats. Each boat's hands get a meal and a bunk. Planks lead out to the ferry stage.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n3-2
words: Tear is a Dunmer town on the border plain, north of the saltrice fields. The Tear road brings you to it from Thorn. For centuries, the slave trade of House Dres was run out of there.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n3-2
