words: Thorn sits on the northern border, where the saltrice grows. The Tear road starts there and runs into Morrowind. Dres raiders once took slaves from it. These days the Accord, a body of the town, argues over who owns the fields.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n3-2
words: I work the toll post at the shore end. This cove is the one still water on the coast, so the boats come to us. At dusk, I lift the box and its weight tells me how the day went.
variants_low: The toll post, at the shore end. Pay there if you land.
variants_high: I work the toll post at the shore end. Come at dusk and I'll show you the box. This cove is the one still water on the coast, so the boats all come.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n3-2
words: The water is safe. Silt is the worry. A pole sounds the way across before the first boat, every morning. If the cove fills, boats go elsewhere and my box goes light.
variants_low: Silt. Mind the boards.
variants_high: The water is safe. Silt is the worry. A pole sounds the way across before the first boat, every morning. Walk the middle of the boards, the edges are soft.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n3-2
words: Up the Tear road is Thorn, a short walk. Past Thorn the road runs on into Morrowind. For Hissmir or Murkwater, pay at the shelter on the islet.
variants_low: Thorn, up the Tear road. Water, the islet.
variants_high: Up the Tear road is Thorn, a short walk. Past Thorn the road runs on into Morrowind. For Hissmir or Murkwater, pay at the shelter on the islet. Fares are fairer before noon.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n3-2
words: Herb-gatherers live in the long house. Boat hands sleep in the plank house on the spit. At the post, it is the toll-holder, Reaches-The-Shore-Last and me.
variants_low: Herb-gatherers, boat hands, the post. Ask no more.
variants_high: Herb-gatherers live in the long house. Boat hands sleep in the plank house on the spit. The post has three of us. Hungry? Eat at the long house table first.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n3-2
words: At my post, I take the toll from each master whose boat enters the pilgrim water. At dusk, I carry the box up from the spit. A heavy box is a good day.
variants_low: Tolls. Pay at the post.
variants_high: At my post, I take the toll from each master whose boat enters the pilgrim water. Pay early in the day while boats are few. The wait is short then.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n3-2
words: I call the sum at my post to the master of each boat going into the pilgrim water. The toll-holder writes it down. I carry the box. Who gets the coin, others argue.
variants_low: Pay the toll. Do not ask who gets it.
variants_high: I call the sum at my post to the master of each boat going into the pilgrim water. The toll-holder writes it down. Pay in full once and your name is good here.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n3
words: Archon is a port on the eastern coast, the one harbour that the province recognises in law. Beaches lie south of the city and marsh lies north. Pilot families steer ships in through the estuary. Past the headland, the harbour authority has no say. I know it only from boat hands.
variants_low: Archon is the eastern port, the legal harbour. Beaches south, marsh north. Pilot families guide ships through the estuary. The harbour authority stops at the headland.
variants_high: Archon is a port on the eastern coast, the one harbour that the province recognises in law. Beaches lie south of the city and marsh lies north. Pilot families steer ships in through the estuary. Past the headland, the harbour authority has no say. Boat hands tell me it is worth seeing.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n3
words: The Prison road and the Border road are old Imperial roads. The Mile House is an old waystation. Folk still call all three by those names. Toward the Rose, you follow the Prison road. On a dry rise beside it, stands the Tag House.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads and a waystation, still called by the old names. The Prison road leads toward the Rose. The Tag House is on a dry rise beside it.
variants_high: The Prison road and the Border road are old Imperial roads. The Mile House is an old waystation. Folk still call all three by those names. Toward the Rose, you follow the Prison road. On a dry rise beside it, stands the Tag House. I have not walked it.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n3
words: Riverwalk is a small halt on a sheltered cove of the sea, a short walk east of Thorn. No food is grown here. We feed the boat hands and give each one a bunk. The ferry stage lies out in the water. Planks run to it from the shore houses.
variants_low: A halt in a sea cove, east of Thorn. We feed the boat hands and give them bunks. Planks lead to the ferry.
variants_high: Riverwalk is a small halt on a sheltered cove of the sea, a short walk east of Thorn. No food is grown here. We feed the boat hands and give each one a bunk. The ferry stage lies out in the water. Planks run to it from the shore houses. Rest well.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n3
words: Tear is a Dunmer town on the border, on the flat coast north of the saltrice lands. From Thorn, the Tear road runs to it. House Dres traded slaves out of Tear for centuries.
variants_low: Tear is a Dunmer border town north of the saltrice country. The road from Thorn reaches it. House Dres ran slaves through it.
variants_high: Tear is a Dunmer town on the border, on the flat coast north of the saltrice lands. From Thorn, the Tear road runs to it. House Dres traded slaves out of Tear for centuries. I would not linger there.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n3
words: Thorn is a city on the border, in the middle of the saltrice country. The Tear road begins there and runs on into Morrowind. House Dres raided Thorn for slaves long ago and profited from its rice. Now the Thorn Ash-Reed Accord debates title to the fields.
variants_low: Thorn is a border city in the saltrice fields. The Tear road begins there. House Dres raided it for slaves. The Thorn Ash-Reed Accord argues over title.
variants_high: Thorn is a city on the border, in the middle of the saltrice country. The Tear road begins there and runs on into Morrowind. House Dres raided Thorn for slaves long ago and profited from its rice. Now the Thorn Ash-Reed Accord debates title to the fields. It is a short walk west.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n3
words: I work the toll post on the spit. The shrine beside it gets swept first each morning, before the post opens. From there the boards run out over the cove to the islet where the ferry lies.
variants_low: I work the toll post on the spit. The ferry lies across the boards. Pay at the post before you cross.
variants_high: I work the toll post on the spit. The water is calm here, so rest on the boards a moment before you cross to the ferry.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n3
words: Silt. Nothing else along this coast gives boats still water, so if the cove fills they tie up elsewhere. The way across is sounded with a pole every morning, before the first boat.
variants_low: Silt. If the cove fills, the boats go elsewhere. The way across is sounded each morning.
variants_high: Silt is the worry. Nothing else along this coast gives boats still water, so a filled cove sends them elsewhere. The way across is sounded with a pole every morning, before the first boat. The boards are safe to walk.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n3
words: Take the Tear road west to Thorn, a short walk. From Thorn it runs on to the town of Tear. For canoes to Hissmir, Murkwater or the Tide Fair, cross the boards to the islet. Deesh-Ra takes the fares there and feeds you first.
variants_low: West along the Tear road is Thorn, then Tear. Canoes leave from the islet.
variants_high: Take the Tear road west to Thorn, a short walk. From Thorn it runs on to Tear. For canoes to Hissmir, Murkwater or the Tide Fair, cross the boards to the islet. Deesh-Ra takes the fares there and feeds you first. Go before dusk.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n3
words: The herb family has the long house out on the piles. Boat hands sleep in the house on the spit that lets beds. Lifts-Two-Traps is the toll-holder at the post. Runs-The-Line-Out and I are his two toll hands.
variants_low: The herb family has the long house. Boat hands sleep on the spit. Ask Lifts-Two-Traps about the post.
variants_high: The herb family has the long house out on the piles. Boat hands sleep in the house on the spit that lets beds. Lifts-Two-Traps runs the post. Runs-The-Line-Out and I are his toll hands. We are glad of the work.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n3
words: I work the toll post on the spit. The ground here grows no food. The coin from the captains buys what is eaten.
variants_low: The ground here grows no food. Captains pay at my post. The coin buys the meals. Pay, then cross.
variants_high: I work the toll post on the spit. The ground here grows no food. The coin from the captains buys the meals. A fed traveller crosses easier.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.n3
words: Captains owe a levy for taking a boat into the pilgrim water. The sum is written down. They pay it at the post. Both Thorn and Hissmir claim the toll. The toll office holds the coin for the state until that is settled.
variants_low: A levy on the boat, paid at the post. Thorn and Hissmir both claim it. Pay me.
variants_high: Captains owe a levy for taking a boat into the pilgrim water. The sum is written down. They pay it at the post. Both Thorn and Hissmir claim the toll. The toll office holds the coin for the state until that is settled. Your coin is safe there.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.stage-mistress
words: Archon is the big port in the east, the one harbour the province treats as legal. Marsh lies north of it. South of it you find beaches. Ships come through the estuary with a pilot family aboard. Past the headland the harbour authority has no power.
variants_low: Archon is the eastern port and legal harbour. Pilot families guide ships through the estuary. Its authority ends at the headland.
variants_high: Archon is the eastern port, the province's legal harbour. Marsh lies north of it and beaches south. A pilot family guides each ship through the estuary. The harbour authority has no power past the headland. The boat folk here talk of it often.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.stage-mistress
words: Hissmir lies up the pilgrim water by canoe. It's a place of pilgrimage where outsiders can touch a Hist. The Root Stewards run the trials there. They can't refuse anyone who comes. Pilgrims eat well here before the canoe sets off. I see to that.
variants_low: Hissmir is up the pilgrim water. The Root Stewards run its trials. All visitors are admitted.
variants_high: Hissmir lies up the pilgrim water by canoe. Outsiders can touch a Hist there. The Root Stewards run the trials. They can't refuse anyone who comes, ojel or not. I'll feed you well before the canoe leaves.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.stage-mistress
words: The Prison road and the Border road are old Imperial roads. The Mile House is an Imperial waystation. We still use those names, Empire or no Empire. The old ones say those roads rotted the cargo. Toward the Rose, the Prison road goes. On a dry rise by it you find the Tag House.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads and a waystation, still called by their old names. The Prison road heads for the Rose.
variants_high: The Prison road and the Border road are old Imperial roads. The Mile House is a waystation on them. People still use the old names. Toward the Rose the Prison road goes. Beside it, up on a dry rise, stands the Tag House. I'd eat before walking it.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.stage-mistress
words: The Compact is a guild. Boatmen, routes and ferries all belong to it. It directs the boats along the rivers and the coast. I work its post at this stage. The Salt-Teeth are pirates who sail inside the Compact. A boat's name can cover a raider.
variants_low: The Compact is the boatmen's guild. It directs boats on river and coast. Salt-Teeth pirates sail inside it.
variants_high: The Compact is a guild of boatmen, with the routes and ferries under it. It directs the boats along the rivers and the coast. I work its post here. Pirates called the Salt-Teeth sail inside the Compact too. I look hard at any boat whose name I don't know.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.stage-mistress
words: Riverwalk is a village in a sheltered cove, just east of Thorn along the Tear road. No food grows here. We feed the boatmen who land and give each boat's hands a bunk. I take the fares at the ferry stage off the islet, at the end of the plank walk.
variants_low: Riverwalk is a cove village east of Thorn. No food grows here. We feed boat hands and bunk them.
variants_high: Riverwalk is a village in a sheltered cove, east of Thorn along the Tear road. No food grows here, so we feed every boat hand who lands and give a bunk besides. You're welcome to a bowl. The ferry stage is out along the plank walk.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.stage-mistress
words: Tear is a Dunmer town on the northern border. It stands on the coastal plain, just beyond the saltrice country. From Thorn the Tear road runs to it. For centuries House Dres ran the slave trade from Tear.
variants_low: Tear is a Dunmer border town. The Tear road runs there from Thorn. Dres ran slaves from it.
variants_high: Tear is a Dunmer town on the coastal plain, just beyond the saltrice country. You reach it from Thorn by the Tear road. House Dres ran the slave trade from there for centuries. Eat before you go that far.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.stage-mistress
words: Thorn is a border city among the saltrice fields, a short walk west of here. The Tear road leaves it for Morrowind. In the old days House Dres raided Thorn for slaves and grew rich on its rice. Now a body called the Ash-Reed Accord argues there about who owns the fields.
variants_low: Thorn is the border city, west up the road. Dres raided it for slaves. The Ash-Reed Accord argues over the rice fields.
variants_high: Thorn is a border city among the saltrice fields, a short walk west. The Tear road leaves it for Morrowind. House Dres once raided it for slaves and grew rich on the rice. Today the Ash-Reed Accord argues over who owns the fields. I'll point you to the road.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.stage-mistress
words: I'm the stage-mistress. I take the fares in the open tent on the islet, at the far end of the plank walk from the shore. The boards under your feet are all different ages. We replace one at a time when it goes soft.
variants_low: The fares are in the tent on the islet. Cross the plank walk and stand there.
variants_high: I'm the stage-mistress, glad of you. The fares are taken in the open tent on the islet, past the end of the plank walk. Mind the boards on the way. They're all different ages, because we replace them one at a time.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.stage-mistress
words: The water in the cove is safe. Mud is the worry. No other water on this coast is sheltered, so if it silts up the boats put in somewhere else. A pole sounds the way across before the first boat each morning. I don't send a canoe out until it's done.
variants_low: The water's safe. Silt is the worry. A pole sounds the way across each morning. Wait for it.
variants_high: The water in the cove is safe, traveller. Silt is the worry, because the boats would go elsewhere if it filled. A pole sounds the way across each morning. I send no canoe out until it's done.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.stage-mistress
words: Thorn is a short walk west up the Tear road. The road goes on from Thorn to the town of Tear. By water, I send canoes off the islet to Hissmir, to Murkwater and to the Tide Fair. Pay at the tent. Eat first.
variants_low: Thorn is west up the Tear road. Canoes to Hissmir, to Murkwater or to the Tide Fair go off the islet. Pay at the tent.
variants_high: Thorn is a short walk west up the Tear road. From there the road runs on to Tear. The water routes are mine to give. I send canoes off the islet to Hissmir, to Murkwater and to the Tide Fair. Pay at the tent. I'll find you a seat and a bowl.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.stage-mistress
words: The herb-gatherers have the long house, the big plank house on piles in the shallows. Boat folk sleep in the plank house on the spit. At the shore end of the walk the toll-holder has his post, with two hands beside him. The ones I can't stand are boatmen who sail off without paying for their bunk.
variants_low: Herb-gatherers in the long house, boat folk on the spit, the toll-holder at the shore end. That is all of us.
variants_high: The herb-gatherers have the long house out on piles. They feed anyone who lands. Boat folk sleep on the spit. The toll-holder sits at the shore end of the walk with two hands. I like the herb-gatherers best. The bunk-dodgers I can't stand.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.stage-mistress
words: This village grows no food of its own. All of it comes in off the boats, so the boat folk get fed first. My part is the fares. I take them in the tent on the islet. No canoe leaves with a passenger who has not eaten.
variants_low: No food grows here. I take fares. Pay at the tent and eat before you ask for a canoe.
variants_high: Nothing grows here, so every bowl comes in off a boat. I take the fares in the tent on the islet. I'll tell you the price of a seat before you sit. The meal comes first if you're hungry.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.stage-mistress
words: Boats moor at the ferry stage, out beyond the islet. I take the fares in the tent there. Passengers pay before they board. A boat's hands I call by the boat's name. A passenger is a traveller to me until the village feeds them. Eaten yet? The long house table is the place.
variants_low: Boats moor at the ferry stage. Fares are paid there before boarding. Boat hands go by their boat's name. Passengers are travellers until fed.
variants_high: Boats moor at the ferry stage beyond the islet. Passengers pay me their fares in the tent before they board. I call the boat hands by the name of their boat. You're a traveller to me until the village feeds you. After that I'll learn your name.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.toll-holder
words: Archon is the eastern port, the province's legal harbour. I only know it from the crews. Marsh lies north of the city. Beaches lie south of it. Families of pilots guide ships in through the estuary. Past the headland, the harbour master has no say.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.toll-holder
words: Hissmir is a xanmeer, one of the old Argonian stone temples, down in southern Shadowfen. Outsiders go there to touch a Hist. Their canoes pass my post on the way up the pilgrim water. Each one gets a line in the Hissmir column.
variants_low: A xanmeer in southern Shadowfen. Outsiders go to touch a Hist. Canoes pay here.
variants_high: Hissmir is a xanmeer, captain, one of the old Argonian stone temples, down in southern Shadowfen. Outsiders go there to touch a Hist. The canoes pass my post on the way up the pilgrim water. I'll write yours in the Hissmir column if you're bound there.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.toll-holder
words: Those are old Imperial work, two roads and a waystation. Folk still use the old names. I don't care for that. The Prison road heads for the Rose. By it, up on a dry rise, is the Tag House.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.toll-holder
words: Riverwalk is this halt, in a cove a short walk past Thorn. We grow no food here. A crew that lands is fed at the long house and given a bunk. The ferry stage lies out across the water, where the boats moor.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.toll-holder
words: Tear is a Dunmer town out on the coastal plain, above the rice country. You reach it by the Tear road out of Thorn. For centuries the Dres house ran its slaving from there.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.toll-holder
words: Thorn is the big city in the saltrice fields, up the Tear road. House Dres raided the city for slaves in the old days and grew fat on its rice. These days Thorn's field-owners send agents out to my spit to shout about the toll.
variants_low: A city in the rice fields. House Dres raided it once. Its agents annoy me.
variants_high: Thorn is the big city in the saltrice fields, captain, up the Tear road. House Dres raided the city for slaves in the old days and grew fat on its rice. Today the field-owners send agents out to my spit to shout about the toll. Go and see it, but keep your coin in your pocket there.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.toll-holder
words: I stand at the head of the boards on the spit. From there I call the toll on every hull that comes in off the sea. They put in here because it's the one calm cove on this stretch of coast. I've seen the swell outside. I wouldn't anchor in it either.
variants_low: A cove. Boats arrive. I enter each hull.
variants_high: Come and stand at the head of the boards a while, captain. I'll show you the cove. I call the toll on every hull from here. The swell outside is why they all stop here. You'll find the water inside stays flat all night.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.toll-holder
words: The water's safe. Silt is what worries me. If the cove fills, the boats will go and tie up somewhere else, and then I've nothing to write. Every morning before the first boat, a pole sounds the way across the cove. I've seen no creature in the water worth a column.
variants_low: Silt. Nothing in the water bites. Mind the boards.
variants_high: Don't worry about the water, captain, it's safe. Silt is the only trouble. If the cove fills, the boats go elsewhere and I've nothing to write. So the way across gets sounded with a pole every morning before the first boat. I'll point out the soft boards myself.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.toll-holder
words: Thorn is a short walk by the Tear road, which carries on out of the city into Morrowind. Canoes for Hissmir leave from the ferry stage, out past the islet. Murkwater and the Tide Fair take canoes from there too.
variants_low: Thorn is up the Tear road. Canoes leave from the ferry stage. The islet.
variants_high: Thorn is a short walk by the Tear road, captain. That road carries on out of the city into Morrowind. For Hissmir, Murkwater or the Tide Fair, go over the boards to the ferry stage past the islet. Deesh-Ra will find you a canoe.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.toll-holder
words: The herb-gatherers keep the long house out on the piles. Boat crews take their bunks on the spit, a step from my post. Two hands share the post with me, Reaches-The-Shore-Last and Runs-The-Line-Out. Between the three of us, every hull that comes gets a line.
variants_low: A household in the long house, crews on the spit, two hands with me at the post. That's the lot.
variants_high: You've come to a friendly cove, captain. The herb-gatherers in the long house will feed you. Crews take their bunks on the spit by my post. Two hands share the toll with me, Reaches-The-Shore-Last and Runs-The-Line-Out. They'll write your hull if I'm eating.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.toll-holder
words: My work is the toll. Boats pay at my post before they go on into the pilgrim water. I call the hull, take the sum and write it down. It's dull work but it's steady. The crews tell me where they've been while I write.
variants_low: The toll. Boats pay it at my post before the pilgrim water. Don't stand on the slate.
variants_high: My work is the toll, captain. I'm good at it. Boats pay at my post before they go on into the pilgrim water. I call the hull, take the sum and write it down. Come by at dusk and I'll show you a full slate. The crews tell me their news while I write.

speaker: npc.dunmer-north.riverwalk.toll-holder
words: Every boat gets a line on my slate, ruled down the middle. Thorn gets a column, Hissmir gets a column, because each of them says the toll is theirs. Boat, column, sum, that's the entry. I don't leave the slate alone on the spit.
variants_low: A line on the slate for every boat. Thorn's column, Hissmir's column. Pay and pass.
variants_high: Every boat gets a line on my slate, captain, ruled down the middle. Thorn gets a column, Hissmir gets a column, because each says the toll is theirs. Boat, column, sum, that's the entry. Pay either agent directly and you've picked a side, so pay me.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.carrier
words: Blackrose is a city on a lake with three rivers running into it. The Rose is the old prison there. Every bundle I carry started in it.
variants_low: A lake city, three rivers. The Rose is its old prison. I go no further than the shelter.
variants_high: Blackrose is a city on a lake with three rivers running into it. The Rose is the old prison there. Every bundle I carry started in it. I only see the Rose's side of the city from here.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.carrier
words: Prison road, Border road, Mile House. The first two are Imperial roads, the third an Imperial waystation. The old names stuck. The Tag House stands beside the Prison road on its dry rise.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads and a waystation, still called by their old names. The Tag House is on the Prison road. This rise.
variants_high: Prison road, Border road, Mile House. The first two are Imperial roads, the third an Imperial waystation. The old names stuck. The Tag House stands beside the Prison road on its dry rise, where you are now.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.carrier
words: The Chainbreakers put up this shelter on the road so Argonian dead from the Rose can reach the dirt. A family lets a body go for the carriage charge. The Chainbreakers pay that and write it down.
variants_low: The Chainbreakers built it for the Rose's dead. Families release a body for a carriage charge, the Chainbreakers pay it. Enough.
variants_high: The Chainbreakers put up this shelter on the road so Argonian dead from the Rose can reach the dirt. A family lets a body go for the carriage charge. The Chainbreakers pay that and write it down. Ux-Vakka will show you the book if you ask him.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.carrier
words: I wrap each body the Rose gives up and carry it home to the villages. Before that, the Chainbreakers have paid the charge. Bones that reach dirt beside a tree can go home too.
variants_low: I carry the Rose's dead to the villages once the Chainbreakers pay. Bones at a tree's dirt can go home too. That is all.
variants_high: I wrap each body the Rose gives up and carry it home to the villages. Before that, the Chainbreakers have paid the charge. Bones that reach dirt beside a tree can go home too. If you find any, bring them to me.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.carrier
words: I tie off the wrapped bundles here for the road home. It is a thatched shelter, a hut and a brazier on a dry rise. I like the ground more than the work.
variants_low: A shelter, a hut, a brazier. I tie bundles here. Ask something else.
variants_high: I tie off the wrapped bundles here for the road home. The rise is dry, the brazier burns. You can sit by it if you keep clear of the cloth. I like the ground more than the work.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.carrier
words: Hoppers, the death kind, wait in the mud under the rise. Stay out of it. After dark, a wisp drifts up.
variants_low: Hoppers in the mud below, a wisp after dark. Go where you like.
variants_high: Hoppers, the death kind, wait in the mud under the rise. Stay out of it. After dark, a wisp drifts up, so stay by the brazier or leave before the light goes.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.carrier
words: Take the Prison road. One way is the Rose, the other way is the villages. I walk it with a bundle on my back and know every step. It is longer than any wait here, even a wait for three bundles.
variants_low: The Prison road. The Rose one way, the villages the other. Pick.
variants_high: Take the Prison road. One way is the Rose, the other way is the villages. I walk it with a bundle on my back and know every step. If you take the village way, I will tell you the turns.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.carrier
words: Ux-Vakka keeps the hut and the book. A family from the Rose stands in the doorway until the coin is paid. I wrap the dead. The families are at their worst while they wait.
variants_low: Ux-Vakka keeps the book. The families wait. I wrap. Leave them be.
variants_high: Ux-Vakka keeps the hut and the book. He is fair about it. A family from the Rose stands in the doorway until the coin is paid. I wrap the dead. The families are at their worst while they wait, so go gently if you speak to them.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.carrier
words: The Rose will not let a body go without coin. The Chainbreakers pay it. The keeper writes it in his book. Then I wrap the bundle. By then, I have watched the counting. I don't care for it.
variants_low: The Chainbreakers pay for the dead, the keeper writes it down, I wrap. That is the work.
variants_high: The Rose will not let a body go without coin. The Chainbreakers pay it. The keeper writes it in his book. Then I wrap the bundle. By then, I have watched the counting. I don't care for it. Watch the knots if you want to learn them.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family-2
words: Blackrose is the city on the lake. A day's march south of it stands the Rose, the Empire's old prison, with families living in it now. My aunt called it home. What did your people call theirs? Home, surely.
variants_low: A city. The Rose is south of it.
variants_high: Blackrose is the lake city. The Rose is a day south of it. Our families live there. I can tell you the way if you want.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family-2
words: The Prison road is one of the old Imperial roads. People still use its old name. It runs toward the Rose. This rise stands beside it, with the Tag House on top.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family-2
words: The Chainbreakers built this shelter on the Prison road. When an Argonian dies in the Rose, the bones come here. Our families let the dead go in return for the carriage charge. The Chainbreakers pay it and write it down.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family-2
words: The Rose was the Empire's prison south of Blackrose, long ago. Families born there three generations back live in it now. None of us says that word. The carriage charge on our dead is the coin the south resents most.
variants_low: We live there. That is all.
variants_high: The Rose is where we live, three generations of us. I will not call it a prison. The charge on our dead is the worst coin we pay.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family-2
words: A thatched shelter on log posts, open at the front, with the keeper's hut beside it and a brazier set between them. While a body waits for the carrier, I sit here. Would my aunt have chosen this roof? I doubt it.
variants_low: Dry ground. Sit or go.
variants_high: It is a poor roof, visitor. Take the bench by the brazier if you want to sit.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family-2
words: Hoppers lie in the mud under the slope. After dark, a wisp comes up from the water. I stay under the thatch with the dead. My aunt would say the same, I think.
variants_low: Hoppers below. A wisp after dark. Go home.
variants_high: Hoppers below the slope, a wisp after dark. Stay by the brazier tonight, visitor. Go at first light.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family-2
words: The Prison road passes the rise. Go one way along it for the Rose, the other way for the villages. For Murkwood Verge, take the track south-east, a few minutes on foot.
variants_low: The road runs two ways. Pick one.
variants_high: The Prison road runs to the Rose one way and to the villages the other. Murkwood Verge is a few minutes south-east on the track.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family-2
words: Ux-Vakka keeps the book. He keeps it fair to us. Okan-Sei is the carrier from the villages. He wraps the dead and looks at us hard while he does it. Vees-Kai waits beside me.
variants_low: Ask the keeper. He talks.
variants_high: The keeper is the one to trust here. I would not say it of the carrier. Sit with Vees-Kai if you wish.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family-2
words: The Chainbreakers pay the charge for each dead one. I lay the coins out in front of me and check them with both hands. Ux-Vakka writes every one in his book before the carrier touches the bundle.
variants_low: I count coins. Leave me to it.
variants_high: Come and watch me count them if you like. I will show you how the book is kept.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family
words: Blackrose is a city on a lake, in the south. Three rivers meet there. Travellers who have only seen the city assume it runs the Rose. It doesn't. The Rose is home to us. Call it that, please.
variants_low: A lake city. Three rivers meet there. The Rose is home.
variants_high: Blackrose is a city on a lake, in the south. Three rivers meet there. Travellers who have only seen the city assume it runs the Rose. It doesn't. The Rose is home to us. You'll be welcome to say so at the shelter.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family
words: The Prison road is one of the old Imperial roads. The Border road is another. The Mile House is an old waystation along them. People kept the old names after the Empire left. The Tag House stands on a dry rise beside the Prison road. You're on it now.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads, old names. This rise is by the Prison road.
variants_high: The Prison road is one of the old Imperial roads. The Border road is another. The Mile House is an old waystation along them. People kept the old names after the Empire left. The Tag House stands on a dry rise beside the Prison road, where you're standing. Walk it south and it comes to the Rose.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family
words: The Chainbreakers put this station up on the Prison road for the bones of our dead, since an Argonian from the Rose must go home to the dirt. A family of the Rose gives up its dead for a carriage charge. The Chainbreakers pay the charge and write it in a book. I wait in the doorway.
variants_low: The Chainbreakers built it for our bones. They pay the charge and write it down.
variants_high: The Chainbreakers put this station up on the Prison road for the bones of our dead, since an Argonian from the Rose must go home to the dirt. A family of the Rose gives up its dead for a carriage charge. The Chainbreakers pay the charge and write it in a book. If you need a tag read, the keeper will do it.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family
words: Outsiders say the Rose was the old Imperial prison, south of Blackrose. They're right about the walls. We don't call it that. Families have been born there three generations deep, so it's the only home we know. In the south, no coin is resented more than the carriage charge on our dead.
variants_low: The Rose was a prison once. Three generations of us were born in it. The charge is hated.
variants_high: Outsiders say the Rose was the old Imperial prison, south of Blackrose. They're right about the walls. We don't call it that. Families have been born there three generations deep, so it's the only home we know. In the south, no coin is resented more than the carriage charge on our dead. Sal-Ozzu can tell you what it costs a household.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family
words: This is the rise where the Rose hands over its dead. There's a thatched shelter, open at the front. The keeper's hut stands beside it. I wait in the doorway while the fee is settled, so I know the ground well. It's dry, I'll give it that. The brazier is lit most of the day.
variants_low: A shelter and a hut. I wait here.
variants_high: This is the rise where the Rose hands over its dead. There's a thatched shelter, open at the front. The keeper's hut stands beside it. I wait in the doorway, so I know the ground well. It's dry here. The brazier is lit. You may warm your hands there if you are quiet about it.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family
words: Death hoppers hunt in the mud under us. After dark, a wisp drifts out of it. I don't go down there at all. The shelter and the hut stand on dry ground, so stay near them. If you mean to travel further, go in daylight.
variants_low: Hoppers in the mud. A wisp after dark. Stay up here.
variants_high: Death hoppers hunt in the mud under us. After dark, a wisp drifts out of it. I don't go down there at all. Stay up by the brazier if the light is going. It's a poor fire, but the hoppers don't come to it.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family
words: The Prison road goes by our rise. Follow it one way and you reach the Rose. Follow it the other way and you reach the villages. For Murkwood Verge, take the track south-east of the hut. It's a few minutes on foot. The track east leads round to the ferry stage.
variants_low: The road. Rose one way, villages the other. Murkwood Verge is south-east.
variants_high: The Prison road goes by our rise. Follow it one way and you reach the Rose, my home. Follow it the other way and you reach the villages. For Murkwood Verge, take the track south-east of the hut. It's a few minutes on foot. The ferry stage is further, east then north then west, a few minutes apiece.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family
words: Ux-Vakka is the tag-keeper. He's got the hut beside the shelter. He writes in his book fairly. Okan-Sei is the carrier from the villages. He wraps the dead. I don't trust the villages' side until the coin is paid. His eyes are rude the whole time. Sal-Ozzu waits here with me.
variants_low: A keeper, a carrier. My own people. I stay in the doorway.
variants_high: Ux-Vakka is the tag-keeper. He's got the hut beside the shelter. He writes in his book fairly. Okan-Sei is the carrier from the villages. He wraps the dead. His eyes are rude about it. Sal-Ozzu waits here with me. After the coin is paid, the carrier is easier to stand.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.rose-family
words: My family waits here. A family of the Rose lets its dead go for a carriage charge. Until it's paid, I stand in the doorway. The bundle stays where it is. The Chainbreakers pay, so we hand over no coin ourselves. It isn't much of a job, only standing.
variants_low: We wait. The carriage charge gets paid. Then the dead go.
variants_high: My family waits here. A family of the Rose lets its dead go for a carriage charge. Until it's paid, I stand in the doorway. The bundle stays where it is. It isn't much of a job, only standing. Ask the keeper for the book if you want the sums. He's fair with it.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
words: The Rose is the old Imperial prison of Blackrose, south of the city along the road, a day's march. Families live in it now. I see them at every handover, so I can tell you they don't call it a prison.
variants_low: An old Imperial prison, south of Blackrose. Families live there now.
variants_high: The Rose is the old Imperial prison of Blackrose, a day's march south along the road. Families live in it now. I see them at every handover. They don't call it a prison. I never do in front of them.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
words: They're abolitionists, the Blackrose Chainbreakers. Slavery's ended in the marsh but the Owing hasn't, so they fight it. They audit the ledgers. Any debt they can show to be false goes on the fire. They also bring the dead's bones home. I keep the book at this station for them.
variants_low: Abolitionists. They fight the Owing, audit ledgers, burn false debts and bring bones home. Ask them.
variants_high: They're abolitionists, the Blackrose Chainbreakers. The Owing is what they fight. They audit the ledgers and burn the debt once the proof is there. They bring the bones of the dead home as well. I keep the book here for them. It's decent work.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
words: A person who owes works for the holder until the sum is cleared. Out where no court sits, the Owing is the only law at all. Holders sell the debt to other holders. It passes to children too, so a child can be born owing. Who sold whose, I don't write in my book.
variants_low: Debt that binds you to work. No court out here, so it's the law. It's sold. It's inherited. Children are born owing. That's all I say.
variants_high: A person who owes works for the holder until the sum is cleared. Where no court sits, the Owing is the only law at all. Holders sell the debt to other holders. It passes to children, so a child can be born owing. Who sold whose, I leave out of my book.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
words: The Empire built three things out here. One is the Border road. Another is a waystation called the Mile House. The third is the Prison road. People still use the Imperial names for them. The Prison road leads on to the Rose. My shelter sits up on a dry rise by the road.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads and a waystation. People keep the old names. The Prison road leads to the Rose. My shelter is beside it.
variants_high: The Empire built three things out here. One is the Border road. Another is a waystation called the Mile House. The third is the Prison road. People still use the Imperial names. The Prison road leads on to the Rose. My shelter sits on a dry rise beside it.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
words: The Chainbreakers built it as a place to take in the bones of Argonian dead from the Rose. The families there release their dead for a carriage charge. The Chainbreakers pay it. I record every payment in the book, then hang the tag on the peg.
variants_low: The Chainbreakers built it for the bones from the Rose. The families take a carriage charge. The Chainbreakers pay it and I record it.
variants_high: The Chainbreakers built this place to take in the bones of Argonian dead from the Rose. The families there release the dead for a carriage charge. The Chainbreakers pay it. I record every payment. You may read the book if you like.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
words: I keep the book for the Chainbreakers, so I can tell you what they're after. They audit the Owing, going through the ledgers of debt line by line. To them, freeing a debtor and carrying a dead one home are one work. If a debtor dies far from the Hist, he may not make it home at all. The Hist is the great tree whose sap makes us what we are.
variants_low: They audit the Owing. Freeing debtors and carrying the dead home are one work to them. A debtor who dies far from the Hist is lost.
variants_high: I keep the book for the Chainbreakers, so I'll tell you plainly. They audit the Owing, ledger by ledger. Freeing a debtor and carrying a dead one home are one work to them. If a debtor dies far from the Hist, the tree of his people, he may not get home at all.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
words: Every basket from the Rose gets a tag from me, hung on a peg. The charge for that body goes in the book before the bundle is wrapped, always in that order. The Rose lets a body go only under the shelter, never out on the road. Without its tag it isn't handed over at all.
variants_low: A tag on every basket. The charge goes in the book first. Bodies go only under the shelter. None goes without a tag.
variants_high: I hang a tag on every basket from the Rose. The charge is written in the book before the bundle is wrapped, so I do that first. The Rose lets a body go only under the shelter, never out on the road. No tag means no handover. A spoken word will not do for a tag.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
words: I'm the tag-keeper here. This is a thatched shelter, open at the front. My hut is a short walk east of it. I hang each basket's tag on the chimes under the eave and write down what was paid. The ground is dry. I can say that much for it. The wind comes straight through the candles.
variants_low: Tag-keeper. A shelter and my hut, on dry ground. That's all there is to see.
variants_high: I'm the tag-keeper here. The shelter is open at the front, so sit under the thatch if the sun is bad. My hut is a short walk east. I hang each basket's tag under the eave and write the payment down. The ground is dry. I'll say that for it.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
words: Below the rise, in the wet mud, death hoppers hunt. I stay up here. After dark, a wisp drifts out of the marsh. I keep the brazier lit through the night and sit at my book.
variants_low: Death hoppers in the mud below. A wisp after dark. Stay up here.
variants_high: Death hoppers hunt in the wet mud below us, so keep to the rise. After dark, a wisp drifts out of the marsh. I keep the brazier lit through the night if you need the light.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
words: Along the Prison road, one way, you reach the Rose. The other way are the villages. Choose your end before you step onto it.
variants_low: Prison road. The Rose one way, the villages the other.
variants_high: The Prison road passes this rise. Follow it one way to the Rose, or the other way to the villages. Choose your end first. Keep to the road.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
words: Three kinds of people come through here. Okan-Sei is the carrier from the villages. He ties off the bundles for the road home. Families from the Rose stand at the door till the coin is down. I deal with them at every handover and I keep the book fair to them. Vees-Kai and Sal-Ozzu are two of them today.
variants_low: A carrier, the families. Me. Leave the families be.
variants_high: Okan-Sei is the carrier from the villages and ties off the bundles for the road home. Vees-Kai and Sal-Ozzu are families from the Rose, waiting at the door till the coin is down. I deal with the families at every handover. I keep the book fair to them. They know it.

speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.rose-bone-waystation.tag-keeper
words: When a basket comes up from the Rose, I open it and hang its tag. The family releases the dead for a carriage charge. That's their word, so I use it. I write the sum in the book, one line for each body. Then the carrier wraps the bundle. The writing is the small part of the work. The families watch every stroke of it.
variants_low: The family pays a carriage charge to release the dead. I write it down. Nothing more to it.
variants_high: When a basket comes up, I hang its tag. The Rose's families release the dead for a carriage charge. They call it that, so I do too. I write each sum in the book, one line a body. You can read the lines if you ask. Then the carrier wraps the bundle.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n1
words: The Nisswo are Argonian priests of Sithis. I came to the Teeth from the travelling Nisswo. They teach that each village should hear many readings.
variants_low: Priests of Sithis. I am one.
variants_high: The Nisswo are Argonian priests of Sithis. I came to the Teeth from the travelling Nisswo. They teach that each village should hear many readings, so one more reading of this place does not frighten me.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n1
words: Imperial hands made the Border road and the Prison road. The Mile House was their waystation. Folk keep calling them by the Imperial names. The Prison road continues toward the Rose. A dry rise beside it holds the Tag House.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads. The Prison road runs toward the Rose. The Tag House sits on a dry rise.
variants_high: Imperial hands made the Border road and the Prison road. The Mile House was their waystation. Folk keep calling them by the Imperial names. The Prison road continues toward the Rose. A dry rise beside it holds the Tag House.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n1
words: Sithis is the void god, the god of change. We teach that a death is a change like any other. Do not call Sithis evil here.
variants_low: The void god of change. A death is a change. Do not call it evil.
variants_high: Sithis is the void god, the god of change. We teach that a death is a change like any other. Call it evil here and the Clutch will not hear you out.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n1
words: A priest rings the bell for pilgrims at the landing. Priests hold the teaching. The band below holds the stair. A nisswo meets every pilgrim and asks for their offering.
variants_low: I ring the bell. Priests hold the teaching. The band holds the stair. A nisswo meets pilgrims and asks for the offering.
variants_high: A priest rings the bell for pilgrims at the landing. Priests hold the teaching. The band below holds the stair. A nisswo meets every pilgrim and asks for their offering. Wait for him at the water.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n1
words: I ring the bell for the landing. No Sithis temple in Murkmire is bigger. The Clutch of Nisswo tend it. Its first purpose is lost.
variants_low: The Teeth. I ring the bell. Ask the band about the rest.
variants_high: I ring the bell for the landing, two strokes at a time. No Sithis temple in Murkmire is bigger. The Clutch of Nisswo tend it, though its first purpose is lost.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n1
words: I flatten my crest at that room. The voriplasm in the flooded deep room strips bare whatever drops in the water. Leeches and swamp jellies stay in the shallows.
variants_low: A voriplasm in the flooded room strips bare what drops there. Leeches in the shallows.
variants_high: Stay out of the water. A voriplasm sits in the flooded deep room and strips bare whatever drops there. Leeches and swamp jellies keep to the shallows near it.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n1
words: Walk north from the head of the pilgrim way. Fourth Stage is there, an old road stage, a short walk.
variants_low: North. Fourth Stage, a short walk.
variants_high: North from the head of the pilgrim way is Fourth Stage, an old road stage. It is a short walk. Go before the light goes.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n1
words: A band of four serves under us priests. Ojel pass inside for the right offering. Empty hands go back the way they came.
variants_low: Four serve under the priests. Bring an offering or leave.
variants_high: Four serve under us priests. Ojel pass inside for the right offering. Bring fruit of your own country. Teeb-Shaal will carry it in for you.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n1
words: Scrubbing is our rite. We clean the black stone down to the waterline. After the second stroke of the bell, it starts. We mend nothing and we add nothing.
variants_low: We scrub the teeth to the waterline. Nothing is mended or added.
variants_high: Come at the second stroke of the bell and watch. The black stone is scrubbed clean to the waterline. Nothing is mended, nothing added. Stay on the bank.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2-2
words: Nisswo is the name of Sithis's priests. They travel, so every village hears more than one reading of the faith. Some of them keep this temple. Their readings are their business.
variants_low: Priests of Sithis. They travel. That is all I know.
variants_high: Nisswo is the name of Sithis's priests. They travel, so every village hears more than one reading of the faith. Some of them keep this temple. Their readings are their business, not mine.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2-2
words: The Prison road is an old Imperial road, still called that by everyone. A dry rise beside it holds the Tag House. I have not walked it.
variants_low: Old Imperial road. Ask a carter.
variants_high: The Prison road is an old Imperial road, still called that by everyone along it. A dry rise beside it holds the Tag House. I have not walked it, only heard the carters.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2-2
words: Sithis is the void god, the source of every change. When a person dies, the priests say to mourn them first, then let them go. I am no priest, so that is all I give you.
variants_low: Sithis is the void god. You mourn the dead, then let them go.
variants_high: Sithis is the void god, the source of every change. When a person dies, the priests say to mourn them first, then let them go. I go to the sermons when I am awake, which is not often.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2-2
words: I keep the watch on the east stair. Teeb-Shaal carries the offerings in from the steps. I stop pilgrims who climb without asking.
variants_low: I keep the watch. Others carry the offerings.
variants_high: I keep the watch on the east stair, from the morning lamps. Teeb-Shaal carries the offerings in from the steps. Come up with yours and I will point you to him.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2-2
words: This is the largest temple of Sithis in Murkmire. I sleep upstairs on a bedroll between day watches, so for me it is where I rest more than where I pray. Why it was built, I do not touch.
variants_low: It is a temple of Sithis. I sleep upstairs. Nothing more from me.
variants_high: It is the largest temple of Sithis in Murkmire. I sleep upstairs on a bedroll between watches. The quiet suits me. Why it was built, I do not touch.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2-2
words: The shallows have leeches and swamp jellies. Deep inside, in the flooded room, a voriplasm eats whatever falls into the water. I have not gone down to look.
variants_low: Leeches and jellies in the shallows. A voriplasm in the flooded room. Stay on the stair.
variants_high: Leeches and swamp jellies keep to the shallows. You can see them from the scaffold. The voriplasm is in the flooded room inside. It strips whatever drops there, so keep your gift in your hands.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2-2
words: Take the track at the end of the pilgrim way and keep north. It is a short walk to Fourth Stage, an old stage on the road.
variants_low: North. Fourth Stage. Short walk.
variants_high: Take the track at the end of the pilgrim way and keep north. Fourth Stage, an old stage on the road, is a short walk. I walk it myself when my watch is done.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2-2
words: There is a band of four under the priests. I am one of them. Pilgrims come up the way with empty hands and expect the door open. I send them back down.
variants_low: Priests, with a band of four under them. Empty hands go back down.
variants_high: The priests keep the temple, with a band of four under them. Bring the right offering and the priests admit you. I turn you round on the stair if you come empty-handed.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2-2
words: The teeth are scrubbed clean down to the waterline, every day. Others hold the brush. My work is the east stair, watching who comes up the track.
variants_low: They scrub the teeth to the waterline. I watch the stair.
variants_high: The teeth are scrubbed clean down to the waterline each day, by hands other than mine. I watch the east stair from the scaffold, where the whole row shows.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2-3
words: The priests call Sithis the void god. Every change belongs to him, a death too. It is no wrong done. I keep the stair, so I leave the rest of the teaching to Zaxi-Rekh.
variants_low: The void god. Ask a priest for more.
variants_high: The priests call Sithis the void god. Every change belongs to him, a death too. None of it is wrong done. Zaxi-Rekh keeps the bell and knows the teaching better. Climb to the top of the steps and she will hear you.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2-3
words: The band wades in the shallows for every rite. The water is cold. Watching, carrying and scrubbing make up the daily rite here, all of it. My share is the stair at night, so I stay dry. Wuleen-Wai takes the water.
variants_low: We watch, we carry, we scrub. Some of us wade the shallows. I take the stair.
variants_high: Every rite has the band wading in the shallows. The water is cold. Watching, carrying and scrubbing are the daily rite, nothing more. I take the stair at night, so I stay dry. Ask Wuleen-Wai about the water.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2-3
words: This is the largest temple of Sithis in Murkmire. The Nisswo of the Clutch tend it. I keep the stair above the landing, so I see every pilgrim who comes up. Its purpose is for the priests to tell. I don't guess at it.
variants_low: A temple of Sithis. The Clutch tend it. Ask the priests about the rest.
variants_high: It is the largest temple of Sithis in Murkmire, with the Clutch of Nisswo to tend it. I see it best from the stair above the landing. Come up in daylight and look at the teeth in the water. The priests will tell you its purpose.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2-3
words: The room far under the temple is flooded. A voriplasm lies in that water. Anything dropped in it is stripped away. Leeches and swamp jellies stay in the shallows by the landing. I look down on them all night from the stair.
variants_low: A voriplasm in the flooded room, leeches and jellies in the shallows. Stay out of the water.
variants_high: There is a voriplasm in the flooded room under the temple. It strips whatever drops into the water. Leeches and swamp jellies stay in the shallows by the landing, so keep your feet on the stone. I watch that water all night.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2-3
words: Fourth Stage lies north, a little walk from here. It was a stopping place on the old road. Take the track from the head of the pilgrim way.
variants_low: North. Fourth Stage. Take the track.
variants_high: Fourth Stage lies north, a little walk from here. It was a stopping place on the old road. Take the track from the head of the pilgrim way. I send most pilgrims there when the steps are full.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2-3
words: Priests of the Clutch run the temple. The four of us in the band stand under them, on the stair and in the water. A stranger gets taken in when the offering is right. Empty hands go back down the steps.
variants_low: Priests rule here, with four of us under them. Bring an offering or go back down.
variants_high: The priests of the Clutch run the temple, with four of us in the band under them. If you bring a good offering, a stranger is let inside. Before you climb, ask Ohl-Nakka at the water. He decides what counts.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2-3
words: My work is the night watch on the stair above the landing. I stand there from the evening lamps until the morning ones. A pilgrim who tries the steps without asking gets stopped. Scrubbing the teeth is the priests' side.
variants_low: I watch the stair at night. That is my work and it does not need your help.
variants_high: I watch the stair above the landing from the evening lamps until the morning ones. Come at dusk and I will show you where pilgrims may stand. The scrubbing is the priests' work, so ask them about it.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2-4
words: The Empire made the Prison road and the Border road. The Mile House was an Imperial waystation. Folk here still call all three by those names. The Prison road leads on to the Rose. Next to that road, on dry ground a little raised, stands the Tag House.
variants_low: The Prison road is an old Imperial road toward the Rose. A Tag House stands on dry ground near it.
variants_high: The Empire made the Prison road and the Border road. The Mile House was an Imperial waystation. Folk here still call all three by those names. The Prison road leads on to the Rose. Next to that road, on dry ground a little raised, stands the Tag House. Pilgrims who come up that way often carry the finest bowls.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2-4
words: Sithis is the void god of change, called Raj-Sithis the Changer in the old speech. The priests teach that death is Sithis at work, so a person who dies has changed. Nothing has been done to wrong them. The bowls I carry in are laid before him.
variants_low: Sithis is the void god of change. The priests teach that death is Sithis at work, so a person who dies has changed.
variants_high: Sithis is the void god of change, called Raj-Sithis the Changer in the old speech. The priests teach that death is Sithis at work, so a person who dies has changed. Nothing has been done to wrong them. The bowls I carry in are laid before him. You may lay one too.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2-4
words: The daily rite is three jobs: watching, carrying and scrubbing. Our band watches the stair and carries the offerings inside, then wades into the shallows until each rite ends. The water is cold. My own part is the carrying.
variants_low: The daily rite is watching, carrying and scrubbing. The band wades into the cold shallows until each rite ends. I carry.
variants_high: The daily rite is three jobs: watching, carrying and scrubbing. Our band watches the stair and carries the offerings inside, then wades into the shallows until each rite ends. The water is cold. Rest by the stair first if you mean to try it. My own part is the carrying.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2-4
words: No temple to Sithis in Murkmire is larger than this one. Priests of the Nisswo look after it, though the reason it was built is lost. I carry the pilgrims' bowls in from the landing. That part of the temple I know well.
variants_low: It is the largest temple of Sithis in Murkmire. The reason for it is lost. I carry bowls in from the landing.
variants_high: No temple to Sithis in Murkmire is larger than this one. Priests of the Nisswo look after it, though the reason it was built is lost. Bring a bowl to the landing and I will carry it in for you.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2-4
words: In the flooded room deep inside the temple lies a voriplasm. It strips whatever falls into that water. Leeches and swamp jellies live in the shallows round the teeth. I do not look into that water.
variants_low: A voriplasm is in the flooded room below. Leeches and swamp jellies are in the shallows. Stay out of the water.
variants_high: In the flooded room deep inside the temple lies a voriplasm. It strips whatever falls into that water, so grip your bowl tight on the stair. Leeches and swamp jellies live in the shallows round the teeth.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2-4
words: Fourth Stage is north of here, only a brief walk. It was a stage on the old road. Follow the track from the end of the pilgrim way and you will reach it.
variants_low: Fourth Stage is north of here, a brief walk. The track starts at the end of the pilgrim way.
variants_high: Fourth Stage is north of here, only a brief walk. It was a stage on the old road. Follow the track from the end of the pilgrim way and you will reach it. You will arrive before you tire.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2-4
words: Priests of the Clutch run the temple, with us four in the band beneath them. The others watch from the stair. I take the bowls from the givers' hands, so I see what each one brings. A stranger is let in for the right offering.
variants_low: Priests run the temple, with four in the band beneath them. A stranger is let in for the right offering. Empty hands wait outside.
variants_high: Priests of the Clutch run the temple, with us four in the band beneath them. The others watch from the stair. I take the bowls from the givers' own hands, so I can tell you what the priests like to see. A stranger is let in for the right offering.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2-4
words: I carry the offerings in from the landing, a bowl at a time. The giver picks the spot for it. After that, I do not lift it again.
variants_low: I carry the offerings in from the landing. The giver picks the spot. I do not lift a bowl again after that.
variants_high: I carry the offerings in from the landing, a bowl at a time. The giver picks the spot, so tell me where you want yours. After that, I do not lift it again.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2
words: The Prison road is one of the old Imperial roads. It runs toward the Rose, with the Tag House by it on a dry rise. Folk still use the old names for them, Mile House for the waystation, Border road for the other road.
variants_low: An old Imperial road, still called by its old name. It runs toward the Rose, with the Tag House by it on a dry rise.
variants_high: The Prison road is an old Imperial road. On a dry rise by its side stands the Tag House. It runs on toward the Rose. People still use the old names for it, for the Border road and for the Mile House, the old waystation.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2
words: Sithis is the void god, the Changer. The priests teach that every death is a change, not a wrong. So you mourn the dead, as long as the grief takes, then you release them. I think of it in the water, with the rite going on around me.
variants_low: Sithis is the void god of change. The priests say a death is a change, to be mourned and then released.
variants_high: Sithis is the void god of change. What the priests here teach is that a death is a change, not a wrong done to anyone. You mourn the dead first, then you release them. I think of that whenever the cold gets to me in the water.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2
words: On the band, we keep the watch on the stair. We carry the offerings inside, then we stand out in the shallows through every rite. I get the shallows more than the others do, waist-deep. Teeb-Shaal takes most of the bowls up the steps. I'd rather carry bowls than wade.
variants_low: We keep the watch on the stair. We carry the offerings inside. Each rite we stand in the shallows. I am the one in the water.
variants_high: The band keeps the watch on the stair. It carries the offerings inside, then stands in the shallows through each rite. I get the water more often than the others. A dry turn on the stair is what I wish for by the end of it.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2
words: It's the biggest temple to Sithis in Murkmire. The teeth are black stone, standing in a row out of the sea. The priests keep them exact. I'm with the band on the east scaffold, where the whole row shows at once. Why it was built I won't guess.
variants_low: It's a temple to Sithis, the biggest in Murkmire. You're looking at it. Why it's here is not mine to guess.
variants_high: It's the biggest temple to Sithis in Murkmire. You've come at a good hour, with the rite quiet. From the east scaffold you can see every tooth in the row, black out of the sea. The door frame on the bank gives you the best first look.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2
words: I know the leeches and the swamp jellies well, since I wade among them through every rite. They keep to the shallows. The voriplasm is another matter. It lies in the flooded room deep inside. Anything that falls into that water comes out stripped. I've no wish to see it.
variants_low: Leeches and swamp jellies keep to the shallows. The voriplasm in the flooded deep room strips anything that falls in the water there. Stay out of both.
variants_high: The leeches and the swamp jellies keep to the shallows, where I wade. The voriplasm lies deeper, in the flooded room. It strips anything that falls into the water there. Keep your offering and your boots back from the edge.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2
words: Fourth Stage is the way out. It's an old road stage. Go north from the temple, it's not far. You pass the door frames on the bank, then the track takes you there. My legs warm up again on that walk after a rite.
variants_low: Fourth Stage, north. A short walk.
variants_high: Fourth Stage is the old road stage. Go north, it's a short way. The track starts past the door frames on the bank. After a rite, I like to walk some of it myself, just to feel my legs again.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2
words: The Clutch priests run the temple. There's me and three men on the band under them. The priests take an outsider in if the offering is right. I mostly see the pilgrims from the water, coming down the way with their offerings in their hands.
variants_low: The priests keep the temple, with a band of four under them. They take outsiders in for the right offering. Bring that or turn back.
variants_high: The Clutch priests run the temple, with a band of four under them, me and three men. They take an outsider in for the right offering. Teeb-Shaal meets the givers at the steps, so give him yours.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.n2
words: I stand with the band in the shallows through each rite, waist-deep. The cold gets into my legs long before it's over. The Clutch scrub the temple's stone as far down as the waterline. They mend nothing and add nothing. Below the line the green stays.
variants_low: I wade through the rite, waist-deep. The Clutch scrub the teeth as far as the waterline.
variants_high: The Clutch scrub the black stone as far down as the waterline each day. They fix nothing. I stand waist-deep in the shallows through each rite, so the cold finds my legs first. It's slow work to watch. Standing through it is slower.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.nisswo-teeth
words: We Nisswo are priests who serve Sithis. We have no fixed doctrine and answer to no central rule. Each of us reads the faith as he was taught, so I cannot settle a dispute for anyone beyond this temple. I keep the Teeth.
variants_low: We Nisswo serve Sithis. We hold no doctrine and no central rule. Do not ask me to settle your dispute.
variants_high: We Nisswo are priests who serve Sithis. We have no fixed doctrine and answer to no central rule. Each priest reads the faith as he was taught. I can tell you how it is read here, but I cannot settle a dispute for the whole province.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.nisswo-teeth
words: The Prison road is an old Imperial road. People still call it by that name. The Tag House is on a dry rise by the road. I have not walked it, because my own road ends at the water.
variants_low: An old Imperial road, still called the Prison road. The Tag House sits on a dry rise by it. I have not walked it.
variants_high: The Prison road is an old Imperial road. People still use that name. On a dry rise by the road is the Tag House. I know it only from the pilgrims who come that way.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.nisswo-teeth
words: Sithis is the god of change. When a pilgrim has lost a kinsman, I tell them what the Nisswo teach. The dead are mourned for their season, then released. Some pilgrims cling to the grief past that season. I have watched them carry it back up the track.
variants_low: Sithis is change. The dead are mourned, then released. That is what we teach.
variants_high: Sithis is the god of change. When a pilgrim comes down grieving, I tell them what we teach. The dead are mourned for their season, then released. Bring your grief here. I will hear it.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.nisswo-teeth
words: I am a nisswo, one of the Argonian priests of Sithis. I meet each pilgrim at the water's edge and ask what offering they carry. Outsiders enter the Teeth only with the right offering, so an empty-handed pilgrim is turned back.
variants_low: I am a nisswo, one of the Argonian priests of Sithis. I meet pilgrims at the water and ask their offering. Outsiders enter only with the right one. An empty-handed pilgrim goes back.
variants_high: I am a nisswo, one of the Argonian priests of Sithis. I meet every pilgrim at the water's edge and ask what offering they carry. Outsiders enter the Teeth only with the right offering. An empty-handed pilgrim goes back, so show me yours first.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.nisswo-teeth
words: What offering do you bring for the Teeth? I ask first, since I stand where the pilgrim way reaches the water and every visitor passes me. The black teeth standing in the sea are the temple. The Clutch of Nisswo keeps all of it.
variants_low: The Teeth are the temple in the sea. The Clutch of Nisswo keeps it. What offering do you bring?
variants_high: What offering do you bring for the Teeth? I ask first, since I stand where the pilgrim way reaches the water. The black teeth in the sea are the temple, kept by the Clutch of Nisswo. I will answer what I can once I have seen your gift.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.nisswo-teeth
words: In the flooded deep room, a voriplasm strips whatever falls into the water. Leeches and swamp jellies stay in the shallows round the teeth. The stone below the waterline is not for touching, so keep your hands off it.
variants_low: A voriplasm in the flooded deep room strips whatever falls into that water. Leeches and swamp jellies stay in the shallows. Touch nothing below the waterline.
variants_high: The flooded deep room holds a voriplasm that strips whatever drops into that water. Leeches and swamp jellies stay in the shallows round the teeth. Watch your feet at the landing. Keep clear of the stone below the waterline.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.nisswo-teeth
words: North of the temple, a short walk, you reach Fourth Stage. That is the old road stage. The pilgrim way ends at the water here, so go back between the two scaffolds to the track.
variants_low: North, a short walk, is Fourth Stage. It is the old road stage. Go back up between the scaffolds.
variants_high: I walk the pilgrim way each day, so I know it well. North of the temple, a short walk, you reach Fourth Stage, the old road stage. Go back between the two scaffolds to the track.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.nisswo-teeth
words: The Clutch priests hold the temple. Four of the band work beneath them. An outsider is taken in only for the right offering. Too many walk down here with empty hands and long questions. I turn them back at the water.
variants_low: Priests hold the temple, with four of the band beneath them. Outsiders enter for the right offering. You have not shown me one.
variants_high: The Clutch priests hold the temple, with four of the band beneath them. An outsider goes in for the right offering. Bring yours to me first. I will tell you plainly if it is right.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.nisswo-teeth
words: My office is the pilgrim way down to the water. From the time the lamps go out, I stand at the west stair and meet each pilgrim. I know a right offering on sight. The scrubbing belongs to the others.
variants_low: I meet pilgrims at the water. That is my office. The scrubbing belongs to the others.
variants_high: Come to the west stair after the lamps go out. I will look at your offering there and tell you plainly whether it will do.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.the-one
words: Those are Imperial names, old ones. The Border road and the Prison road were laid by the Empire. The Mile House is a waystation on them. We still use the Empire's names. Toward the Rose, that is where the Prison road leads. Beside it is the Tag House, up on a dry rise.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads and a waystation, with the old names still in use. Toward the Rose, that is where the Prison road leads. The Tag House sits up on dry ground beside it.
variants_high: Those are Imperial names, old ones. The Border road and the Prison road were laid by the Empire. The Mile House is a waystation on them. We still use the Empire's names. Toward the Rose, that is where the Prison road leads. Beside it is the Tag House, up on dry ground, a fair place to rest your feet.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.the-one
words: Sithis is the void god of change. I hold a brush, not a sermon, so that is the part I can say plainly. The teeth are clean above the waterline by evening. The green starts back by morning.
variants_low: Sithis is the void god of change. That is all I carry.
variants_high: Sithis is the void god of change. I hold a brush, not a sermon, so that is the part I can say plainly. Stand on the west scaffold at dusk. The tide takes the light off the teeth.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.the-one
words: Up from the landing I haul a bucket. With it I clean the teeth to the waterline, no deeper. The scrubbing is a ritual. Nothing gets repaired or added. The band leaves the stone beneath that line untouched.
variants_low: Bucket from the landing. Scrub to the waterline. It is a ritual, so nothing is mended or added. The stone beneath that line stays untouched.
variants_high: Up from the landing I haul a bucket. With it I clean the teeth to the waterline, no deeper. The scrubbing is a ritual. Nothing gets repaired or added. The band leaves the stone beneath that line untouched. The green down there stays green.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.the-one
words: I scrub the black teeth, so I see this place closer than most. Murkmire has no bigger temple of Sithis. The Clutch of Nisswo looks after it. Ask me what it was built to do and I point you at the stone above the waterline.
variants_low: Murkmire has no bigger temple of Sithis. The Clutch of Nisswo looks after it. I scrub it. Nothing more from me.
variants_high: I scrub the black teeth, so I see this place closer than most. Murkmire has no bigger temple of Sithis. The Clutch of Nisswo looks after it. Come at low tide and watch the stone dry above the waterline. It shows best then.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.the-one
words: Everything dangerous here lies below the waterline. Down in the deep room the sea has flooded, a voriplasm strips whatever drops into the water. Leeches and swamp jellies stay out in the shallows. I watch my brush hand near the edge.
variants_low: A voriplasm lies in the flooded deep room. It strips whatever drops down. Leeches and jellies stay out in the shallows. Keep out of the water.
variants_high: Everything dangerous here lies below the waterline. Down in the deep room the sea has flooded, a voriplasm strips whatever drops into the water. Leeches and swamp jellies stay out in the shallows. Wade only if you must. Check your legs after.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.the-one
words: A short walk north brings you to Fourth Stage, an old road stage. Take the track at the end of the pilgrim way. I walk the other way each day, down to the landing for my bucket.
variants_low: Fourth Stage is north. Short walk. Take the track.
variants_high: A short walk north brings you to Fourth Stage, an old road stage. Take the track at the end of the pilgrim way. You have time to reach it before the lamps come on at dusk.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.the-one
