words: Four hands of the band work under the priests who keep the temple. I am none of them. I carry the bucket. An outsider gets taken inside when the offering is right. Pilgrims with empty hands stand on the bank a long while.
variants_low: Priests keep the temple. Four of the band serve under them. Bring the right offering or stay out.
variants_high: Four hands of the band work under the priests who keep the temple. An outsider gets taken inside when the offering is right. Bring something plain, laid with care. Teeb-Shaal carries the offerings. He is the man you want to meet.

speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.teeth-of-sithis.the-one
words: Each morning when the lamps go out, I carry the bucket up from the landing to the west scaffold. I work the teeth from there with a brush. My arms are green to the elbow by noon. Above the line I leave nothing dirty.
variants_low: I carry a bucket and I scrub. That is the work.
variants_high: Each morning when the lamps go out, I carry the bucket up to the west scaffold. I work the teeth with a brush from there. Come by at the midday break. I eat then. I can show you how the brush is held.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
words: Blackwood is hill country in the west of the province. A road climbs through it into Cyrodiil. The hill people stay by their own tree's roots. They care little for strangers. A riddle they will always take.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
words: We are the remains of a Legion column. The recall came and the men were never paid. Their sons and grandsons live on the shelf above the Mile House track. I am one of them.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
words: Chasepoint is a stage on the coast road. The Legion built it. Wreck-salvage families keep it now. Salvage rights pass from parent to child. Rope is dried in the old stable. Two of the families each claim to be keeper there.
variants_low: A coast road stage the Legion built. Salvage families keep it. Rights pass down. Two families claim the keeper's post.
variants_high: Chasepoint is a stage on the coast road, put up by the Legion. Wreck-salvage families keep it now. Their rights pass from parent to child. They dry rope in the old stable. Two families each claim to be keeper there.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
words: Some garrisons stayed behind in the province once the Empire pulled out. Their heirs are counted as Legion too. The old road stages are Legion work. Salvage families keep a few of them today.
variants_low: Garrisons stayed behind once the Empire pulled out. Heirs are Legion too. The stages are Legion work. Salvage families keep a few.
variants_high: Some garrisons stayed behind in the province once the Empire pulled out. Their heirs are Legion too, as my men are. The old road stages are Legion work. Salvage families keep a few of them today.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
words: The Prison road and the Border road are old Imperial roads. The Mile House was a waystation on them. Folk still use the old names. The Prison road heads for the Rose. A dry rise carries the Tag House beside it.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
words: Page forty of the pay book shows the arrears, so a pardon alone is no use to me. The Mile House talks of a pardon and a wage from Gideon. They add that the governor refuses to pay for clearing us. The toll company would rather hire the men than buy them off.
variants_low: A pardon without the arrears in the pay book is worth nothing. The Mile House talks of Gideon, a pardon, a wage. The governor refuses to clear us. The toll company would rather hire the men.
variants_high: Page forty of the pay book shows the arrears, so a pardon alone is no use to me. The Mile House talks of a pardon and a wage from Gideon. They add that the governor refuses to pay for clearing us. The toll company would rather hire the men than buy them off. Bring me word if it is true.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
words: I keep the watch for the column. I write the roster in my own hand. The pay book is in my tent, with the column's last entry in it. A stranger gets my questions first. I hear his business before anyone draws.
variants_low: I keep the watch. I write the roster. The pay book holds the last entry. A stranger answers me before blades come out.
variants_high: I keep the watch for the column. I write the roster in my own hand. The pay book holds the column's last entry. A stranger speaks with me before any blade is drawn. Speak plainly, citizen. It goes well.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
words: The column pitched four tents on a flat shelf up in the hills, over the Mile House track. We have a tarn fed by a spring at our backs. The Gideon road cannot see the camp.
variants_low: Four tents on a flat shelf over the Mile House track. A tarn lies behind them. Nothing more.
variants_high: Four tents sit on a flat shelf over the Mile House track, with a spring tarn behind them. Fill your flask there, citizen. The water is clean.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
words: Up the hill above the tents the hackwings have their nests. Stay on the path under the bench and they keep to their rocks. After dark, the rats get into the meal sacks. We hang what we can.
variants_low: Hackwings up the hill. Rats at night. Keep to the path.
variants_high: Up the hill above the tents the hackwings have their nests. Stay on the path under the bench. After dark, the rats get into the meal sacks, so hang your food from the pole by my tent.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
words: Take the track down from the barricade. It brings you to the Eagle's Mile House, then farther to Cartwright's Cross. You will find both on the Gideon road. Past the Cross the Blackwood Road climbs west. I have never walked it.
variants_low: Down the track from the barricade. Mile House, then Cartwright's Cross. The Gideon road is there.
variants_high: Take the track down from the barricade. It brings you to the Eagle's Mile House, then farther to Cartwright's Cross. You will find both on the Gideon road. Past the Cross the Blackwood Road climbs west. I have never walked it.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
words: Six names stand on the roster: mine, then five heirs of the column. Their grandfathers were drawn from every province. The colours came down to them from their fathers. Each one stands a watch.
variants_low: Six on the roster. Me, then five heirs of the column. Each stands a watch.
variants_high: Six names are on the roster: mine, then five heirs of the column. Their grandfathers were drawn from every province. The colours came down to them from their fathers. Each one stands a watch. I am proud of that.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n1
words: I set the watch. It is called on the hour, day and night. The men at the barricade take a levy from each traveller. That money buys what we eat.
variants_low: Watch on the hour. The barricade takes a levy from all. It buys our food.
variants_high: I set the watch, called on the hour, day and night. The barricade takes a levy from each traveller for our food. Pay it plain and you will have no trouble from me.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-2
words: Blackwood is the hill country, out west in Black Marsh. The road up to Cyrodiil climbs through it. Hill folk keep to the roots of their own tree and show strangers little interest. They like a riddle.
variants_low: Hill country in the west of the marsh. The Cyrodiil road climbs through it. They like riddles. Leave them be.
variants_high: Blackwood is the hill country, out west in Black Marsh. The road up to Cyrodiil climbs through it. Hill folk keep to the roots of their own tree. They like a riddle, sir, if you have one.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-2
words: It's what's left of a Legion column. Once recalled, the Legion never paid them a coin. The sons and grandsons of those men live in the camp on the bench above the Mile House track.
variants_low: What's left of a Legion column. The Legion never paid them. Their sons and grandsons live on this bench.
variants_high: It's what's left of a Legion column, sir. Once recalled, the Legion never paid them a coin. The sons and grandsons of those men live in the camp on this bench.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-2
words: Gideon is the frontier city in the west. Coming from Cyrodiil by the Blackwood Road, it's the first town you meet. The courts there still work. An Owing made there is only paper, so you can fight it before a judge.
variants_low: Gideon is the frontier city in the west. First town on the Blackwood Road from Cyrodiil. Its courts still work. An Owing there is paper you can contest.
variants_high: Gideon is the frontier city in the west, sir. Coming from Cyrodiil by the Blackwood Road, it's the first town you meet. The courts still work. An Owing made there is only paper, so you can fight it before a judge.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-2
words: The Prison road and the Border road are old Imperial roads. So is the Mile House, a waystation. Folk still use the old names. The Prison road heads for the Rose. A Tag House sits on a dry rise beside it.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads, the Prison road and the Border road. Folk keep the old names. A Tag House on a dry rise beside the first.
variants_high: Old Imperial roads, sir, the Prison road and the Border road, with the Mile House as a waystation. Folk keep the old names. The Prison road heads for the Rose. A Tag House sits on a dry rise beside it.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-2
words: Soldiers of the Legion, posted on the border road. Command recalled them about two centuries ago. We kept the colours. That's the whole of it.
variants_low: Legion soldiers on the border road. Recalled two centuries gone. That's all.
variants_high: Soldiers of the Legion, posted on the border road. Command recalled them two centuries back. We kept the colours, sir.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-2
words: Four tents on a bench above the Mile House track. I stand a watch here, that's all. The tarn's at our back.
variants_low: Four tents on the bench above the Mile House track. Nothing here for you.
variants_high: Four tents on a bench above the Mile House track. Take the fire if you're cold, sir. The tarn's at our back.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-2
words: Wings in the nests on the hill above. I stand the day watch right under them. The rats come at night, down from the marsh.
variants_low: Wings in the nests uphill. Rats at night. Keep clear of both.
variants_high: Wings in the nests on the hill above. I stand under them by day. Rats at night. Keep to the track, sir.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-2
words: Go down the track. You reach the Mile House first, the one with the eagle. Cartwright's Cross lies further along the road.
variants_low: Down the track. The Mile House, then Cartwright's Cross. Go.
variants_high: Down the track, sir. The Mile House with the eagle comes first. Cartwright's Cross lies further along the road. Mind the ruts.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-2
words: The serjeant writes the duty roster himself, in his own hand. Six names on it, mine too. They're sound men. Every one stands his watch.
variants_low: The serjeant keeps the roster in his own hand. Six names. Ask him.
variants_high: The serjeant writes the roster in his own hand. Six names, mine too. They're sound men, sir. Every one stands his watch.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-2
words: I stand the watch. It's called on the hour, day and night. Mine is the day watch, on the uphill side.
variants_low: We stand the watch. It's called on the hour. That's the work.
variants_high: I stand the watch. It's called on the hour, day and night. Mine is the day, uphill. It's honest work, sir.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-3
words: Blackwood is hilly ground along the western edge of the province. The Blackwood Road climbs up through those hills into Cyrodiil. I only know the hill people from the road folk who pass my fire. They keep close to their own tree and show strangers little curiosity, but they like a riddle.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-3
words: That's us. We're what's left of a Legion column. The Legion never paid these men when it was recalled. Their sons and grandsons live here now, in a camp on a shelf of level ground up the hill from the Mile House track. I feed them.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-3
words: The Imperials laid those roads. The Mile House was their waystation. People still use the old names, Border road and Prison road. The Prison road heads off to the Rose. You'll find the Tag House on a dry rise by that road.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-3
words: The column was Legion soldiers posted along this frontier. About two centuries back, the Legion called them home with their wages still owing. Part of them stayed on here instead of marching out. The pay never came. The last entry in the pay book is theirs. The men on the roster are their sons and grandsons.
variants_low: The Legion was recalled about two centuries back with our wages owing. Part of the column stayed. The pay never came.
variants_high: The column was Legion soldiers posted along this frontier. When the Legion was recalled, their pay was owing. Part of them stayed on here. The pay never came. The last entry in the pay book is theirs. The men on the roster are their sons and grandsons.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-3
words: This is a posting on a level bench by a spring tarn, up in the hills where the Gideon road can't see it. I cook at the fire by the command tent. Six of us are on the roster now. The pot has to stretch to all of us.
variants_low: It's a camp on a bench. Ask the serjeant if you want more. I've a pot to mind.
variants_high: It's a posting on a level bench by a spring tarn, up where the Gideon road can't see it. I cook here for the watch. Sit by the fire if your feet are tired. The pot's thin, but it's hot.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-3
words: Hackwings nest on the hill over the tents, but they keep to the hill. The rats are the trouble. They get into the meal sacks at night, so I stack the sacks myself.
variants_low: Hackwings on the hill. Rats in the sacks. Keep off the hill.
variants_high: Hackwings nest on the hill over the tents, but they keep to the hill. The rats get into the meal sacks at night. I stack the sacks myself, so you'll not be bitten by anything here if you stay by the fire.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-3
words: Take the track north-west from the barricade to the Mile House, a few minutes' walk. For Cartwright's Cross it's longer: east, then south-west, then north-west, then west along the Blackwood Road, then north-west again. Each leg is a few minutes. After the Cross you're on the Gideon road.
variants_low: North-west to the Mile House, a few minutes. The Cross is further. Follow the turnings.
variants_high: North-west along the track from the barricade brings you to the Mile House in a few minutes. For Cartwright's Cross, go east, then south-west, then north-west, then west on the Blackwood Road, then north-west again. Each leg is a few minutes. After the Cross you're on the Gideon road.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-3
words: Six are on the roster. Every one of them stands a watch, me included. Severa and Anwen eat at my fire. Gnaeus Martius is the serjeant. He writes the roster in his own hand.
variants_low: Six on the roster. Every one stands a watch. The serjeant keeps the roster.
variants_high: Six are on the roster. Every man stands a watch. Severa and Anwen eat at my fire. Gnaeus Martius is the serjeant. He writes the roster himself, in his own hand. The names are all in there.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2-3
words: I'm the cook for the watch, so I make what the levy buys. It buys less barley every season. A man who pays at the barricade stays a traveller until the camp has fed him. I keep a ladle spare for that.
variants_low: I cook. A man stays a traveller until the camp has fed him. That's how it is here.
variants_high: I cook for the watch with whatever the levy buys. That's less barley every season. A man who pays at the barricade stays a traveller until the camp has fed him. For you I'll find a ladle.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2
words: Blackwood's the hill country across the western side of Black Marsh. The road named for it climbs those hills up to Cyrodiil. The hill people stay near the roots of their own tree and don't care to talk to strangers. They do love a riddle, I'm told. I can't say I've had one out of them.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2
words: That's us, the leavings of a Legion column. The men were owed their pay when the Legion marched home. It never came. Their sons and grandsons hold the colours still, in a camp on this bench above the Mile House track. The book calls it a post.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2
words: Gideon is the frontier city, out west. It's the first settlement you reach on the Blackwood Road coming down from Cyrodiil. Its courts still sit and hear cases. That matters for an Owing, which is a debt worked off in labour. An Owing made in Gideon is a paper contract. A court can contest it.
variants_low: The frontier city in the west, first on the Blackwood Road from Cyrodiil. Its courts still sit. An Owing made there is paper, so a court can contest it.
variants_high: Gideon is the frontier city, out west. It's the first settlement on the Blackwood Road coming down from Cyrodiil. Its courts still sit. An Owing made there is a paper contract, so a court can contest it. If you're bound to one, that road is worth walking. Leyawiin trade keeps us fed when the road is open.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2
words: Those are old Imperial roads, with the Mile House as a waystation on them. Folk still use the old names. The Prison road heads toward a place called the Rose. The Tag House sits on a dry rise beside it.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2
words: The column was Legion soldiers set to hold the border road. The order to leave came about two centuries back. The column's last entry is still in our pay book. We're what the book still counts. Call the levy a robbery and I'll answer you sharply.
variants_low: Legion soldiers on the border road. Recalled two centuries ago. We're what's left of them.
variants_high: The column was Legion soldiers set to hold the border road. The order to leave came about two centuries back. We keep their duty roster and wear their colours. I'm proud of that much.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2
words: We're four tents on a bench, a flat shelf of hill with the Mile House track running below it. There's a spring pool behind us. I'm Severa Maro. I go down to the barricade to ask each traveller for the levy of passage. That's the Legion's name for it, so I use it.
variants_low: Four tents on a bench over the Mile House track. Pay the levy of passage at the barricade.
variants_high: We're four tents on a bench over the Mile House track, with a spring pool at our backs. I'm Severa Maro. Stop at the barricade, pay the levy of passage and I'll point you to the fire. The cook has a pot on most days.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2
words: Rats in the meal sacks, hackwings on the hill above. I'd sooner lose a day to the hackwings. They don't eat what the levy bought.
variants_low: Rats at night, hackwings on the hill. Keep off the slope.
variants_high: Rats in the meal sacks, hackwings on the hill above. Don't climb the slope behind the tents. The hackwings don't care for visitors. I'd sooner not carry you down.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2
words: Go down the track from the barricade and the Mile House comes first, the one called of the Eagle. Cartwright's Cross comes after it. Both lie along the Gideon road, so either one sets you toward the city. Settle the levy before you start down. I'd sooner take it face to face than chase you.
variants_low: Down the track. Mile House first, then Cartwright's Cross, both on the Gideon road. Levy first.
variants_high: Go down the track from the barricade and the Mile House comes first, the one called of the Eagle. Cartwright's Cross comes after it. Both are on the Gideon road. Mind the steep ground below us.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2
words: Six on the roster. The serjeant is Gnaeus Martius. The other five of us had grandfathers from different provinces. He writes every name in his own hand. He won't strike one while the man lives.
variants_low: Six on the roster. Gnaeus Martius, the serjeant, keeps it. Ask him about the rest of us.
variants_high: Six on the roster. The serjeant is Gnaeus Martius. The other five of us had grandfathers from different provinces. He writes every name in his own hand. I eat from the same pot as the rest each evening.

speaker: npc.imperial-fringe.the-broke-column.n2
words: I step out at the barricade and ask for the levy of passage, as the book words it. Until the pot has fed you, you're a traveller to us. Your coin goes to the cook fire. It's thin work, I'll say that. The pot gets thinner each month.
variants_low: I ask for the levy at the barricade. You're a traveller until you've been fed. The coin goes to the pot.
variants_high: I step out at the barricade and ask for the levy of passage, as the book words it. You're a traveller to us until you've eaten. Pay it and the cook fire will have a bowl for you, thin as it is.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-dyer
words: Alten Corimont is the river port at the foot of the nine bends, in eastern Shadowfen, where the waterway runs to the sea. Argonian smugglers and pirates run it. None of them sides with anyone in a war. Crews of every kind may tie up at the docks. The docks are where the gangs dredging the lower channel get hired.
variants_low: Alten Corimont is the port below us. Smugglers and pirates run it. The gangs get hired there.
variants_high: Alten Corimont is the river port at the foot of the nine bends, in eastern Shadowfen, where the waterway runs to the sea. Argonian smugglers and pirates run it. None of them sides with anyone in a war. Crews of every kind may tie up at the docks. The gangs dredging the lower channel get hired there. Our roll goes the same way.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-dyer
words: Gang Ground is a camp for the families of one dredging gang. It stands on firm ground, with the Border road on one side and the marsh on the other. It has stood about forty years. The highest terrace stays dry, so a hatching shed stands there. The gang's eggs lie inside. The eggs are why the families stay put.
variants_low: Gang Ground is where the gang families live. Ask them about the rest.
variants_high: Gang Ground is a camp for the families of one dredging gang. It stands on firm ground, with the Border road on one side and the marsh on the other. It has stood about forty years. The highest terrace stays dry, so a hatching shed stands there. The gang's eggs lie inside. The eggs are why the families stay put. I won't fault them for that.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-dyer
words: Our village stands on a low island with a Hist growing at its middle. A Hist is a great tree with a mind of its own. Alten Corimont is the port you reach after poling nine bends of river down. The water up here is fresh. Down the lower channel, the gang families were hatched beneath our tree. Every year the roll takes more of our adults away downriver.
variants_low: Nine Bends is the village round the Hist on the island. The port is nine bends below. Ask the elder the rest.
variants_high: Our village stands on a low island with a Hist growing at its middle. A Hist is a great tree with a mind of its own. Alten Corimont is the port you reach after poling nine bends of river down. The water up here is fresh, so drink. Down the lower channel, the gang families were hatched beneath our tree. Every year the roll takes more of our adults away downriver.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-dyer
words: The old ones say the Imperial roads rotted the cargo. The Mile House, the Border road and the Prison road are three names you'll hear. All three are old Imperial work, two roads and a waystation. The people still use the Imperial names for them. The Prison road leads toward the Rose. Beside it the Tag House sits on a dry rise.
variants_low: The Prison road is an old Imperial road. It leads toward the Rose. The Tag House sits by it.
variants_high: The old ones say the Imperial roads rotted the cargo. The Mile House, the Border road and the Prison road are three names you'll hear. All three are old Imperial work, two roads and a waystation. The people still use the Imperial names for them. The Prison road leads toward the Rose. Beside it the Tag House sits on a dry rise.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-dyer
words: Reed comes to me cut, an armful at a time, from the cutters on the bank. In the vat, I steep it until the colour takes. Green comes first. Blue takes longest. The dye stains me to the wrist.
variants_low: The cutters bring me armfuls of reed. I steep it in the vat. The dye stains me to the wrist.
variants_high: Reed comes to me cut, an armful at a time, from the cutters on the bank. In the vat, I steep it until the colour takes. Green comes first, then the red-root takes longer. The dye stains me to the wrist. Come and watch a batch turn.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-dyer
words: Drink the water here. It's still fresh, a thing you won't find down by the port. I draw all my vat water from the bank. Dye goes dull in bad water. The tree in the middle of the ring is kin to us.
variants_low: The water's fresh. Drink it or leave it.
variants_high: Drink the water here. Fill a skin before you go. It's still fresh. I draw my vat water from the bank for that reason. Dye goes dull in bad water. The tree in the middle of the ring is kin to us.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-dyer
words: Hunters lie in the river where you come up to us. Jellies float in the shallows round the landing stage. A moon adder lies along the bank. I carry my cloth to the water on the far side of the vat house, away from all three.
variants_low: Hunters in the river. Jellies at the stage. A moon adder on the bank.
variants_high: Hunters lie in the river where you come up to us. Jellies float in the shallows round the landing stage. A moon adder lies along the bank. Wade nowhere you can't see the bottom. The tree's chimes will tell you the village is close.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-dyer
words: There's no road, not even in sight of us. You pole downriver a day to the gang camp. The port lies beyond it. On the way back up, listen for the chimes. They carry a bend downstream of the village.
variants_low: No road. Pole downriver a day to the gang camp. The port is past it.
variants_high: There's no road here, not even in sight. Pole a day downriver to the gang camp, with the port on beyond it. On the way back up, listen for the chimes. They carry a bend below the village. Follow the sound to the landing.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-dyer
words: The elder, Deeka-Seesh, hears every quarrel and debt between the houses. Each year more of the grown ones are on the roll. The cutters bring me reed and a week of gossip with it. I pay for the reed. The gossip comes free and I don't want it.
variants_low: Debts go to the elder. More of the grown ones are on the roll each year. Ask the cutters for gossip.
variants_high: Quarrels and debts between the houses are brought to Deeka-Seesh, our elder. More of the grown ones are on the roll each year. Xuth-Duun cuts the best reed on this bank. His talk comes with it. I take the reed and let the talk run off.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-dyer
words: I dye cloth and cord at the vat with roots from the marsh. The only coin that reaches Nine Bends comes off the roll, the list of our people hired out downriver. More of the grown ones are on it each year. Some houses have every adult away.
variants_low: I dye. The coin comes off the roll, the hiring downriver. Some houses have every adult on it.
variants_high: I dye cloth and cord at the vat with marsh roots. Come by when the red root is steeping, for the whole lane smells of it. Our only coin comes off the roll, the hiring downriver. More adults sign on each year. Some houses have every one of them away.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-net-menders
words: Alten Corimont is the river port out east in Shadowfen. Argonian pirates and smugglers run it. It takes no side in a war. Any boat may tie up. The dredging gangs are hired off its docks.
variants_low: A river port in east Shadowfen. Pirates and smugglers run it. No side in a war. The dredging gangs hire there.
variants_high: Alten Corimont is the river port out east in Shadowfen. Argonian pirates and smugglers run it. It takes no side in a war. Any boat may tie up there. The dredging gangs are hired off its docks.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-net-menders
words: Gang Ground is the camp of a dredging gang's families. It sits on firm ground where the Border road meets the marsh. The dry top terrace holds a hatching shed.
variants_low: The camp of a dredging gang's families. Firm ground by the Border road and the marsh. A hatching shed on top.
variants_high: Gang Ground is the camp of a dredging gang's families. It sits on firm ground where the Border road meets the marsh. The dry top terrace holds a hatching shed. They stay for it.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-net-menders
words: The Hist has its own mind, a tree. Eggs lie in a clutch by its roots. Each hatchling drinks sap on its naming day. It shapes body and scales for good. Sap is blood and soul. The minder reads the signs for the clutch.
variants_low: The Hist has a mind. Eggs lie by its roots. Hatchlings drink sap at the naming. It shapes us for good. Sap is blood and soul. The minder reads the signs for the clutch.
variants_high: The Hist has its own mind, a tree. Eggs lie in a clutch by its roots. Each hatchling drinks sap on its naming day. It shapes body and scales for good. Sap is blood and soul. The minder reads the signs for the clutch. Ask her.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-net-menders
words: Our Hist stands on a low island. Alten Corimont, the port, is nine bends of river below us. The water here is fresh. More of our adults go downriver on the roll each year.
variants_low: Our Hist, on a low island, nine bends above the port. Fresh water. The roll takes more adults each year.
variants_high: Our Hist stands on a low island. Alten Corimont, the port, is nine bends of river below us. The water here is fresh, so drink. More of our adults go downriver on the roll each year.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-net-menders
words: Three old Imperial works stand out there: the Mile House waystation, the Border road, the Prison road. We use the old names yet. Follow the Prison road to the Rose. A dry rise beside it holds the Tag House.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads and a waystation, with old names. Follow the Prison road to the Rose. The Tag House is on a dry rise by it.
variants_high: Three old Imperial works stand out there: the Mile House waystation, the Border road, the Prison road. We use the old names yet. Follow the Prison road to the Rose. A dry rise beside it holds the Tag House.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-net-menders
words: Our fish traps stand where the free port's boats load now. Both claims are old, ours and the port's. Ask the elder if the village will speak up.
variants_low: Traps are ours. The free port's boats load there now. Both claims are old. Ask the elder if the village will speak up.
variants_high: Our fish traps stand where the free port's boats load now. Both claims are old, ours and the port's. Ask the elder if the village will speak up. She hears the quarrels.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-net-menders
words: I make torn nets and worn gear sound again. I work in the open, so watch. Bring a net if you have one. I count knots as I tie.
variants_low: I mend torn nets and worn gear. In the open. Bring a net.
variants_high: I make torn nets and worn gear sound again. I work in the open, so watch if you like. Anyone may bring a net, any net.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-net-menders
words: I mend nets on the rack by the landing. We built the village round the Hist. Kin to us, that tree. Nine bends of river lie to the port.
variants_low: Nets. The village is built round the Hist. Nine bends of river lie to the port.
variants_high: I mend nets on the rack by the landing. We built the village round the Hist, our kin. Nine bends of river to the port. I know each bend by the nets it tore.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-net-menders
words: Step careful at the landing. Jellies drift against the stage poles where I hang nets. A moon adder lies under the bank. Big hunters wait in the water below.
variants_low: Jellies at the landing. A moon adder under the bank. Hunters in the water below.
variants_high: Step careful at the landing. Jellies drift against the stage poles by my nets. A moon adder lies under the bank. Hunters wait in the water below, so pole wide.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-net-menders
words: No road comes in sight of the village. Pole a day downriver to the gang camp. The port lies beyond. The fishers name each bend by the net it tore.
variants_low: No road. Pole a day down to the gang camp. The port is past it.
variants_high: No road comes in sight of the village. Pole a day downriver to the gang camp. The port lies beyond it. The fishers name each bend by the net it tore, so ask them.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-net-menders
words: More of our adults sign onto the roll each year. Some houses have lost every grown hand. The gang bosses send coin back. I mend nets for those who stay.
variants_low: The roll takes more adults each year. Some houses have lost all of theirs.
variants_high: More of our adults sign onto the roll each year. Some houses have lost every grown hand. The gang bosses send coin back for them. Bring me a net, I will mend it for salt.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-net-menders
words: I mend nets for the fishers. The adults go downriver on the roll, more of them each year. Some houses have no grown hand left.
variants_low: Nets. The roll takes more adults each year. Some houses have every one gone.
variants_high: I mend nets for the fishers. I watch each boat leave from my rack. More adults go down on the roll every year. Some houses are left with none.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-reed-cutters
words: Alten Corimont sits on a river in eastern Shadowfen. The water there runs on to the sea. Pirates and smugglers of the Argonians run the place. They back no side in any war. Any ship can tie up at the docks. The lower channel gangs that dredge are hired there.
variants_low: Alten Corimont is the port. Pirates and smugglers run it. They take no side. Gangs get hired there.
variants_high: Alten Corimont sits on a river in eastern Shadowfen. The water there runs on to the sea. Pirates and smugglers of the Argonians run the place. They back no side in any war. Any ship can tie up at the docks. The lower channel gangs that dredge are hired there. Bring salt if you go.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-reed-cutters
words: Gang Ground is where a dredging gang's families live. The camp sits on firm earth, with the Border road on one side and the marsh on the other. It has stood about forty years. The dry top terrace has a hatching shed with the gang's clutch inside.
variants_low: Gang Ground is a camp of dredging families on firm earth by the Border road. Forty years old. The clutch is in a shed.
variants_high: Gang Ground is where a dredging gang's families live. The camp sits on firm earth, with the Border road on one side and the marsh on the other. It has stood about forty years. The dry top terrace has a hatching shed with the gang's clutch inside. Ask for the shed keeper first.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-reed-cutters
words: Nine Bends is where I live. Our tribe built it around a single Hist tree. The ground is a low island. The port, Alten Corimont, lies nine bends of river below us. We still have fresh water. The gangs of the lower channel were hatched beneath that tree. More of our adults sign onto the roll downriver each year.
variants_low: Nine Bends is the tree village, nine bends above the port. The water is fresh. Adults go downriver on the roll.
variants_high: Nine Bends is where I live. Our tribe built it around a single Hist tree. The ground is a low island. The port, Alten Corimont, lies nine bends of river below us. We still have fresh water. The gangs of the lower channel were hatched beneath that tree. More of our adults sign onto the roll downriver each year. Rest at the elder's house.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-reed-cutters
words: The Imperials laid the Prison road and the Border road long ago. The Mile House was their waystation. People still use the old names. Follow the Prison road toward the Rose. Beside that road, on a dry rise, sits the Tag House.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads and a waystation, still called by the old names. The Prison road heads for the Rose. The Tag House sits by it.
variants_high: The Imperials laid the Prison road and the Border road long ago. The Mile House was their waystation. People still use the old names. Follow the Prison road toward the Rose. Beside that road, on a dry rise, sits the Tag House. Stay on the dry ground.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-reed-cutters
words: I cut reed along the bank. Then I tie it in bundles for the carrying. The dyer takes it from me by the armful. Anyone building a house buys from me too.
variants_low: Reed along the bank, tied in bundles. I sell it by the armful to the dyer or a builder.
variants_high: I cut reed along the bank and tie it in bundles for carrying. I sell by the armful to the dyer and to anyone building. A house wants more armfuls than you think.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-reed-cutters
words: We live round one big tree. The water is fresh here, so drink it straight from the bank. Down toward the port it goes salt. I cut my reed on this bank.
variants_low: Fresh water, round a tree. Drink if you are thirsty. I have reed to cut.
variants_high: We live round one big tree on this bank. The water is fresh here. Fill your skin before you go down, because salt starts toward the port.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-reed-cutters
words: Swamp jellies float near the landing stage. A moon adder sleeps against the bank. Big hunters wait in the river below the village. I cut reed on the bank and watch where I put my feet.
variants_low: Jellies at the landing. A moon adder on the bank. Hunters in the river below.
variants_high: Swamp jellies float near the landing stage, so step around them. A moon adder sleeps against the bank. Big hunters wait in the river below the village.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-reed-cutters
words: Not one road reaches us. Pole downriver for a day and the gang camp shows. The port lies past it. I cut reed along the bank and have no reason to go.
variants_low: No road. Pole down a day to the gang camp. The port is past it.
variants_high: Not one road reaches us. Pole downriver for a day and the gang camp shows. The port lies beyond it. Start early and let the current carry you.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-reed-cutters
words: Some houses have every adult downriver on the roll now. More go each year. I sell reed to the dyer, sharpen my knife at the smith and settle with the elder. I deal with whoever is left.
variants_low: Some houses have every adult gone on the roll, more each year. I deal with whoever is left.
variants_high: Some houses have every adult downriver on the roll. More go each year. The kin-house by the common has only children and grandparents. Be gentle with them.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-reed-cutters
words: The roll pays the only coin here. More of our adults go downriver on it every year. I stay and cut reed instead. The dyer pays me by the armful. It's slow coin.
variants_low: Adults go downriver on the roll. More each year. I cut reed.
variants_high: More adults go downriver on the roll each year. I stay and cut reed for the dyer. If you want paid work, the gang camp is a day down the water.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-smith
words: Alten Corimont is the river port in eastern Shadowfen, out where the waterway meets the sea. Argonian smugglers and pirates run it. Their rule is to pick no side when others fight. Any boat can tie up at the docks. The gangs that dredge the lower channel get their hire there.
variants_low: Alten Corimont is a river port in eastern Shadowfen. Pirates and smugglers run it. It picks no side. The dredging gangs are hired there.
variants_high: Alten Corimont is the river port in eastern Shadowfen, out where the waterway meets the sea. Argonian smugglers and pirates run it. Their rule is to pick no side when others fight. Any boat can tie up at the docks. The gangs that dredge the lower channel get their hire there. Our adults go with them.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-smith
words: Gang Ground is where a dredging gang's families live. The camp sits on firm ground, with the Border road on one side and the marsh on the other. It's about forty years old. The hatching shed stands on the top terrace, where the ground is dry. The gang's eggs are inside. The families stay because of them.
variants_low: Gang Ground is a dredging gang's family camp, forty years old, on firm ground by the Border road. The clutch lies in the shed on the top terrace.
variants_high: Gang Ground is where a dredging gang's families live. The camp sits on firm ground, with the Border road on one side and the marsh on the other. It's about forty years old. The hatching shed stands on the top terrace, where the ground is dry. The gang's eggs are inside. The families stay because of them. I've mended a few hooks for them.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-smith
words: It's a low island with a Hist in the middle and the houses round it. Nine bends of river lie between us and the port, Alten Corimont. The water is still fresh, so drink as much as you like. The gang families below were hatched under our tree. Each year, more of our adults are away on the roll.
variants_low: Low island, one Hist, nine bends above Alten Corimont, the port. The water is fresh. More adults leave on the roll each year.
variants_high: It's a low island with a Hist in the middle and the houses round it. Nine bends of river lie between us and the port, Alten Corimont. The water is still fresh, so fill your skin at the landing. The gang families below were hatched under our tree. More of our adults are away on the roll each year.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-smith
words: Beyond the work camp run the old Imperial roads, the Border road and the Prison road. The Mile House is an old waystation. People still use the old names for all three. The Rose is where the Prison road leads. The Tag House sits on a rise of dry ground by that road. I've never walked it.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads and a waystation: the Border road, the Prison road, the Mile House. The Tag House sits on dry ground by the Prison road.
variants_high: Beyond the work camp run the old Imperial roads, the Border road and the Prison road. The Mile House is an old waystation. People still use the old names for all three. The Rose is where the Prison road leads. The Tag House sits on a rise of dry ground by that road. The fishers say the boardwalks are worse than the roads.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-smith
words: I work iron at the forge. Mostly it is mending: hoes, pot handles, whatever the households bring me. The raw metal is bog iron. It is smelted into a bloom, a lump the forge can work. Households give me coin when they have it and goods when they don't.
variants_low: I work iron at the forge and mend tools. The bloom is the raw metal. Coin or goods, I take either.
variants_high: I work iron at the forge. Mostly I mend the household tools of the village. The raw metal is bog iron, smelted into a bloom. Households give me coin or goods. I take trodh as a gift only.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-smith
words: I'm the smith here. The village is built round a Hist. That's a great tree with a mind of its own. Poling up from the port, you pass nine bends of river before it shows. My anvil sits where I can hear the tree hum while I work.
variants_low: The village is built round a Hist, nine bends of river above the port. A Hist is a tree with a mind. I've iron waiting.
variants_high: I'm the smith here. Sit by the anvil and I'll tell you. The village is built round a Hist, a tree with a mind of its own. From the port it's nine bends of river up. I hear the tree's low sound all day at my forge.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-smith
words: Big hunters wait in the river below the village, along the approach. Jellies float thick round the landing stage. A moon adder lies along the bank. The fishers carry my gaff hooks to push jellies off the stage poles.
variants_low: Hunters in the water below us, jellies at the landing, a moon adder on the bank. Watch your feet.
variants_high: Big hunters wait in the river below the village, along the approach. Jellies float thick round the landing stage. A moon adder lies along the bank. Take a gaff hook from my wall for the stage poles. It costs you nothing.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-smith
words: Nothing but the river leads out of here. Pole downriver from the landing for a full day to the gang camp. The port is beyond the camp, farther down the water.
variants_low: No road. Pole downriver a day to the gang camp, then on to the port.
variants_high: Nothing but the river leads out of here. Pole downriver for a full day to reach the gang camp, with the port farther down the water. Fill your skin at the landing first. The water is fresh.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-smith
words: Deeka-Seesh is our elder. When two households fall out over a debt, they bring it to her. She settles it. Fewer of us stay to quarrel now, with more adults gone downriver on the roll each year. Those who stay bring me their iron and their opinions.
variants_low: Debts between households are the elder's business. Adults leave downriver on the roll every year. Ojel are not my business.
variants_high: Deeka-Seesh is our elder. Quarrels and debts between the households are brought to her. Fewer adults stay each year, as more go downriver on the roll. The ones left are decent company at the forge door.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.hh-smith
words: Coin reaches Nine Bends one way, on the roll. That's the list of adults hired out to the gangs downriver, It grows longer every year. The ones at home bring me their hoes and pot handles. I mend them at the anvil by the trade house.
variants_low: Coin comes from the roll. More adults go downriver on it each year. Bring me iron or leave.
variants_high: Coin reaches Nine Bends one way, on the roll. That's the list of adults hired out downriver. More of them sign on each year. I mend the hoes and gaff hooks they leave at home. Have a cup of trodh while you wait.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-2
words: In eastern Shadowfen, on the water, lies the port Alten Corimont. Argonian pirates and smugglers run it. They pick no side. Any crew may tie up. Dredging gangs are hired from those docks.
variants_low: Alten Corimont is a port in eastern Shadowfen on the water. Argonian pirates run it and pick no side. Dredging gangs are hired from its docks.
variants_high: In eastern Shadowfen, on the water, lies the port Alten Corimont. Argonian pirates and smugglers run it. They pick no side, so any crew may tie up. Dredging gangs are hired from those docks. Take a pole.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-2
words: Gang Ground is the camp for a dredging gang's kin. Firm earth holds it, between the marsh and the Border road. Up on the dry top terrace, the gang's clutch lies in a hatching shed.
variants_low: Gang Ground is a camp for a dredging gang's kin. Firm earth, between the marsh and the Border road. The clutch lies in a hatching shed up top.
variants_high: Gang Ground is the camp for a dredging gang's kin. Firm earth holds it, between the marsh and the Border road. Up on the dry top terrace, the gang's clutch lies in a hatching shed. They buy smoked fish from us.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-2
words: Our village sits on a low island round the Hist tree. The port is nine bends down the water. The water here is fresh. More grown ones go on the roll downriver each year.
variants_low: Nine Bends is a village round a tree, nine bends up from the port. The water is fresh. The grown ones go downriver, more each year.
variants_high: Our village sits on a low island round the Hist tree. The port is nine bends down the water. The water here is fresh, so drink it straight from the bank. More grown ones go on the roll downriver each year.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-2
words: Ojel means outsider. It is a plain word, no insult. The slur is lukiul, coined by the An-Xileel for Argonians hatched beyond the marsh. They cannot hear the Hist.
variants_low: Ojel means outsider. It is a plain word, no insult. Lukiul is a slur. Do not say it. Those it names cannot hear the Hist.
variants_high: Ojel means outsider. It is a plain word, no insult, so do not take it ill. The slur is lukiul, coined by the An-Xileel for Argonians hatched beyond the marsh. They cannot hear the Hist. Never say it to an Argonian.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-2
words: The Prison road and the Border road are old Imperial roads, with the Mile House waystation. People still use the old names. The Tag House stands on a dry rise by the Prison road.
variants_low: Old Imperial roads, the Prison road and the Border road. Folk keep the old names. The Tag House stands on a dry rise by the Prison road.
variants_high: The Prison road and the Border road are old Imperial roads, with the Mile House waystation between them. People still use the old names. The Tag House stands on a dry rise by the Prison road. I have only heard of it.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-2
words: We who stayed keep the trade house and the smokehouse going. I turn the fish. Ask me how many come back and I turn another.
variants_low: We who stayed keep the trade house and the smokehouse going. I turn fish. That is my part.
variants_high: We who stayed keep the trade house and the smokehouse going. Reads-The-Weather-Wrong trades the fish I turn at the door. Ask me how many come back and I turn another.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-2
words: Nine Bends is the tribe's village, built round our Hist, a great tree with a mind. The port lies nine bends down the water. I smoke fish at the landing.
variants_low: Nine Bends. The village round our Hist, the tree. The port is nine bends down the river. I have fish to turn.
variants_high: Nine Bends is the tribe's village, built round our Hist. That is a great tree with a mind of its own, older than any of us. The port lies nine bends down the water. Come to the smokehouse by the landing and eat.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-2
words: Jellies sting under the landing stage. A moon adder lies along the bank. I haven't seen river hunters come past my racks. They wait on the approach below.
variants_low: Jellies at the landing, a moon adder on the bank. Hunters on the approach below. Watch your feet.
variants_high: Jellies sting under the landing stage, so step down slowly. A moon adder lies along the bank. I haven't seen river hunters come past my racks. They wait on the approach below. Pole through it. Do not wade.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-2
words: We have no road. Pole downriver a day to reach the gang camp. The port lies on past it.
variants_low: No road. Pole downriver a day to the gang camp. The port is past it.
variants_high: We have no road. Pole downriver a day to reach the gang camp. The port lies on past it. Leave once the lamps are out. Take food from the elder's guest stores.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-2
words: More of our grown ones are away on the roll each year. Some houses have every adult downriver. I watch the landing empty a little more each season.
variants_low: Our grown ones are away on the roll, more each year. Some houses have every adult downriver. Ask the elder, not me.
variants_high: More of our grown ones are away on the roll each year. Some houses have every adult downriver, only children and grandparents left. I watch the landing empty a little more each season. Deeka-Seesh, the elder, hears what the houses owe.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-2
words: I split the catch for the smokehouse and turn each fish by hand. It is good work. Grown ones go downriver to the gang camp, more of them every year.
variants_low: I split fish and I turn them. The grown ones go downriver to the gang camp, more each year. That is all of it.
variants_high: I split the catch for the smokehouse and turn each fish by hand. It is good work. I do it well. More grown ones go downriver to the gang camp each year. Bring a hand to the racks if you want to learn it.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-3
words: Alten Corimont is the river port, in eastern Shadowfen, where the waterway runs out to the sea. Pirates and smugglers of our own people run it. They take no side in a war, so any ship may tie up. The dredging gangs are hired from its docks.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-3
words: Gang Ground is the camp for a dredging gang's families, about forty years old. It stands on firm ground, with the marsh on one side and the Border road on the other. Its top terrace is dry. A hatching shed stands on it with the gang's clutch inside. The families stay for the eggs.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-3
words: Our village is built round the tree, up the river from Alten Corimont, the port. Between us and the port lie nine bends. The water here is fresh. The gang families downriver hatched at these roots. Each year more of our adults are away on the roll.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-3
words: The Prison road and the Border road are old Imperial roads. The Mile House is an old waystation. People still use the old names. The Prison road leads toward the Rose. Beside that road, on a dry rise, stands the Tag House. I have walked none of them.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-3
words: The houses with no grown hands run the trade house and the smokehouse. For the kin-house, I sweep and lay each mat straight, my sister's and my brother's first. Whether they come back, I can't tell you.
variants_low: We run the trade house and the smokehouse. I sweep the kin-house. That is all I say.
variants_high: The houses with no grown hands run the trade house and the smokehouse. I sweep the kin-house and lay each mat straight, my sister's and my brother's first. Come and see it, if you can bear a quiet room.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-3
words: Nine Bends has fresh water, good to drink straight from the bank. I trade at the first house on the way in from the west. At night, I sweep the kin-house, my sister's mat by the wall and my brother's beside it.
variants_low: The water is fresh here. Drink it or do not.
variants_high: The water here is fresh, so drink your fill from the bank. I will show you the trade house, where I trade, if you need cord or fish.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-3
words: Jellies drift in at the landing stage, so I fetch water from the bank above it. The moon adder lies under that bank. Below the village, the river hunters work the deep pools.
variants_low: Jellies at the landing. A moon adder under the bank. Hunters in the deep pools.
variants_high: Jellies drift in at the landing stage, so I fetch water from the bank above it. Step round the moon adder under that bank. Below the village, the river hunters work the deep pools. I would not wade there.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-3
words: The only way to us is by water. From the landing you pole down a day to the gang camp. The port lies beyond the camp. My people went off down the water.
variants_low: Pole down from the landing. The camp is a day off.
variants_high: From our landing you pole down the river a day to the gang camp. The port lies beyond it. Carry water. Those whose mats I sweep went this way.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-3
words: Some houses have every grown hand downriver on the roll. Only children and grandparents sleep there. More go down to the gang camp each year. I sweep round the little ones. I will not talk about who is late home.
variants_low: Houses are empty of grown hands. More go every year. Ask a neighbour about the rest.
variants_high: Some houses have every grown hand downriver on the roll. The children and grandparents sleep there alone. I sweep round them. More go down to the gang camp each year. The houses are very quiet.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2-3
words: I trade cut cane, cord and smoked fish at the trade-house door. The coin comes off the roll. Each year more of our grown ones are away on it. I sweep the mats of those who went and have not come back.
variants_low: I trade cane, cord and fish. More of us go on the roll each year.
variants_high: I trade cane, cord and smoked fish at this door. I will weigh you a fair bundle. More of us go down on the roll every year. The coin is what we get for it.

words: Alten Corimont is a port on the river in eastern Shadowfen. The waterway there runs down to open water. Argonian pirates and smugglers are in charge. They back neither side of any war. Every crew is welcome at the docks. The lower channel's dredging gangs get hired there.

words: Buyers off the boats mention three old names: Prison road, Border road, Mile House. The two roads and the waystation are Imperial work from long ago. People keep the old names. Follow the Prison road toward the Rose and a dry rise carries the Tag House beside it. I have never walked it.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.n2

words: This is Nine Bends, the village round the tree. The river is fresh here. You can drink it without boiling it. I hold the trade-house key and sell cut cane and smoked fish at the door. This morning I called the sky dry. It rained by noon.

speaker: npc.pirate-freeholds.upriver-hist-village.npc-opening-tree-minder
words: Think of the Hist as a huge tree. Its mind is its own. On the naming day, every hatchling drinks the sap. We lay our eggs in a clutch at its roots. words: We call it the Many-Root Conclave. It's an order of stewards for the Hist. They see that a tree gives its consent when it is asked. Minders from the order keep the trees. The Conclave sent me here to tend one tree, read its signs and learn what it wants.

words: The refuge downriver has a clutch to name and hasn't a Hist of its own. Our village has offered to do the naming. Only a Hist can do it, at the hatchery pool cut into this bank. The camp with the clutch lies a day down the water. Ask the elder about the offer.

words: I'm the tree-minder here. A minder tends the village Hist. It's a great tree. The mind in it is its own. At dusk, once the last bowl is filled, I clear the leaves that have fallen round the root. I was sent by the Many-Root Conclave. It's an order of Hist stewards.
